findings.title: place_order returns OANDA orderID as broker_order_id, but get_open_positions returns tradeID — the two never match in the sync loop
findings.impact: Every OANDA trade the system opens fails the ID match in _sync_loop. Within one sync interval the local entry is falsely closed as SYNC_DETECTED (with a P&L lookup against the wrong trade ID → 404 → no P&L), and the real broker position is re-imported as a duplicate 'broker_sync' entry with agent_id/reasoning/market_context lost. Trade attribution and P&L records are silently corrupted — exactly 'random-seeming losses after weeks'.
findings.fix: Return the trade ID for filled orders: `fill.get("tradeOpened", {}).get("tradeID")` (fall back to fill.get("id")); for unfilled pending orders keep the order ID but sync must then also check pending orders, or resolve order→trade on fill.

findings.title: sync_key sent as order clientExtensions instead of tradeClientExtensions — the comment never lands on the Trade, so sync_key matching is dead on OANDA
findings.impact: Position.sync_key is always None for OANDA, so the sync-key fallback match in base._sync_loop (line 706-707) and management/api.py:1026-1043 never works. Combined with the orderID/tradeID mismatch there is NO working match path — every OANDA trade is duplicated and falsely closed by sync.
findings.fix: Send `order_body["tradeClientExtensions"] = {"comment": order.sync_key, "tag": "OpenForexAI"}` (optionally in addition to clientExtensions). Then the dual read at 413-416 can be reduced to `t["clientExtensions"]["comment"]`.

findings.title: Non-idempotent order placement (and partial close) wrapped in blind retry_async — network timeout after broker accepted the request produces duplicate orders / double partial closes
findings.impact: A timeout on a filled market order silently opens a second identical position (doubled exposure). A timeout on a partial close of 5000/10000 units closes another 5000 on retry — position flat when the strategy wanted to keep half. Rare, network-dependent, surfaces only as unexplained losses. Note MT5Broker deliberately does NOT retry order_send — the adapters diverge on retry semantics.
findings.fix: Do not retry mutating requests on transport errors, or make them idempotent (OANDA supports a client order ID via clientExtensions — check for its existence before resubmitting). Restrict retry_async to idempotent GETs. Bonus: retry_async never retries HTTP 5xx anyway because raise_for_status is called after it, so the current retry only fires in exactly the dangerous case.

findings.title: Invalid JSON5 during routing reload silently replaces the working routing table with an EMPTY table
findings.impact: A single typo in event_routing.json5 followed by a reload (POST /routing/reload or ROUTING_RELOAD_REQUESTED event) wipes ALL routing: candle triggers stop reaching AA agents, signal_generated stops reaching BA supervisors — every routed event is dropped, and the drop is logged only at DEBUG (bus.py:405). The system appears alive (direct-target request/response still works) while trading logic silently stops firing.
findings.fix: In _parse_rules, re-raise on ValueError/FileNotFoundError instead of returning []. reload() then propagates, bus.reload_routing keeps the previous rules and emits ROUTING_RELOAD_FAILED — turning a silent outage into a visible, non-destructive error.

findings.title: Synchronous SQLite reads (read_events/read_event/read_trace) are called directly from async FastAPI routes, blocking the trading event loop
findings.impact: The management API runs in the same asyncio loop as the trading system (same process: bus dispatch, agents, broker adapters). On an event_log.db that has grown for weeks (see unbounded-growth finding), opening the event browser or a trace in the UI freezes the entire event loop for seconds to minutes: candles are not dispatched, agent decisions and order/fill handling stall, broker heartbeats time out. This produces exactly the rare, random-seeming trading losses described — losses correlate with someone looking at the monitoring UI during live trading.
findings.fix: Wrap the read calls in `await asyncio.to_thread(read_events, ...)` (same for read_event/read_trace) in api.py, or make the event_log read functions async via run_in_executor like persist_event already does. For read_trace, replace the per-level LIKE scan with an indexed lookup (e.g. store parent_id/root_id columns and index them).

findings.title: NameError on undefined `cycle_pair` in _publish_m5_trigger_counter is swallowed by except-pass, so the M5_TRIGGER_COUNTER monitoring event is never emitted
findings.impact: The m5_trigger_counter monitoring event (count/every/due/paused/session/run) is NEVER published for any agent, on every single M5 candle, with zero error trace. Operators watching the divider counter to verify agents are firing see nothing and cannot detect missed analysis cycles — exactly the class of silent, weeks-later-visible failure.
findings.fix: Add the pair to the method signature (or read it from the tool context): `pair=self._tool_dispatcher._context.pair if self._tool_dispatcher else None` and use that instead of `cycle_pair`. Add a regression test that asserts the event is emitted.

findings.title: Manual execute endpoint runs BA/GA cycle despite snapshot validation_errors, while AA path and live loop fail closed
findings.impact: An operator-triggered broker-agent execute with a failing tool/transform block sends the invalid snapshot to the LLM and can place real orders on broken market context — the invalid-snapshot event is emitted but the trade happens anyway.
findings.fix: Mirror the AA gate: skip `_run_with_tools` (or return the validation errors) when validation_errors is non-empty in the BA and generic execute branches.

findings.title: EC loops have no per-cycle exception guard — any exception escaping _run_cycle kills the whole EC permanently and silently
findings.impact: One transient failure (e.g. an operator adds a required field to the ec_output/ec_cycle_* schema in config/event_schemas.json5, or any unforeseen error in the non-try region) permanently silences a guard/relay EC. Every subsequent signal flows unguarded (or is never relayed) with no monitoring event per skipped run — the classic weeks-later financial-loss failure.
findings.fix: Wrap the `await self._run_cycle(...)` calls in both loops in try/except Exception that logs, emits SYSTEM_ERROR/EC_RUN_FAILED, and continues — mirroring agents/agent.py. Additionally move the EC_OUTPUT/EC_CYCLE_* publishes inside a try so a schema-validation failure marks the run failed instead of killing the EC.

findings.title: Invalid stdlib logging kwargs in _account_poll_loop except-block raise TypeError and permanently kill the account polling task on the first poll error
findings.impact: The first transient account-status error (weekend outage, 503, network blip — guaranteed within weeks of live trading) silently kills account polling. ACCOUNT_STATUS_UPDATED events stop; balance/equity/margin data go stale until a restart or a hot-reload happens to re-run start_background_tasks. Risk sizing based on stale equity → mis-sized positions.
findings.fix: Use printf-style: `_log.warning("Account poll error broker=%s: %s", self.short_name, exc)` (matches every other log call in the file).

findings.title: MT5 place_order marks pending (LIMIT/STOP/STOP_LIMIT) orders as OPEN — sync loop then falsely closes them
findings.impact: A resting limit order is stored locally as an OPEN position with broker_order_id=order ticket. positions_get() never returns pending orders, so the next _sync_loop pass (60s) sees 'broker_order_id not in broker_ids' and closes the entry as SYNC_DETECTED. When the order actually fills later, the position is re-imported as an anonymous broker_sync entry — attribution and any local SL/TP bookkeeping lost.
findings.fix: Return TradeStatus.PENDING when action == TRADE_ACTION_PENDING and retcode == DONE (result.deal == 0); only MARKET fills are OPEN.

findings.title: history_deals_get date window uses UTC now while MT5 deal times are broker-local-as-epoch — deals closed in the last ~3 hours are excluded
findings.impact: get_closed_trade_result's fallback and find_closed_trade_by_sync_key return None precisely for freshly closed trades — the only trades the sync/orphan logic ever looks up (orphan check fires 120s after request). Orphaned filled+closed entries get marked REJECTED (base.py:1236-1244) and their P&L never recorded; sync-detected closes lose pnl/close_price.
findings.fix: Query with broker-labelled bounds: date_to = datetime.now(UTC) + broker_offset (+ safety margin), i.e. `datetime.now(self._broker_tz).replace(tzinfo=UTC)`; centralize the inverse of _broker_timestamp for query parameters.

findings.title: Candle.spread stored in three different units: OANDA writes raw price delta, MT5 writes broker points, the model documents pips
findings.impact: Everything downstream is unit-broken depending on broker: analysis_snapshot._compact_candle rounds spread to 2 decimals (analysis_snapshot.py:183) so OANDA spreads render as 0.0 to the LLM, while MT5 spreads look 10x too large; any spread-based cost/entry-quality reasoning is systematically wrong on one broker or the other.
findings.fix: Normalize at the adapter boundary: convert both to pips using a pip-size table (see data/normalizer.py) before constructing Candle; document and enforce the unit in normalize_candle.

findings.title: PG agent_decisions DDL lacks decision_type_new/reasoning/market_snapshot columns that save_agent_decision inserts into — every decision write/read fails on a fresh PostgreSQL database
findings.impact: On any fresh PostgreSQL deployment, every save_agent_decision raises asyncpg.UndefinedColumnError and every get_analysis_records/get_analysis_record call fails. Agent decision audit trail is silently or loudly lost depending on caller exception handling — decisions that drove trades become unreconstructable.
findings.fix: Add decision_type_new TEXT, reasoning TEXT, market_snapshot TEXT (and confidence DOUBLE PRECISION per migration 003) to the PG DDL, or better: implement a real migration runner for PostgreSQL mirroring SQLiteRepository._run_migrations.

findings.title: Incomplete (still-forming) last bucket of resampled M15/M30/H1/H4/D1 candles is returned as if complete and feeds indicators
findings.impact: At e.g. 10:05 UTC an H4 request returns an '08:00' H4 bar built from only 25 of 48 M5 bars: its high/low/close/tick_volume are partial-period values. ATR/RSI/BB/SMA computed by CalculateIndicatorTool (tools/market/calculate_indicator.py:78-95) and by order_execution.py (which imports `atr` for stop sizing) treat this bar as complete. ATR is systematically understated right after a bucket boundary and drifts within the bucket → stops/targets sized too tight, RSI/BB signals flap intra-bucket. Values never match broker charts and the error size depends on where in the bucket 'now' falls — exactly the random-looking, weeks-to-notice loss pattern reported.
findings.fix: In `resample_candles` (or in the container after resampling), drop the trailing bucket when `bucket_start + target_mins > newest_source_ts + source_mins` is not satisfied (i.e. keep a bucket only if its full period is covered / its last expected source slot is present), optionally behind an `include_partial: bool` flag for callers that want the live bar. Also fetch broker history with start_pos=1 or discard the forming M5 bar before persisting.

findings.title: synthetic_dxy aligns component candle series by head index, not by timestamp/tail — unequal series lengths silently produce mixed-timestamp DXY values
findings.impact: If EURUSD returns 160 candles and USDJPY 150 (null-candle drops / gaps are normal in live operation), DXY[-1] multiplies USDJPY's latest close with EURUSD's close from 10 candles ago. calculate_indicator's DXY tool then hands the agent a stale/mixed 'current' dollar index with no error — exactly the class of rare, random-seeming wrong-decision input that only shows up as losses weeks later. Even equal lengths misalign mid-series when nulls were dropped at different positions per pair.
findings.fix: Align components by timestamp: build a dict {timestamp: close} per pair, iterate over the intersection of timestamps (or align from the tail: series[len(series)-n+i]), and return values keyed/paired with their timestamps.

findings.title: All PostgreSQL agent-memory methods target tables/columns that the PostgreSQL schema setup never creates
findings.impact: With system.json5 database.backend=postgresql, the first call to any agent-memory method raises asyncpg UndefinedColumnError/UndefinedTableError — agent decisions, conversations and performance snapshots are never persisted, so agents cannot resume with memory after restart. Currently latent because these methods have no production callers (see dead-code finding), but the docstring invites wiring them up as-is.
findings.fix: Either add the agent-memory DDL (agent_conversations, agent_performance, the three agent_decisions columns) to _ensure_core_tables / a PG migration runner, or delete the PG agent-memory methods and the false docstring claim until PG support is real.

findings.title: OpenAI adapter (and Ollama/LMStudio) sends canonical Anthropic-style tool messages unconverted to the OpenAI chat API — multi-turn tool loops are broken
findings.impact: Any agent configured with the openai, ollama, or lmstudio module fails with a 400 API error on every tool-use turn >= 2 (i.e. as soon as the LLM actually calls a tool). The agent's LLM cycle raises, the trading decision for that trigger is silently lost. Works fine in demos that never reach turn 2, then breaks in live use.
findings.fix: Move `_sanitize_messages`/`_convert_message` from azure.py into openai.py (Azure inherits or shares it) and apply it in OpenAILLMProvider.complete_with_tools before the API call.

findings.title: Azure silently degrades a tool conversation to a text-only completion (no tools, output capped at 1024 tokens, stop_reason forged to end_turn)
findings.impact: When Azure intermittently returns invalid_prompt, the agent receives what looks like a normal, final answer (`wants_tools` False, stop_reason end_turn) — a trading decision produced WITHOUT access to market-data tools, and possibly truncated at 1024 tokens with the truncation hidden by the forged "end_turn". This is exactly the rare, random-seeming, non-crashing defect class the owner reports, and it violates the project's fail-closed rule (guards must block, never silently pass).
findings.fix: Remove the without-tools fallback entirely; let the RuntimeError propagate so LLMService returns an error payload and the agent aborts the cycle. At minimum, mark the response distinctly (e.g. stop_reason="error" or a degraded flag) instead of "end_turn".

findings.title: Output truncation is invisible: OpenAI/Azure pass finish_reason 'length' through unmapped, Anthropic returns 'max_tokens', llm_service hardcodes 'end_turn' for complete() — and no consumer checks any of them
findings.impact: When a response hits max_tokens, the truncated text is treated as the complete final decision. A cut-off JSON decision or half-written instruction flows into trade logic looking normal. Cross-provider the same truncation surfaces as three different stop_reason strings ('length', 'max_tokens', 'end_turn'), so even future checks would be provider-dependent.
findings.fix: Map finish_reason "length" -> "max_tokens" in openai.py and azure.py _parse paths; add stop/finish reason to LLMResponse and propagate it through llm_service instead of hardcoding "end_turn"; make the agent treat stop_reason=="max_tokens" as a hard error (fail closed).

findings.title: All 'ALL___' pair fallbacks target an unregistered adapter member — every such call times out (affects supervisor/ALL-pair agents)
findings.impact: Any agent whose context has no pair (e.g. broker-wide supervisor agents like 'OANDA-ALL___-BA-SUP1', see agent.py:1503 which nulls the pair for ALL___) gets a silent message drop plus a 20s timeout on get_account_status / get_open_positions / modify_order / close_position — tools appear randomly broken and slow, and risk-management actions are skipped.
findings.fix: Resolve the target to a real registered adapter member of the broker (query bus.registered_agents() by prefix, or have adapters also register the ALL___ alias). Remove the misleading 'ALL___' fallback from all five tools once fixed centrally.

findings.title: is_market_open() can never return False — every UTC hour belongs to a session and weekends are not checked — the order-blocking guard in order_execution is dead
findings.impact: Orders are never blocked for the Fri 22:00 UTC – Sun 22:00 UTC weekend close or holidays by this guard. The only remaining protection is the 20-minute M5 staleness check — which itself is skipped when the timestamp is missing or unparsable (see separate finding). Pending/limit orders placed into a closed market execute at Sunday-open gap prices — a classic rare weekend-gap loss.
findings.fix: Add weekday logic: market open from Sunday ~21/22:00 UTC to Friday ~21/22:00 UTC (`dt.weekday()` checks), and make `detect_session` return "closed" outside that window.

findings.title: trigger_sync ignores the adapter's 'error' field and reports a failed sync as successful with 0 discrepancies
findings.impact: The tool exists for the agent to detect positions closed externally / stale order book. On a broker outage the LLM is told 'sync succeeded, no discrepancies' and continues trading against a stale internal order book — e.g. hedging or re-entering against a position that no longer exists. Silent, rare, loss-producing: exactly the reported defect class.
findings.fix: Check `if response.get("error"): return {"sync_triggered": False, "error": response["error"]}` (or raise) before reading discrepancies.

findings.title: Synchronous urllib GitHub call (6 s timeout) executed on the event loop inside async get_console_initial — stalls the entire trading process
findings.impact: Every time a user opens the web console (or GitHub is slow/unreachable), the whole event loop freezes for up to ~6 seconds: M5 candle triggers, order placement, SL/TP management and broker sync all stall. Produces sporadic late fills / missed triggers correlated with nothing visible — classic random-seeming live-trading degradation.
findings.fix: Run it off-loop: `remote = await asyncio.to_thread(_fetch_remote_release_info)` (or use an async HTTP client), and/or cache the result for several minutes.

findings.title: Imported event-routing rules are never remapped with agent_id_map/agent_id_prefix, so routing points at the old (possibly foreign, possibly locally-existing) agent IDs
findings.impact: The whole point of agent_id_prefix/agent_id_map is renaming on import (e.g. to avoid collisions). After such an import the new agents (e.g. "X_OANDA-EURUSD-AA-TRD1") exist but every imported rule still says from/to "OANDA-EURUSD-AA-TRD1". Two failure modes in live trading: (a) the imported strategy's agents silently receive no events and never trade / never receive stop-loss-relevant events; (b) worse, if an agent with the ORIGINAL ID already exists locally (the very reason a prefix was used), the imported rules route the imported strategy's events INTO the pre-existing live agent — cross-wired signals producing random-seeming trades and losses weeks later.
findings.fix: In apply_import_package, before merging each rule, rewrite rule["from"] and rule["to"]: if the value (or the concrete IDs a template/pattern refers to) equals a source agent id present in package["agents"], replace it with _map_agent_id(source_id, mapping). At minimum handle exact-ID from/to values; for wildcard/template targets emit a validation error when a non-empty mapping is supplied. Mirror the same check in validate_package so a mapping + routing import is rejected until remapping is implemented.

findings.title: detect_session() covers all 24 UTC hours and ignores the weekday, so 'closed' is unreachable and is_market_open() always returns True
findings.impact: The trading-window guard in openforexai/tools/trading/order_execution.py:208 (`if not is_market_open(): raise RuntimeError(...)`) is a no-op — it can never block. On Saturday/Sunday agents receive MarketSnapshot.session='sydney'/'tokyo' etc. (data/container.py:650), so LLM prompts are built with a wrong active-session label, and weekend order attempts are only stopped by the secondary 20-minute candle-staleness check — which is skipped entirely when context.broker_name or context.pair is unset (order_execution.py:211-212) or when the timestamp fails to parse (bare except at 230-231). Rare weekend/holiday orders and session-biased mis-decisions are exactly the random-seeming loss pattern reported.
findings.fix: Add a weekday check: if dt.weekday() == 5 (Saturday) or (weekday == 4 and hour >= 21) or (weekday == 6 and hour < 21): return "closed". Also normalize dt to UTC first (dt = dt.astimezone(UTC) if dt.tzinfo else dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC)).

findings.title: units: int cannot represent MT5 lot granularity — MT5 adapter silently rounds requested units to 0.01-lot steps and float-truncates read-back units, so local order book and broker disagree on position size
findings.impact: Persistent silent mismatch between recorded and actual position size: risk-based sizing is off by up to ~8% (e.g. 12,347 vs 12,000), P&L attribution drifts, and a full close using order-book units can exceed broker units by 1 (float truncation) triggering `ValueError("units to close exceed current position size")` (mt5.py:424-425) — a rare, position-stuck failure. `close_units == current_units` (mt5.py:459) can also misclassify a full close as partial (status stays OPEN).
findings.fix: Quantize units to the broker's lot step at sizing time (round down to a multiple of 1000 for MT5, reject < min lot), store the broker-confirmed size back into OrderBookEntry.units after fill, and replace int(p.volume*100_000) with int(round(p.volume*100_000)).

findings.title: Synchronous requests.get (30s timeout, one per event) executed inside async tool path — freezes the entire asyncio event loop
findings.impact: When an agent invokes get_news, the whole asyncio event loop blocks for (network latency x number of matching events), worst case 30s PER event on a slow/hanging mql5.com response. During that time no ticks are processed, no EventBus messages dispatched, no order fills handled, no EC guard timers fire — the trading system is frozen for up to minutes at exactly the moments it queries news (i.e., around high-impact releases when the market moves fastest). This produces rare, random-seeming stale-price/late-order losses that never appear as a crash.
findings.fix: Fetch pages with an async HTTP client (aiohttp/httpx.AsyncClient) or wrap the whole create_events_markdown call in `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` from GetNewsTool.execute; also move write_text/read_text off the loop.

findings.title: Candle.spread is stored in three different units (OANDA: raw price delta, MT5: integer points, model doc: pips) and container derives ask = close + spread
findings.impact: For MT5 brokers, MarketSnapshot.current_tick.ask = bid + 12 (e.g. bid 1.0850 → ask 13.0850): any consumer using the ask (spread-aware entry logic, chart annotation, LLM snapshot) is wildly wrong. For OANDA, the spread shown to the LLM ("latest_spread") rounds 0.00012 to 0.0 — the model always sees zero spread and never accounts for transaction cost. Both are slow-bleed, non-crashing money defects.
findings.fix: Pick one canonical unit (pips per the model doc): OANDA: `(ask_close - bid_close) / pip_size(pair)`; MT5: `r["spread"] * point / pip_size` (points→pips, usually /10). Fix container.py:633 to `ask = close + spread * pip_size(pair)` using data/normalizer.pip_size.

findings.title: Save-time placeholder resolution permanently bakes resolved values into forced_arguments, destroying runtime templates
findings.impact: After one wizard save, forced_arguments contain e.g. pair: "EURUSD" instead of "{pair}". If the agent's pair (or broker/llm) is later changed, the forced tool arguments silently keep the OLD baked value — tools (get_candles, place_order via forced pair, etc.) operate on the wrong instrument. Trades/analyses run against the wrong pair without any error: exactly the rare, random-seeming financial-loss class.
findings.fix: Do not resolve placeholders during serialization. Pass `replacements` only in validateForm (to check the template resolves to a valid typed value) and call coerceForcedValue WITHOUT replacements in serializeForcedArguments, persisting the raw template string. Skip numeric/boolean coercion for values still containing `{...}` placeholders.

findings.title: Stored XSS: FTS snippet (raw, unescaped document content) rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.impact: A KB document containing e.g. executes arbitrary JS in the management UI whenever a search hit shows that snippet. The management UI can rewrite trading config (agents, routing, broker modules) via its REST API — script execution here is a direct path to manipulated live-trading behavior.
findings.fix: HTML-escape title/content before FTS insert or escape the snippet server-side except for the <mark> markers (e.g. escape then re-insert markers via unique sentinels); alternatively render the snippet as text and highlight matches client-side. Do not feed snippet into dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

findings.title: MockRepository no longer satisfies AbstractRepository (missing save_ec_run) — all 14 order-lifecycle tests ERROR at fixture setup, leaving order placement/close/modify/sync with zero effective coverage
findings.impact: Every test guarding place_order, close_position (full/partial/all), modify_order, rejected-order finalization, order-book sync matching, auto risk sizing, and DataContainer candle repair is dead. Regressions on these money paths (exactly the class of rare live-trading loss the owner reports) ship completely unguarded while CI appears to 'have tests'.
findings.fix: Add `async def save_ec_run(self, run) -> str: self.ec_runs.append(run); return str(run.id)` to MockRepository (plus an `ec_runs` list), then fix the downstream failures this unmasks (see other findings).

findings.title: Order-lifecycle tests target a removed architecture: ToolContext no longer accepts broker=/repository=/data_container= kwargs — tools now work exclusively via bus_request, so even after fixing MockRepository these tests raise TypeError
findings.impact: The entire order-lifecycle unit-test layer asserts an architecture that no longer exists. There is no test harness at all for the actual bus-request order path (ORDER_REQUEST → broker adapter → ORDER_RESPONSE → order-book update), so payload-shape mismatches between tool and adapter — the #1 suspected live-loss defect class — are untestable and untested.
findings.fix: Rewrite these tests around the bus architecture: spin up an EventBus, register a stub broker adapter member and RepositoryService responder, and drive the tools through bus_request end-to-end. Delete the direct-injection MockBroker/ToolContext(broker=...) pattern from conftest.

findings.title: trigger_sync tests call a method that does not exist on MockBroker and use a removed argument order (pair, repository, event_bus) — sync matching/import logic has never been re-verified against the current implementation
findings.impact: Sync-key matching, unmatched-position import, and orphaned-PENDING resolution (the mechanism that reconciles local order book with broker truth after SL/TP hits — direct P&L attribution) are untested. A regression here silently corrupts the order book weeks into live trading.
findings.fix: Rewrite the tests against BrokerBase.trigger_sync with a bus-based stub repository responder (`_repo_request` goes over the EventBus), using the correct (pair, event_bus) signature.

findings.title: Backfilled closed_at is labeled UTC (+00:00) while the system convention stores MT5 timestamps as broker_tz (+03:00) — reintroduces the exact mislabeling migrate_broker_timezone.py exists to fix
findings.impact: For the same broker deal, a backfilled closed_at differs by 3 hours (as an instant) from adapter-written closed_at rows. Trade-duration, session attribution and time-bucketed P&L analytics on backfilled rows are off by 3h; running the script after migrate_broker_timezone.py silently re-pollutes the DB with mixed timezone labels — precisely the rare, weeks-later, random-looking data corruption class.
findings.fix: Read broker_utc_offset_hours from the MT5 module config and replicate the adapter's _broker_timestamp: datetime.fromtimestamp(int(deal_time), tz=UTC).replace(tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=offset))). Better: reuse the adapter's get_closed_trade_result instead of a diverged copy.

findings.title: Updater silently overwrites user-edited runtime config files (prompt/snippet libraries, llm_tool_config, event_schemas, snapshot_helpers) because _is_preserved only whitelists system.json5, modules/, RunTime/, data/, logs/, .venv/
findings.impact: Owner tunes agent prompts / decision snippets / snapshot helpers over weeks (CLAUDE.md documents these as hot-editable config areas). One click on 'Update' in the UI (which runs this script via api.py _run_update_job) silently resets every prompt and snippet library to the release defaults. Agents keep trading with the reverted prompts — a subtle behavior change that surfaces only as degraded/erratic trading decisions, exactly the 'random-seeming losses weeks later' failure class.
findings.fix: Extend _is_preserved to preserve config/prompt_library*.json5, config/snippet_library*.json5, config/llm_tool_config.json5, config/event_schemas.json5, config/openai.json5 and config/snapshot_helpers.py — or invert the policy: only ever replace config/config.default.json5 inside config/ and preserve everything else under config/.

findings.title: Tests 5 and 6 reference EventType.M5_CANDLE_AVAILABLE, which does not exist (enum has M5_CANDLE_UPDATE / M5_CANDLE_TRIGGER), and expect payload key 'pair' that the producer never sets
findings.impact: Test 6 ('live M5 streaming') never prints a single candle and reports 'Total candles received: 0'; each publish raises AttributeError into the broker's candle loop. The tool is unusable for diagnosing the exact data-feed problems it was written for.
findings.fix: Replace M5_CANDLE_AVAILABLE with EventType.M5_CANDLE_UPDATE (or M5_CANDLE_TRIGGER), and read the pair from msg.instrument / payload['broker_name'] instead of payload['pair'].

findings.title: PostgreSQL backend inserts into agent_decisions columns (decision_type_new, reasoning, market_snapshot) that are never created — no migration path exists for Postgres
findings.impact: On the PostgreSQL backend every save_agent_decision raises asyncpg UndefinedColumnError; every agent decision/analysis record is lost (or, if callers swallow the exception, silently lost) from the moment the backend is switched to Postgres. Decision audit trail and analysis UI are empty.
findings.fix: Either add the four columns to the CREATE TABLE in _ensure_core_tables and create agent_conversations/agent_performance/ec_runs/assessment_memory there too, or implement a real Postgres migration runner with dialect-compatible SQL. Better: drop decision_type_new entirely (see compat-shim finding) and unify schema management in one place per dialect.

findings.title: Preview disables all URL sanitization (urlTransform identity) and enables raw HTML (rehypeRaw) — stored XSS / javascript: links
findings.impact: Any imported or shared KB document (kbImport writes arbitrary content) becomes an XSS vector the moment it is opened — preview is the default mode. Same blast radius as the SearchPanel XSS: full management-API access from injected script.
findings.fix: Remove the urlTransform override (restore defaultUrlTransform) and either drop rehypeRaw or add rehype-sanitize after it with a schema allowing only benign tags/attributes.

findings.title: Deprecated '@handlers' target still half-supported — a matching @handlers rule counts as 'matched' and silently swallows the event
findings.impact: A leftover '@handlers' rule in event_routing.json5 makes matching events vanish without even the unmatched-event monitoring signal — an invisible black hole for e.g. signal or order events.
findings.fix: Owner wants all compat shims removed: delete the '@handlers' special-case in resolve() (routing.py:203-208) and resolve_targets (routing.py:109-110), reject '@handlers' rules at parse time in _rules_from_dict (skip + error log, so they cannot set matched_any), and fix the docstring (routing.py:37-40).

findings.title: Rule matched but zero targets resolved → message dropped with only a DEBUG log, no warning-level signal
findings.impact: If the target AA/BA agent of a matched rule is disabled or crashed, every signal/trigger for it evaporates silently. E.g. signal_approved routed to '{sender.broker}-ALL___-BA-*' with no BA running: signals are lost for weeks with nothing above DEBUG level.
findings.fix: In _dispatch, treat `matched and not target_ids` as a distinct condition: log at WARNING and emit a dedicated monitoring event (e.g. MATCHED_NO_TARGET). Raise _warn_unmatched's log level to warning to match the documented contract.

findings.title: Direct-target QueueFull drop does not emit AGENT_QUEUE_FULL monitoring event; routed-path drop does
findings.impact: A backed-up broker-adapter queue dropping an order_request or position_close_request produces no monitoring event — dashboards show nothing while orders are lost; the caller only sees a generic timeout.
findings.fix: Emit the same AGENT_QUEUE_FULL monitoring event in the direct-target QueueFull handler (bus.py:320-324).

findings.title: Direct-targeted message to an unregistered member is dropped at DEBUG level with no monitoring event
findings.impact: During adapter restart / runtime agent swap, an order_request or position_close_request targeted at a briefly-unregistered member silently vanishes; the tool times out with no root-cause trace. Rare, timing-dependent, exactly the reported defect class.
findings.fix: Log at WARNING and emit a dedicated monitoring event (e.g. DIRECT_TARGET_UNREGISTERED with target, event, sender, message_id).

findings.title: Schema-load failure silently disables ALL payload validation (fail-open), and the schema path is CWD-relative
findings.impact: Start the process from a different working directory (or introduce a typo into event_schemas.json5) and every payload-shape check disappears system-wide with a single startup log line. Producer/consumer field mismatches — the owner's #1 defect class — then propagate unchecked. Contradicts the owner's documented fail-closed policy (EC guard memory).
findings.fix: Anchor _SCHEMA_PATH to the project root (same mechanism as _project_root() in management/api.py) or inject it via the constructor; on load failure either raise at startup or emit a persistent monitoring alarm instead of degrading silently.

findings.title: Request/response-future boilerplate (create future, register by str(msg.id), publish, wait_for, cancel) duplicated in 7+ call sites with divergent cancellation semantics
findings.impact: Any fix to the request/response protocol (timeout handling, cleanup, late-response accounting) must be applied in 7 places; the shield/no-shield divergence already means late responses are sometimes swallowed as cancelled and sometimes resolve a future nobody awaits.
findings.fix: Extract one helper (e.g. `await bus.request(msg, timeout=...)`) on EventBus that owns future creation, registration, shielding policy, wait and guaranteed cancel_response_future in finally; migrate all call sites.

findings.title: Event log grows without bound — no rotation, pruning, or archiving exists anywhere
findings.impact: After weeks of live trading data/event_log.db reaches gigabytes: every insert must maintain 5 indexes on a huge table, per-write latency climbs, the default thread-pool executor threads pile up on slow writes and SQLITE_BUSY contention (each write opens its own connection, no WAL), and disk eventually fills. Failures are only `_log.error`-ed (line 111) and events silently stop being recorded — plus the blocking-read finding gets progressively worse. Slow, invisible degradation over weeks matching the reported failure mode.
findings.fix: Implement rotation: a periodic task that deletes (or moves to an archive DB) events older than N days / beyond N rows, plus `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` and periodic `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum`. Either use archived_at as designed or drop the column.

findings.title: created_at is stored in a mutable UI display offset (ui_utc), breaking lexicographic time filtering and ordering across offset changes
findings.impact: Any change of ui_utc (config edit, DST-motivated adjustment) or events written before configure() runs at startup (offset 0) versus after (offset N) yields a DB with mixed offsets: from_time/to_time filters silently include/exclude the wrong events and newest-first ordering interleaves wrongly. When the owner forensically reconstructs why a losing trade happened, the event timeline is wrong — masking the true cause.
findings.fix: Always store created_at in UTC (`message.created_at.astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat()`), delete the _utc_offset/configure() mechanism entirely, and convert to the UI timezone only at display time in the frontend/API layer.

findings.title: New SQLite connection plus full DDL executescript plus two PRAGMA table_info migration probes run on EVERY event write and read
findings.impact: Per-event fixed overhead of connect + 8 schema statements on the hottest persistence path; under bursts (every candle, every tool call, every LLM event) the default executor threads serialize on the DB lock, writes time out with 'database is locked', get logged and dropped — sporadic holes in the event log that only show up when the log is needed for loss forensics.
findings.fix: Create one long-lived connection (or a small pool) guarded by a threading.Lock, run DDL/migrations exactly once at startup, and set `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000`.

findings.title: Auto-pinned error events accumulate in _protected without any bound or automatic eviction — memory leak in a weeks-long process
findings.impact: A flaky broker connection or an LLM outage over a weekend emits thousands of error events, each pinned forever with its full payload. Over weeks of live trading the process's memory grows monotonically; GC pressure and eventual OOM/pagefile thrashing degrade event-loop latency (delayed order handling) long before an outright crash — a slow, random-seeming degradation.
findings.fix: Cap the protected buffer (e.g. an OrderedDict with maxlen ~500, evicting oldest auto-pinned entries first while keeping manual pins), or auto-unpin events older than N hours.

findings.title: Timer session filter is dead: `self._is_session_allowed(None)` always returns True, so the skip branch is unreachable and timer cycles run outside configured sessions
findings.impact: Any agent with timer.enabled=true plus a session_filter (e.g. new_york/london windows in system.json5) will analyse — and via a BA chain potentially trade — around the clock, including illiquid Asian-session hours the operator explicitly filtered out. The AGENT_TRIGGER_SKIPPED/'session_filter' path for timers can never fire.
findings.fix: Pass the current time instead of None, e.g. `self._is_session_allowed(datetime.now(UTC))` (the method already normalises aware datetimes to broker tz), or remove the dead branch if timers are intentionally unfiltered.

findings.title: _resolve_analysis_timestamp raises RuntimeError for every non-m5_candle_trigger AA cycle — AA cycles triggered by prompt_updated/timer/analysis_result always crash after the LLM call
findings.impact: Every PROMPT_UPDATED event (and any AA timer or chained analysis_result trigger) runs a full paid LLM cycle (with pass_trigger=false the user message is even empty), then raises at line 1001 BEFORE `_persist_analysis_result` and before the ANALYSIS_RESULT publish. The cycle is marked failed, the analysis is silently lost, tokens are burned. Downstream BAs never see these analyses.
findings.fix: Make `_resolve_analysis_timestamp` fall back (e.g. `datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()`) for non-candle triggers, or gate the whole publish/persist block on `trigger == M5_CANDLE_TRIGGER` — and stop running full LLM cycles for prompt_updated if that trigger is only meant as a config-refresh signal.

findings.title: Session-filter candle extraction only checks payload["candle"], but analysis_result payloads carry the candle under trigger_payload — session filter fails open for downstream (BA) agents
findings.impact: A BA configured with a session_filter and analysis_result/ec_output triggers is never actually session-filtered: candle_ts is always None → filter fails open → trades execute outside allowed session windows. Currently no BA in system.json5 has a session_filter, so this is latent, but the moment one is added it silently does nothing.
findings.fix: Also probe payload["trigger_payload"]["candle"]["timestamp"] and top-level payload["timestamp"] when extracting candle_ts; consider failing closed (skip) when a session_filter is configured but no timestamp can be resolved, per the EC-guard fail-closed policy.

findings.title: Runtime config refresh (_apply_config) swaps _tool_dispatcher/_system_prompt/context without taking _run_lock, mutating state under a cycle that is mid-flight
findings.impact: A config save during an in-flight timer/API cycle: the cycle started with old context (pair set to the resolved cycle pair) but its next tool turn executes through the NEW dispatcher/context whose pair is the config default — tool calls (order placement, candle fetches) run against the wrong pair/broker mid-cycle. Also every unrelated config save resets the AnyCandle divider phase (line 202), shifting analysis timing.
findings.fix: Acquire self._run_lock (or defer via a pending-config flag applied between cycles) before calling _apply_config in the refresh branch; preserve _m5_candle_event_count across refreshes unless the divider value changed.

findings.title: ISO-timestamp parsing duplicated at ~12 sites; the decided_at parse diverges (no Z-handling, no tz attach, no error guard)
findings.impact: A malformed timestamp raises ValueError inside _publish_analysis-path code (crashing that publish) instead of falling back; a tz-naive string produces a naive decided_at persisted next to aware datetimes — mixed-tz rows in the DB that mis-sort trade timelines.
findings.fix: Promote _parse_timestamp (analysis_snapshot.py:214) to a shared util (e.g. utils/time_utils.parse_iso_utc) and replace all inline copies.

findings.title: Snapshot-building + snapshot-system-prompt + cycle execution logic is duplicated (and already divergent) between _run_cycle_inner and the management API execute endpoint
findings.impact: The 'execute agent now' API path and the live trigger path produce different prompts and skip the assembly-script cancel and decision-only engine — manual test runs do not reproduce live behaviour, and every future change must be made twice (they have already drifted).
findings.fix: Extract one shared method on Agent (e.g. run_manual_cycle(profile_overrides, input_text)) that reuses _run_cycle_inner's snapshot/prompt logic, and have the API endpoint call it instead of duplicating the pipeline.

findings.title: Timer-loop cycles and runtime config refresh mutate shared ToolContext/agent state concurrently with message-loop cycles; _run_lock does not protect them
findings.impact: When an agent has both timer and event triggers enabled, an overlapping timer cycle can overwrite `context.pair` mid-cycle, so tools (including auto_place_order for a BA) execute against the WRONG instrument, and the finally-restore can persist the wrong pair. Config-save during a running timer cycle swaps the dispatcher between turns, mixing tool configs. Timers are currently disabled in config, so this is latent — but any config change enabling a timer arms it.
findings.fix: Acquire `self._run_lock` in `_run_timer_loop` (and around `_apply_config` runtime refresh, or defer refresh until the lock is free), restore `context.triggering_message` in the finally block, or better: stop mutating the shared context — pass per-cycle pair/extra explicitly through ToolContext copies.

findings.title: _should_use_snapshot_context omits ec_output although the cycle explicitly treats ec_output analysis payloads as equivalent to analysis_result — BA cycles triggered via EC run without the market snapshot
findings.impact: The same BA makes execution decisions WITH a broker/market snapshot when triggered by analysis_result but WITHOUT one when triggered by ec_output. The BA prompt's conditional guards (broker_execution_context.broker_may_open_trade, allowed_direction) are "if exists" rules, so on the EC path they vacuously pass — orders can be opened without the broker-constraint context the other path enforces. Divergent, trigger-dependent trading behavior that looks random in production.
findings.fix: Add `EventType.EC_OUTPUT.value` to the set (and handle it in `_snapshot_trigger_payload_for_cycle`), or switch the gate to the same content-based `_is_analysis_trigger` detection used at lines 750-754.

findings.title: Decision-only cycle records the WRONG system prompt in the LLM_REQUEST audit event
findings.impact: The monitoring/audit trail for every snapshot-decision cycle (the main AA trading path per config) shows a system prompt that was never sent. Post-mortems of bad trading decisions will analyse the wrong prompt and reach wrong conclusions.
findings.fix: Build the decision-only prompt once into a local variable and pass it as `system_prompt_override` to `_emit_llm_request` (and use its length at line 1220), then reuse it in the `llm_complete` call.

findings.title: Duplicate tool output_keys are never validated — later block silently overwrites earlier (e.g. H1 candles replace M5 candles)
findings.impact: Two get_candles blocks configured with the same output_key (e.g. both "candles" for SHORT_TF and LONG_TF) mean every calc script and the assembly script silently compute swing levels/ATR on the wrong timeframe's candles — systematically skewed decisions with zero diagnostics. This is the candle-source key collision the owner suspects.
findings.fix: In _normalize_tool_blocks (or phase 1 of _execute_tool_blocks), detect duplicate resolved output_keys and append f"{block_id}:duplicate_output_key:{output_key}" to errors.

findings.title: safe_globals is one shared module-level mutable dict used as exec globals for ALL scripts of ALL agents — `global` statements and module attribute mutations leak state across agents and across cycles
findings.impact: Cross-agent, cross-cycle state contamination: a value computed for EURUSD agent A leaks into GBPUSD agent B's script namespace, or a stale value from last week's cycle masks a NameError that should have failed the block — nondeterministic decisions that depend on execution history.
findings.fix: Build a fresh globals dict per exec call: `exec(compiled, {**safe_globals}, locals_payload)` (or a factory function returning a new dict), and consider passing frozen wrappers for math/statistics.

findings.title: Preview applies NO default transform while live path injects the tool-specific default — preview output shape differs from live snapshot output
findings.impact: A block validated in the UI preview shows raw tool JSON, but the live snapshot contains DEFAULT_CANDLE_TRANSFORM_SCRIPT/DEFAULT_INDICATOR_TRANSFORM_SCRIPT output — calc scripts written against the previewed shape break (or silently miscompute) in production.
findings.fix: Route preview blocks through the same default-resolution as _normalize_tool_blocks (extract a shared resolve_transform_script(block) helper), and use `raw.get("transform_script")` with `if ... is None` so an explicit empty string disables the default.

findings.title: preview_calculation_block returns {'error': ...} on unknown type but its consumer reads only 'result'/'errors' — the error is silently dropped
findings.impact: UI calculation preview for a mistyped block type shows result=null with an empty errors list — the user gets no signal that the type is invalid, then saves a config that the live path silently skips (see finding on line 654).
findings.fix: Return `{"result": None, "errors": [f"unknown_calculation_type:{calc_type}"]}` to match the shape of every other return.

findings.title: Prompt-selector script exceptions are swallowed and silently fall back to prompt id 1; int/str id mismatch also silently selects prompts[0]
findings.impact: A broken selector script (or string-typed ids in system.json5) makes every cycle silently run with the first/default system prompt instead of the market-condition-specific one — behavioral drift on the money path with zero diagnostics, invisible for weeks.
findings.fix: Log/emit the selector exception (agent has monitoring emitters); normalize both sides of the id comparison (`str(p.get("id")) == str(selected_id)`), and fail loudly (or emit a warning event) when no prompt matches.

findings.title: Prompt-selector script receives LIVE references to the snapshot (no deepcopy, unlike every other script sandbox) and can mutate the decision snapshot in place
findings.impact: A selector script that 'cleans' or annotates tool_outputs (natural, since assembly scripts are allowed to) mutates the actual decision snapshot dict that the agent later reuses (agent.py passes decision_snapshot onward after building the system prompt at agent.py:878) — the snapshot the LLM/decision engine sees differs from the one emitted via _emit_analysis_snapshot_built.
findings.fix: Deepcopy snap and its sub-dicts before putting them in locals_, matching the transform/assembly sandboxes.

findings.title: exec with separate globals/locals dicts: functions and comprehensions defined inside config scripts cannot see script-level variables or injected helpers (NameError at call time)
findings.impact: Config scripts that work when written 'flat' break unpredictably the moment a user factors code into a helper function or uses a comprehension referencing a script variable — producing transform_failed/calc error dicts; combined with the calc-error-swallowing finding this yields silent snapshot degradation, and on the live tool path it causes skipped cycles (missed trades) that look random.
findings.fix: Pass the SAME dict as globals and locals: `env = {**safe_globals_fresh, **locals_payload}; exec(compiled, env, env)` and read results back from env — this gives scripts normal module-level scoping.

findings.title: config/snapshot_helpers.py is cached forever (including a not-found False sentinel) — violates the project's mandatory no-restart hot-reload rule for config/ files
findings.impact: Editing normalization/direction-classification logic in config/snapshot_helpers.py (e.g. fixing a wrong ATR threshold) silently does nothing until a full restart — the operator believes the fix is live while agents keep trading on the old logic; if the file was missing at startup, every default candle/indicator transform NameErrors forever.
findings.fix: Reload the module when the file's mtime changes (cache (mtime, module)), or expose a reload hook triggered by the management API save route, consistent with the other config hot-reload mechanisms.

findings.title: Entire in-file fallback normalization cluster is dead code duplicating config/snapshot_helpers.py — and it falsely suggests a safety net that is never wired into the script sandbox
findings.impact: ~200 lines of misleading dead code; maintainers 'fix' the dead copy and see no effect (the owner's read-before-opinion pain); the illusory fallback hides a hard runtime dependency on an optional-looking config file.
findings.fix: Delete the dead cluster entirely; if a built-in fallback is desired, register the in-file functions into transform_locals when the config helper is absent — otherwise make the helper file mandatory at startup.

findings.title: CALCULATION_HANDLERS machinery is dead: registry is always empty, handler branch unreachable, sources/grouping logic only serves the unreachable path
findings.impact: Dead machinery obscures the actual single code path (script blocks → 'global' group), inviting edits to unreachable code; the sources feature in profile configs is silently non-functional for scripts (a configured 'sources' mapping on a script block does nothing).
findings.fix: Remove CALCULATION_HANDLERS, the handler branches, resolved_sources building, and the grouping constants — or actually register handlers if typed calculations are intended.

findings.title: Prompt-selector exec logic duplicated in management API test endpoint with divergent sandbox globals and divergent fallback semantics
findings.impact: A selector script using `math.log(...)` passes the UI test endpoint check... actually the reverse: it FAILS the test endpoint (NameError: math) while working live — or a script tested green behaves differently live because the fallback entry differs. Operators cannot trust the test tool; the two copies will drift further.
findings.fix: Extract a shared run_prompt_selector(script, snapshot) function in analysis_snapshot.py used by both the live path and the API test endpoint, with identical globals and fallback behavior.

findings.title: EC session_filter is parsed and stored but never enforced — ECs run 24h regardless of configured session windows
findings.impact: An EC that relays/guards signals or adjusts trailing stop-losses (e.g. OXS_T-EURUSD-EC-TRSLF) with a session filter configured (e.g. London/NY only) silently also runs during illiquid Asian hours or around rollover: signals get relayed and SLs get moved on wide-spread, thin-liquidity candles. Losses look random and only correlate with time-of-day after weeks.
findings.fix: In `_run_message_loop` (and the timer loop) evaluate the session filter before `_run_cycle`, mirroring agents/agent.py `_is_session_allowed` (candle-timestamp based), and emit a trigger-skipped monitoring event when blocked. Factor the session check into one shared helper instead of a third copy.

findings.title: EC loops ignore the global runtime pause — ECs keep executing scripts, calling tools and LLMs while the system is paused
findings.impact: Operator pauses the system (e.g. during a news event or to investigate an incident) expecting no trading activity; a trailing-SL or relay EC keeps firing on M5 candles, modifying stop-losses / relaying signals via its tools. Positions get altered during an intentional freeze — losses attributed to 'random' behavior.
findings.fix: Import `openforexai.runtime.control` and skip trigger processing (with an EC trigger-skipped monitoring event) when `is_paused()`, same as the agent loops.

findings.title: Timer enable/disable is not hot-swappable: the timer loop runs on self._running only and the timer task is only created once in start()
findings.impact: Once EC config refresh exists (or via EC_CONFIG_RESPONSE today if it were delivered), turning a timer-driven EC's timer off via config save has no effect — the EC keeps executing on schedule (e.g. periodically adjusting SLs) although the operator disabled it; conversely enabling a timer does nothing until full restart. Violates the no-restart principle.
findings.fix: Change the loop condition to `while self._running:` plus `if not self._timer_enabled: await asyncio.sleep(1); continue`, and always create the timer task in start() (it idles cheaply when disabled).

findings.title: ToolsProxy.call discards ToolResult.is_error — EC scripts get no reliable error signal from tool calls, so guard scripts can fail open
findings.impact: A guard script doing `positions = await tools.call("get_open_positions")` and iterating the result treats an error dict/string as 'no open positions' (or crashes depending on shape) — e.g. `{"error": ...}.get("positions", [])` yields [] → guard concludes no exposure → approves a signal that should have been blocked. Rare (only when the broker tool intermittently fails) and financially harmful.
findings.fix: Either raise a dedicated `ToolError(parsed)` from ToolsProxy.call when `result.is_error` (scripts then fail closed by default via EC_RUN_FAILED), or return a stable envelope `{"ok": bool, "data": parsed, "error": ...}`.

findings.title: Malformed config_json is silently swallowed and replaced by {} — the EC runs with empty configuration and no signal
findings.impact: A typo while editing an EC's config_json (trailing comma etc.) makes the EC silently run with `config == {}`. A trailing-SL script reading `config.get("atr_multiple", 2)` falls back to defaults, or a guard reading thresholds treats missing values permissively — behavior changes with zero indication anywhere.
findings.fix: Log an error and emit a MonitoringEventType.SYSTEM_ERROR / EC-config-invalid event on parse failure; consider refusing to run (fail closed) until config_json parses, like the compiled-script None guard at line 340.

findings.title: Config-response timeout leaves the EC registered on the bus forever, making it unrevivable via config save and turning its queue into a dead letterbox
findings.impact: If ConfigService is slow/busy for 30s at boot (or the EC starts before ConfigService's loop), the EC dies silently but stays 'registered'. Routed events pile into its queue until maxsize (then broadcasts get drop-warnings), and toggling enable off/on in the config UI does NOT restart it because the registered-check filters it out. The EC is unrecoverable without a full restart — invisible until its guard/relay function is missed.
findings.fix: On config timeout call `self._bus.unregister_member(self.ec_id)` before returning (and ideally emit SYSTEM_ERROR + retry the config request a few times).

findings.title: trigger_sync (inbox task) and _sync_loop (background task) run the same import logic concurrently with no lock — TOCTOU double-import of broker positions
findings.impact: When an agent calls trigger_sync while the periodic sync is mid-pass over the same pair, an externally-opened position is imported twice → two OPEN order-book rows for one broker position; both later get closed with the same realized pnl → double-counted P&L and phantom trade history.
findings.fix: Guard the whole sync body with an `asyncio.Lock` per adapter (or per pair) shared by _sync_loop and trigger_sync.

findings.title: Orphan resolution marks entries REJECTED when find_closed_trade_by_sync_key returns None — but OANDA never overrides the default that always returns None, so filled-and-closed trades are recorded as never having happened
findings.impact: An order that fills and then closes (fast SL hit) before the ORDER_RESULT response is persisted (bus timeout, crash, the stringify bug) leaves a PENDING entry without broker_order_id; 120s later it is marked REJECTED. The realized loss exists at the broker but never in the order book — account balance drifts from recorded P&L with no discoverable trade record. Also note the entry is marked REJECTED even when the lookup merely isn't supported, conflating 'unknown' with 'rejected'.
findings.fix: Implement find_closed_trade_by_sync_key for OANDA (transactions endpoint filtered by clientExtensions.comment). In base.py, distinguish 'lookup unsupported/None' from 'confirmed rejected' — e.g. keep the entry PENDING with a retry counter and only reject after N failed lookups, and emit a monitoring event instead of silently rejecting.

findings.title: trigger_sync's matched-entry update omits stop_loss/take_profit and emits no discrepancy events, unlike _sync_loop's twin code
findings.impact: A sync triggered by an agent tool does not refresh local SL/TP after broker-side stop modifications (e.g. trailing stop moved), so local risk data stays stale until the periodic loop runs; and sync-detected closes found via trigger_sync never appear on the event bus, so EC guards / composers that react to ORDER_BOOK_SYNC_DISCREPANCY miss them — same event observable or not depending on which code path found it.
findings.fix: Deduplicate: extract one _sync_pair(pair, event_bus, emit_events: bool) used by both; include SL/TP in the update and publish the same events from both paths.

findings.title: ~80 lines of position-sync logic duplicated between _sync_loop and trigger_sync, including two identical OrderBookEntry import constructions
findings.impact: Every future sync fix must be applied twice; the two copies have already drifted, producing path-dependent persistence behavior.
findings.fix: Extract a single `async def _sync_pair(self, pair, event_bus, *, publish_events: bool) -> list[dict]` used by both the loop and trigger_sync. Move `_adapter_agent_id` to a shared module imported by the tools.

findings.title: TradeStatus enum explicitly 'kept for backward compatibility' duplicates a subset of OrderStatus — two enums for the same order-state concept
findings.impact: Divergent twin enums for one concept; any new state (e.g. PARTIALLY_FILLED) added to OrderStatus cannot round-trip through TradeResult, and cross-enum string comparison at order_execution.py:546 silently degrades any non-OPEN fill state to PENDING. Owner explicitly wants compat shims removed.
findings.fix: Delete TradeStatus, use OrderStatus in TradeResult, and update brokers/DB adapters (sqlite.py:250, postgresql.py:250) and order_execution.py:546 to compare enum members directly.

findings.title: int(p.volume * 100_000) truncates float lot volumes — units off by one, full closes rejected as 'exceed current position size'
findings.impact: A position of 0.29 lots is reported as 28999 units. If a caller derives units from the true size (29000) or from OANDA-style bookkeeping and requests close of 29000, line 424 raises 'units to close exceed current position size' → close REJECTED → position stays open unintended (unbounded loss exposure). Also `close_units == current_units` (line 459) misclassifies full closes as partial, leaving entries OPEN locally.
findings.fix: Use int(round(p.volume * 100_000)) (or Decimal(str(p.volume)) * 100000) in both places.

findings.title: get_open_positions sets current_price to the OPEN price — t.get("price", t["price"]) is a no-op fallback to the same key
findings.impact: Every consumer of Position.current_price on OANDA (POSITIONS_RESPONSE payloads to agents/UI) sees the entry price forever — e.g. an agent evaluating whether to close early computes zero price movement while unrealized_pnl says otherwise; displayed/queried data is wrong and inconsistent with MT5.
findings.fix: Fetch current pricing (GET /v3/accounts/{id}/pricing?instruments=...) once per get_open_positions call, or derive: current = open_price + unrealizedPL / currentUnits (direction-signed); at minimum document the field as unavailable rather than silently wrong.

findings.title: Fixed broker_utc_offset_hours cannot model broker DST — all MT5 timestamps off by 1h for half the year
findings.impact: During winter, every MT5 candle timestamp converts to a UTC instant 1h wrong. base._select_recent_m5_window compares candle.timestamp against expected_open (UTC): with a wrong offset the freshest candle appears older/newer than expected, trigger selection picks a stale bar, gap detection misfires, cross-broker (OANDA vs MT5) candle tables for the same pair disagree by 12 M5 slots — subtle, seasonal, exactly the reported defect profile.
findings.fix: Use a named IANA zone (zoneinfo, e.g. 'EET') per broker, or auto-derive the offset by comparing a fresh M5 candle time against wall-clock UTC at connect().

findings.title: get_closed_trade_result P&L uses only the LAST exit deal's profit — earlier partial-close profits, commission and swap are dropped
findings.impact: pnl_account_currency written into the order book for sync-detected closes understates or misstates realized P&L whenever a position was partially closed or carried swap — recorded performance diverges from account statements over weeks; OptimizationAgent trains on wrong outcomes.
findings.fix: Sum profit + commission + swap + fee across all deals of the position (entry deals have profit 0 so summing all is safe): `pnl = sum(Decimal(str(d.profit + d.commission + d.swap + getattr(d, 'fee', 0))) for d in sorted_deals)`.

findings.title: Units→lots conversion silently resizes orders (round to 0.01 lot) and produces volume 0.0 for units < 500
findings.impact: Actual position size deviates from the risk-model size by up to ±500 units with no log; local units vs broker units mismatch feeds the close/partial-close comparisons; small accounts (risk-sized units < 500) can never open a position and the failure surfaces only as a rejected order.
findings.fix: Query symbol_info(pair).volume_step/volume_min, round to the step, raise if below volume_min, and write the actually-sent units back into the TradeResult/order book.

findings.title: MT5 silently falls back to entry_price for pending-order price where OANDA raises ValueError
findings.impact: The same malformed TradeOrder is rejected on OANDA but silently placed at signal.entry_price (or the wrong price field) on MT5 — a resting order at an unintended level that eventually fills and loses money with no error trail.
findings.fix: Mirror OANDA's validation: raise ValueError when the required price field for the order type is missing; never cross-fall-back between limit_price and stop_price.

findings.title: OANDA never implements find_closed_trade_by_sync_key although it tags orders with sync_key — orphaned OANDA entries are always marked REJECTED
findings.impact: An OANDA order that filled and closed before the first sync (place_order response lost, entry left without broker_order_id) is unrecoverable: the entry is marked REJECTED even though real money was made/lost — the trade vanishes from local P&L accounting.
findings.fix: Implement it via GET /v3/accounts/{id}/transactions (filter type ORDER_FILL, match clientExtensions comment == sync_key) — or explicitly document/log that OANDA cannot recover orphans.

findings.title: Broker-rejection signaling diverges: OANDA raises HTTPStatusError, MT5 returns TradeResult(status=REJECTED)
findings.impact: Consumers (order_execution.py:519-540) see two different payload shapes for the same business event 'broker rejected the order': OANDA rejections raise RuntimeError and leave the order-book entry PENDING (never marked REJECTED with a reason), MT5 rejections are recorded properly — divergent books per broker.
findings.fix: In the OANDA adapter, catch 4xx responses on order endpoints and return TradeResult(status=REJECTED, close_reason=<errorMessage/rejectReason from body>), matching MT5.

findings.title: _call_blocking timeout abandons the still-running MT5 call — an order can fill after the caller was told it timed out
findings.impact: On a slow terminal, place_order raises TimeoutError → base reports order failed → agent/supervisor retries → duplicate position; the first fill is only discovered by the sync import as an anonymous entry. Same for close: a 'failed' close that actually closed leads to a second close attempt.
findings.fix: For mutating calls, after a timeout reconcile via positions_get/history before allowing a resubmit (e.g. search for the sync_key comment); or use a much larger timeout for order_send than for reads and surface 'outcome unknown' instead of 'failed'.

findings.title: PG adapter never creates assessment_memory, ec_runs, or kb_* tables — get/set_assessment_memory and save_ec_run fail with UndefinedTableError on PostgreSQL
findings.impact: On PostgreSQL, every EC run persistence attempt and every assessment-memory read/write raises asyncpg.exceptions.UndefinedTableError. EC audit history and agent assessment memory silently disappear if callers swallow the exception, or crash the composer loop if not.
findings.fix: Create assessment_memory and ec_runs (and kb_documents/kb_fts equivalents, see separate finding) in _ensure_core_tables, or run the shared migrations directory against PostgreSQL.

findings.title: PG twin has no _safe_row_to_order_book_entry: one corrupt row aborts the entire get_open_order_book_entries result, diverging from SQLite's skip-with-warning behavior
findings.impact: On PostgreSQL a single undeserializable historical row makes every sync-loop invocation raise, so ALL open positions stop being reconciled (worse than SQLite losing one). Behavior of the system depends on which backend is configured.
findings.fix: Pick one policy (recommend: raise/quarantine per previous finding) and implement it identically in both adapters, ideally in shared code in base.py.

findings.title: Single shared aiosqlite connection with implicit transactions: concurrent coroutines' statements interleave and one task's commit() commits another task's half-finished multi-statement operation
findings.impact: Under concurrent agent/composer/API activity, partially-applied logical operations become durable (FTS index divergence, or an order_book UPDATE committed by an unrelated task before its caller decided to abort). Rare, load-dependent, non-crashing corruption.
findings.fix: Guard each logical operation with an asyncio.Lock around execute+commit, or use one connection per operation / `async with conn` transaction scoping (aiosqlite supports `isolation_level=None` + explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT under a lock).

findings.title: Migration runner is non-atomic and intolerant: a crash between executescript and the filename INSERT (or a mid-script failure) re-runs non-idempotent migration 003, whose duplicate ALTER TABLE then crashes startup
findings.impact: After a crash or partial failure during migration, every subsequent startup raises sqlite3.OperationalError('duplicate column name: reasoning') inside initialize() — trading system cannot boot until someone hand-edits schema_migrations.
findings.fix: Wrap each migration in try/except that tolerates 'duplicate column name' for ALTER statements (or make migrations idempotent), and record the filename in the same transaction as the script where possible.

findings.title: Legacy dual-column decision_type shim: value written to both decision_type and decision_type_new, read back via COALESCE(decision_type_new, decision_type)
findings.impact: Owner explicitly wants all backward-compat dual-field reads removed. The shim also hides data drift: rows where the two columns ever diverge are resolved silently by COALESCE priority.
findings.fix: Backfill decision_type from decision_type_new where needed, drop decision_type_new (or the legacy column), write and filter on a single column.

findings.title: Analysis record shape diverges between backends: PG returns a 'setup_type' key, SQLite does not
findings.impact: Any consumer of get_analysis_records that reads record["setup_type"] gets KeyError (or None via .get, silently losing the field) on SQLite while working on PostgreSQL — same concept, different shape per backend. Frontend/optimization logic behaves differently depending on configured DB.
findings.fix: Add setup_type to the SQLite _row_to_analysis_record, or better, deduplicate _row_to_analysis_record into base.py so it cannot drift (see duplicate finding).

findings.title: Knowledge-base methods silently no-op on PostgreSQL: PG adapter never overrides kb_* so it inherits base-class stubs that return empty results
findings.impact: On PostgreSQL the handbook API returns HTTP 200 with empty lists and kb_create_document 'succeeds' returning an empty id — user documents are silently discarded with no error anywhere. The non-abstract silent defaults in the port are the enabler: a missing implementation is undetectable.
findings.fix: Either implement kb_* for PostgreSQL or make the port methods raise NotImplementedError by default so the gap fails loudly.

findings.title: Whole deserialization/helper layer duplicated verbatim between the SQLite and PostgreSQL adapters, despite base.py declaring itself the home for shared utilities
findings.impact: Drift has already produced the setup_type divergence and the _safe_row wrapper divergence; every future fix must be applied twice and demonstrably isn't.
findings.fix: Move all row→model deserializers, _series_table/_sanitize, _to_db and _deserialize_json_field into base.py as shared functions consumed by both adapters.

findings.title: _bootstrap_migration_history is a backward-compat shim for databases created 'before migration tracking was introduced'
findings.impact: Owner wants all compat shims removed. This one also carries risk: it infers migration state from partial evidence (003 registered solely because 'reasoning' column exists — the other three ALTERs of 003 are assumed).
findings.fix: Once all live DBs have a populated schema_migrations table, delete _bootstrap_migration_history and its call site (lines 67-70).

findings.title: DDL executed on every hot-path call: _ensure_order_book_table (CREATE TABLE + 3 CREATE INDEX + PRAGMA table_info + conditional ALTERs) runs before every single order-book read/write
findings.impact: Several extra schema statements per repository call, serialized through the single SQLite connection — added latency on the order execution and sync paths, and extra pool round-trips on PG.
findings.fix: Run all _ensure_* once in initialize() (SQLite already has initialize/_run_migrations for this) and drop the per-call invocations, or cache a _tables_ready flag.

findings.title: kb_search swallows ALL exceptions and returns [] — DB failures and FTS syntax errors are indistinguishable from 'no hits'
findings.impact: Searching for anything with punctuation (e.g. 'EUR/USD', '"risk') silently returns nothing — the user believes the knowledgebase does not contain the term. Real database failures are hidden the same way.
findings.fix: Catch only sqlite3.OperationalError and in that case fall back to a literal query (wrap each term in double quotes with internal quotes doubled); let all other exceptions propagate to a 500.

findings.title: Null candles are synthesized with UTC tzinfo while MT5 candles carry broker-local tzinfo — same instant produces different TEXT primary keys and breaks ORDER BY / REPLACE in SQLite
findings.impact: When `_ensure_m5_complete_for_read` writes a null for a slot whose real MT5 candle arrives seconds later (every 5-min boundary race), both rows persist forever under different keys. `LIMIT n` newest-row selection then returns instant-misordered mixtures within every 3h overlap window: null rows crowd out real candles from the LIMIT window (fewer real bars than requested after `_drop_null_candles`), and the `list(reversed(raw))` 'oldest-first' assumption is violated across tz families. Result: indicator windows silently shortened/shifted for MT5 pairs, unbounded junk rows, and D1 bucket alignment computed on non-UTC instants — rare, data-dependent wrong indicator values.
findings.fix: Normalize every Candle timestamp to UTC (`.astimezone(UTC)`) at a single choke point — either in the Candle model (pydantic validator) or in the store before `isoformat()` — so all rows share one canonical text representation. Fix MT5Broker to convert to UTC instead of relabeling to broker tz.

findings.title: Tick ask computed as close + spread — adds a pips/points value directly to a price
findings.impact: Any consumer of `DataContainer.get_snapshot()`'s `current_tick.ask` (or `Tick.mid`) gets a price wrong by orders of magnitude for MT5 (and ask==bid for OANDA where candle spread is absent → 0). Currently only tests call `get_snapshot`, so the bug is latent — but it sits on a public data-access API named identically to the port method, waiting to be wired into an agent/risk path. Also note the pips-vs-points unit inconsistency between MT5 (points) and the model contract (pips) propagates to analysis_snapshot.py:183 and management/api.py which show `spread` to LLMs/UI at 10x scale for MT5.
findings.fix: Compute `ask = last.close + last.spread * pip_size(pair)` after fixing the MT5 adapter to convert points→pips (spread_raw / 10 for 5/3-digit symbols, using `mt5.symbol_info(pair).digits`), or store spread in absolute price units everywhere and update the model docstring.

findings.title: _NULL_FILTER_BUFFER_M5 (1 week) is too small for D1 reads — weekend null candles crowd real candles out of the LIMIT window, silently shortening D1 history
findings.impact: `get_candles(..., 'D1')` and `get_snapshot()` return ~50 D1 bars instead of the configured 60, silently. Any D1 indicator with period 50+ (SMA50, EMA50) returns None or is computed on a shorter-than-intended window; snapshot D1 context handed to LLM agents is truncated. No error, no log — just quietly degraded long-timeframe analysis.
findings.fix: Scale the buffer with the requested window (e.g. `buffer = ceil(window_days / 7) * 2 * 288 + margin`), or better: exclude expected-closed sessions from `_missing_slots_in_recent_window` instead of persisting null rows at all, and query the DB by time range rather than row LIMIT.

findings.title: Every read with any missing recent slot triggers a broker fetch of the FULL window — up to 17,592 candles per D1/get_snapshot read
findings.impact: Repeated multi-second broker round-trips and full-window DB rewrites on the hot read path; under the 60s `_BROKER_FETCH_TIMEOUT` a slow MT5 terminal stalls every agent snapshot/indicator read for that pair, and live candle writes queue behind the lock. Wasted rate limits on OANDA.
findings.fix: Fetch only the missing span: `fetch_count = slots_between(min(missing_before), now) + margin`, or fetch from the newest existing timestamp forward. Keep the large backfill only for the empty-DB case.

findings.title: register_broker ('Kept for bootstrap compatibility'), no-op subscribe_to_bus, and no-op initialize are compat shims still invoked by bootstrap
findings.impact: Owner explicitly wants all backward-compat constructs removed. These no-ops make bootstrap look like it wires subscriptions/initialization that don't exist; note `_initial_backfill` only backfills pairs registered via this 'compat' call before run() starts, so deleting it naively breaks startup backfill — the pairs list should be passed explicitly.
findings.fix: Replace with an explicit `register_pairs(broker_short_name: str, pairs: list[str])`, delete subscribe_to_bus and the empty initialize, and update bootstrap.py accordingly.

findings.title: AbstractDataContainer exists explicitly as a backward-compat superset of AbstractRepository
findings.impact: Owner wants all compat constructs removed: the dual-port hierarchy doubles the surface area (two adapter modules per backend, two ports) for one concept ('the store'), and code still type-hinting AbstractRepository silently lacks the agent-memory API.
findings.fix: Merge AbstractRepository into AbstractDataContainer (one port, one adapter per backend), migrate all `AbstractRepository` type hints, and delete the old port.

findings.title: _get_candles_from_db and get_candles duplicate the entire M5-read + null-drop + resample + trim pipeline
findings.impact: Any fix (e.g. excluding the forming bucket, buffer sizing) must be applied in three places; they have already drifted once (`_emit` only in get_candles). Classic source of the 'one path fixed, other path still wrong' rare defect.
findings.fix: Extract a private `_read_and_resample(broker, pair, timeframe, limit)` used by all three, with `ensure_complete: bool` parameter.
