findings.title: The entire agent-memory API (6 methods, duplicated in both containers) has zero production callers
findings.impact: ~450 lines of untested, unexercised persistence code across both backends. The port's promise that 'agents can resume meaningfully after a restart' (data_container.py docstring) is not fulfilled anywhere — LLM conversations and performance snapshots are never actually saved. Maintenance burden plus a false sense of having agent memory.
findings.fix: Either wire the agent lifecycle (agents/agent.py run_cycle) to call save_llm_conversation/save_agent_decision_with_reasoning as the port documents, or delete the six methods from both containers and the port until needed.

findings.title: Legacy dual-field writes in save_agent_decision_with_reasoning: decision_type written to old+new column, hardcoded agent_role, empty input_context/output 'kept for compat'
findings.impact: Owner explicitly wants all backward-compat constructs removed. The old/new decision_type twin-column scheme means any future consumer reading the wrong column gets stale or duplicated semantics; empty '{}' legacy blobs waste space and mislead analysis tooling into thinking input_context/output were captured.
findings.fix: Migrate to a single decision_type column (rename decision_type_new -> decision_type in a migration), drop the hardcoded agent_role='trading' and the empty legacy JSON fields, and remove the COALESCE dual reads in both parent repositories.

findings.title: Class/module docstrings are factually wrong in both directions: claim candle/trade methods are NotImplementedError stubs (they are fully implemented) and claim agent-memory is 'ready to use' (it cannot work against the PG schema)
findings.impact: A maintainer reading these docstrings will (a) wrongly avoid the PG backend for candle storage, and (b) wrongly trust the agent-memory methods on PG — the inverse of the truth on both counts. Misleading documentation on a money-adjacent persistence layer directly feeds wrong operational decisions.
findings.fix: Rewrite the docstrings to state the verified reality: candle/trade/order methods fully implemented in PostgreSQLRepository; agent-memory methods require schema objects (agent_conversations, agent_performance, extended agent_decisions) that PG setup does not yet create.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget asyncio.create_task(self._handle(msg)) without holding a reference — task can be garbage-collected mid-flight and the caller's future never resolves
findings.impact: Rarely and non-deterministically, an LLM request produces no LLM_RESPONSE; the agent blocks in llm_helpers' asyncio.wait_for for 180 s, then raises TimeoutError — a random-looking missed trading cycle weeks apart, with no crash and no error log at the moment it matters.
findings.fix: Keep a `self._tasks: set[asyncio.Task]` — `task = asyncio.create_task(...); self._tasks.add(task); task.add_done_callback(self._tasks.discard)` — and wrap the final publish in _handle in try/except with error logging.

findings.title: Empty tools list is sent as tools=[] with tool_choice='auto' — OpenAI/Azure reject an empty tools array with 400
findings.impact: Any EC script or caller that uses ask_llm without tools against an OpenAI-family provider gets a 400 on every attempt (retried 3x with backoff, then RuntimeError). The Azure error text ('empty array') does not contain 'invalid_prompt', so the fallback does not mask it — the EC just fails each run.
findings.fix: Only include "tools"/"tool_choice" in kwargs when the list is non-empty (both openai.py and azure.py).

findings.title: _inject_images_* stringifies structured list content of the last user message, destroying tool_result blocks when images are present
findings.impact: Agents that combine chart images with tool calls fail (or feed the LLM a Python-repr string of tool results instead of the actual results) on every turn after the first tool call — intermittent, config-dependent failures of exactly the image+tools setups used for chart analysis.
findings.fix: In all three injectors: if the existing content is a list, append the image blocks to the list (Anthropic) / append image_url parts (OpenAI) instead of replacing it; only wrap in a text block when content is a str.

findings.title: Malformed tool-call JSON is silently swallowed and replaced with empty arguments {}
findings.impact: When the model emits truncated/invalid JSON arguments (more likely when output is truncated, see the 'length' finding), the tool is executed with EMPTY arguments — e.g. an order/indicator tool called with all-default parameters — instead of failing. Silent wrong-parameter execution on a money path.
findings.fix: On JSONDecodeError (or non-dict result), log at ERROR and surface it — e.g. mark the ToolCall invalid so the dispatcher returns an is_error ToolResult — never proceed with {}.

findings.title: _inject_images_openai and _to_openai_tool are copy-pasted between openai.py and azure.py; complete_structured fence-parsing is triplicated; message builders are divergent twins
findings.impact: Fixes applied to one copy (e.g. the list-content image bug, or the null-content Azure workaround) silently miss the twin, producing provider-dependent behavior differences that surface as rare inconsistencies.
findings.fix: Extract shared helpers (image injection, tool conversion, fence-strip JSON parsing, OpenAI-format message builders) into one module (e.g. adapters/llm/_openai_common.py) and have both providers plus anthropic's structured parsing use them.

findings.title: set_debug_diagnostics / _emit_debug_diagnostic machinery has no caller anywhere — all attempt-callback plumbing in azure.py is dead, and transcript context headers are always empty
findings.impact: Large dead surface that suggests HTTP-attempt diagnostics exist when they don't (LLMService also never emits them, see next finding) — misleading during incident analysis; transcripts lack the agent/turn attribution they were designed to carry.
findings.fix: Either wire LLMService to call llm.set_debug_diagnostics per request (careful: shared provider instance + concurrent per-request tasks would race on the single callback/context — needs per-call context instead), or delete set_debug_diagnostics from ports/llm.py + azure.py and all attempt-callback closures, and drop the no-op in agent.py.

findings.title: scan_prompts_for_images ignores messages whose content is a list — markers inside content blocks are neither stripped nor resolved
findings.impact: A tool that returns a chart path via imagetmp[] works on the first turn (str content) but silently stops working once conversations use block-format content — the LLM 'sees' a filename string instead of the image, degrading decisions without any error.
findings.fix: Also scan/strip 'text' blocks inside list content in scan_prompts_for_images (mirror _strip_messages_comments in ports/llm.py:47-62, which already handles the list-content case for comments).

findings.title: _resolve_broker_name_override accepts any unvalidated string as broker_name (KeyError fallback returns broker_key.upper())
findings.impact: get_candles then sends CANDLES_REQUEST with broker_name="OANDA" while DataContainer stores candles under the runtime short_name (e.g. "OAPR1"); container._get_candles_from_db auto-tracks the unknown key (container.py:546 _ensure_pair_tracked) and returns an empty list with error=None — the tool returns [] with NO error. The agent silently analyses zero/empty market data or a trading tool targets a nonexistent broker member and times out. Occurs only on the occasions the LLM chooses to fill the optional broker argument with the wrong casing/name — rare and random-seeming.
findings.fix: On KeyError, also try matching broker_key case-insensitively against registered module names AND against each registered instance's short_name; if nothing matches, raise a ValueError so the tool call fails loudly instead of silently resolving to a phantom broker.

findings.title: llm_tool_config.json5 is cached forever — get_tool_default never sees config edits, violating the project's core no-restart rule
findings.impact: The owner edits config/llm_tool_config.json5 (e.g. default candle count, indicator history, swing-level parameters) expecting immediate effect per the documented 'Kein Neustart erforderlich' principle; the running system silently keeps trading with the old defaults until the next process restart. Note also: a transient read error at first call permanently caches {} (line 56), silently discarding all configured defaults for the process lifetime.
findings.fix: Either drop the cache and re-read on demand with an mtime check, or add an invalidation hook (clear _tool_defaults_cache) wired to a PUT /config/files/llm_tool_config management route, matching the hot-reload pattern of event_routing/agent_tools. Do not cache the empty dict on read failure.

findings.title: _supervisor_approval future can never be resolved — every supervisor-gated tool call stalls 15s and is rejected
findings.impact: If the owner ever configures approval_modes: {"place_order": "supervisor"} in an agent's tool_config (the documented mechanism, docs/template.tool.en.md:225), every order attempt blocks the agent cycle for 15 seconds and is then rejected with 'Supervisor approval timed out' — the supervisor gate is a designed feature that structurally cannot work. Currently dormant (no config uses it), but it is a loaded trap.
findings.fix: Make the approval message a direct request-response like bus_request (set target_agent_id to the supervisor/BA member and have the responder echo correlation_id=str(request.id)), or propagate the approval message id through the EC relay chain. Also pass triggered_by for chain integrity. If supervisor approval is not planned, delete the path.

findings.title: Bus-candle-dict → Candle conversion implemented 4x with different error handling, all swallowing bad candles silently
findings.impact: A producer-side payload change (e.g. renaming a key) would not crash anything — candles would silently vanish from indicator inputs and snapshots, exactly the 'random-seeming losses weeks later' failure class. Silent except-pass also hides systematic data corruption.
findings.fix: One shared candles_from_payload() (e.g. in models/market.py or messaging) that logs/counts every dropped row and is used by tools, container, and snapshot code.

findings.title: _compute_dxy ignores response 'error' and a missing component yields all-None values that pass the failure check
findings.impact: One broker data outage for a single component pair (e.g. USDCHF) makes the tool return {"values": [{"timestamp": null, "value": null}, ...]} instead of the intended {"values": None, "reason": ...}. The agent receives null DXY values with no explanation; in chartshot the series is silently dropped. Wrong/absent dollar-index context feeds trading decisions without any error signal.
findings.fix: Check `resp.get("error")` per component and require all 5 DXY_COMPONENTS to be present (raise or return a reason naming the missing pair). Additionally treat an all-None dxy_values list as failure: `if not any(v is not None for v in dxy_values)`.

findings.title: DXY result timestamps are always null (ref_candles computed but never used), breaking the documented contract and silently disabling DXY in chartshot
findings.impact: Agents asking for a DXY series for divergence analysis get values with null timestamps (cannot correlate to candles). A DXY line configured in a chartshot config silently never renders — `_align_to_df` returns all-NaN and the addplot is skipped with no warning.
findings.fix: Use ref_candles (tail-aligned to dxy_values after fixing the alignment bug) to attach ISO timestamps: pair each returned value with the timestamp of the candle it was computed from, like the main path does via `_ts`.

findings.title: smooth_period is a silent no-op for history=1 and warm-up-biased for small history; candle fetch does not account for smoothing
findings.impact: An agent (or snapshot block) requesting e.g. SLOPE_E with smooth_period=10 and history=1 — the exact use case the schema advertises ('Useful for slope indicators to reduce noise') — receives the raw unsmoothed value while believing it is smoothed. For history=N via chartshot (which passes smooth_period, chartshot.py:264-265), the first ~2×smooth_period points are warm-up-biased toward values[0], drawing a distorted line. Also silently ignored for BB (dict values) and on the DXY path.
findings.fix: Internally extend the computed window: request/compute `history + 3*smooth_period` values, run the smoothing EMA over the full extended series, then return the last `history` smoothed values. Document/reject smooth_period for BB and DXY explicitly.

findings.title: `or`-based defaulting makes documented value 0.0 impossible for min_gap_atr and prominence
findings.impact: An agent or chartshot config (chartshot.py:303 passes `float(swing_cfg.get("min_gap_atr", 0.3))`) that sets 0.0 to see all unclustered levels silently gets 0.3-ATR clustering instead. Levels the strategy relies on are merged away with no error — near-duplicate S/R levels vanish and entries/stops are computed against wrong levels.
findings.fix: Use explicit None checks: `raw = arguments.get("min_gap_atr"); min_gap_atr = float(raw) if raw is not None else float(_D("min_gap_atr", 0.3))` — same for prominence.

findings.title: _get_candles swallows all exceptions (incl. bus timeouts) and returns [], making infrastructure failure indistinguishable from 'no swing levels'
findings.impact: During a DataContainer stall or bus timeout the tool reports a clean result with zero support/resistance levels. A snapshot/agent consuming it concludes 'no nearby S/R' and can place or hold trades without the risk context — a silent money-path failure. This directly violates the project's fail-closed guard principle.
findings.fix: Let exceptions propagate (the dispatcher wraps them as is_error ToolResults) or include an explicit "error" field in the returned dict; at minimum log and distinguish 'DataContainer error' from genuinely empty data.

findings.title: CPU-heavy synchronous mplfinance/matplotlib rendering runs directly on the asyncio event loop
findings.impact: While a chart renders, the single event loop that also dispatches EventBus messages (order requests, candle updates, guard events) is completely blocked. Order placement/close latency spikes by seconds whenever any agent takes a chartshot — slippage and stale-price fills that look random in production.
findings.fix: Move DataFrame build + mpf.plot + savefig + file write into `await asyncio.to_thread(_render_sync, ...)`; keep only the bus requests on the loop.

findings.title: DXYPlugin.calculate (incl. _pair_closes correlation logic) is unreachable from the live tool path; its advertised output fields are never produced
findings.impact: The correlation-with-trading-pair feature described to developers (and mirrored in the tool docs) silently does not exist in production; the live DXY tool returns bare index floats. Anyone extending DXYPlugin.calculate changes nothing observable.
findings.fix: Either route the DXY tool path through DXYPlugin.calculate (passing pair closes explicitly as a parameter, not via instance mutation) so direction/correlation are actually returned, or delete DXYPlugin.calculate/_pair_closes and fix the description to match the real output.

findings.title: system.json5 read + json5-parsed synchronously from disk on every chartshot execution, inside the event loop
findings.impact: Adds blocking latency to every chart render on the loop shared with order handling. Note: fresh-read is intentional per the project's no-restart hot-reload principle — keep the fresh read but move it off the loop.
findings.fix: `data = await asyncio.to_thread(_load_chartshot_cfg, config_name)` (or subscribe to the ConfigService cache which is already hot-reloaded via PUT /config/system).

findings.title: Stale-candle guard fails open: parse errors swallowed by except-pass and empty timestamp skips the check entirely
findings.impact: A malformed or missing candle timestamp (e.g. after a DB/normalizer change) silently disables the only working market-freshness guard; orders get placed against stale or closed markets with no log entry.
findings.fix: Fail closed: raise RuntimeError("Cannot validate M5 candle freshness; order blocked.") when latest_ts is empty or unparsable, instead of `pass`.

findings.title: MT5 pending (LIMIT/STOP) orders are recorded as OPEN in the order book — mt5.place_order maps retcode DONE to status OPEN even for TRADE_ACTION_PENDING
findings.impact: On MT5, LIMIT/STOP orders are stored as OPEN with fill_price possibly 0/None. Exposure checks (get_open_positions vs order book), sync logic and P&L reporting treat an unfilled pending order as a live position; the sync loop may then 'close' it as SYNC_DETECTED because no broker position exists — phantom closed trades with wrong P&L in the history that trains future decisions.
findings.fix: In mt5.place_order return TradeStatus.PENDING when order.order_type != MARKET (mirroring OANDA); consumer mapping can stay.

findings.title: lots→units conversion truncates float product: int(lots * 100_000) loses units (e.g. 0.29 lots → 28999 units)
findings.impact: Orders and partial closes are consistently a unit short for many lot values (0.29, 0.58, 0.7...). On MT5 the volume re-round hides it, but OANDA receives the raw unit count; over weeks, position sizes and partial-close remainders drift from intent, and a partial close of '0.29 lots' leaves 1 unit open (position stays OPEN with 1 unit — dust positions accumulating margin and sync noise).
findings.fix: Use `int(round(lots * 100_000))` or `int((Decimal(str(lots_arg)) * 100_000).to_integral_value())` in both files (shared helper).

findings.title: Status filter applied AFTER the SQL LIMIT — 'closed'/'rejected' queries silently miss matching entries
findings.impact: With limit=20 and a busy book, asking for status_filter='rejected' returns only the rejected entries among the 20 newest rows — typically zero — even though rejected entries exist. Agents auditing recent rejections/closures get incomplete history and repeat mistakes.
findings.fix: Push the status filter into the repository query (add a status arg to get_order_book_entries) or over-fetch (e.g. limit*10) before filtering, then slice.

findings.title: trailing_stop_distance declared 'in pips' but sent to OANDA unconverted as a price distance
findings.impact: An agent following the schema passes e.g. 20 (pips); OANDA receives distance=20.0 price units — on EURUSD that is 200,000 pips, i.e. a trailing stop that never triggers (or is rejected). Positions believed to be trailing-protected run unprotected — rare, delayed losses.
findings.fix: Convert pips to price distance per pair (pip size 0.0001, 0.01 for JPY quotes) before building the OANDA order body, or change the schema/model to define the field as a price distance consistently.

findings.title: _broker_adapter_id implemented identically in 7 tool/module files plus an 8th twin _adapter_agent_id in the broker base
findings.impact: Any change to the adapter-ID scheme (padding width, suffix) must be applied in 8 places; missing one silently breaks direct bus delivery for that tool (messages dropped, 20-30s timeouts) — the exact silent-drop failure mode already present with ALL___.
findings.fix: Move one canonical `broker_adapter_id(broker_name, pair)` into openforexai/messaging/agent_id.py (next to AgentId) and import it everywhere; delete the 8 copies.

findings.title: Bridge mutual/self query deadlocks agents for the full 90s timeout — agents process messages serially and cannot answer AGENT_QUERY while blocked inside their own bridge call
findings.impact: Whenever two agents happen to query each other in the same window (rare, timing-dependent), both stall 90s; every candle trigger / order event queued in both inboxes during that window is processed 90s late, producing stale trading decisions. Self-targeting config burns 90s on every call. Random-seeming, non-crashing degradation.
findings.fix: Reject target_agent_id == context.agent_id up front; either process AGENT_QUERY concurrently in the agent (spawn a task) or propagate a call-chain marker in the AGENT_QUERY payload and fail fast on cycles; optionally answer queued AGENT_QUERYs from a side task while a cycle is running.

findings.title: system.json5 re-read and json5-parsed from disk on every tool call, plus calendar JSON re-loaded once per event id (O(n·m)) — all blocking the event loop
findings.impact: Each get_news call blocks the loop for the config parse plus N redundant calendar parses, stacking on top of the network stalls; all bus traffic (including order responses) is delayed during it.
findings.fix: Read broker offset/news config via ConfigService (in-memory) instead of re-parsing system.json5; load the calendar events ONCE per call and pass the loaded list (or use Mql5EconomicCalendar) into the markdown builder; offload remaining file IO with asyncio.to_thread.

findings.title: create_event_markdown and create_events_markdown duplicate the entire fetch/strip/markdownify pipeline verbatim
findings.impact: Any fix to the scraping logic (e.g., the body-fallback bug above) applied to one copy silently leaves the other broken — a classic source of 'fixed but still happening' defects.
findings.fix: Extract a single _fetch_event_markdown(event, url) helper used by both functions.

findings.title: Package import rewrites config/system.json5 from the in-memory config — persists env-substituted secrets in plaintext and bakes in the config.default.json5 merge
findings.impact: One package import irreversibly rewrites system.json5 with (1) plaintext secret values where `${API_KEY}`-style references used to be, and (2) the entire default config baked into the custom file — so future upgrades of config.default.json5 no longer take effect and rotating the env var no longer changes the running config. Silent config corruption that only surfaces much later.
findings.fix: Never write the runtime `_system_config` back to disk. Read the raw on-disk system.json5 (json5.loads of the file text, no env substitution, no default merge), apply the package delta to that raw dict, and write that. Keep updating the in-memory `_system_config` separately via load_json_config after the write.

findings.title: Monitoring subscriber queue leaked when agent run-lock acquisition times out; agent state also snapshotted before the lock is held
findings.impact: Each 'agent busy' 503 permanently leaks a monitoring subscriber queue; the monitoring bus keeps pushing every event into it (maxsize 4096) forever — growing memory and per-event fan-out cost over weeks of uptime. The pre-lock snapshot can restore a stale pair/profile onto a live trading agent after the inspection run.
findings.fix: Move the subscribe (and the previous-state capture) inside/after successful lock acquisition, or wrap everything from subscribe onward in try/finally that always unsubscribes; capture previous state only after the lock is held.

findings.title: Generic `except Exception` in _execute_agent_inspection swallows intended HTTPExceptions and re-raises them as 500
findings.impact: UI receives 500 'Execute failed' instead of the actionable 400/404 message; error logs fill with fake 'unexpected error' tracebacks, masking real failures during incident triage.
findings.fix: Add `except HTTPException: raise` before the generic `except Exception` handler.

findings.title: agent_tools hot-reload is unregister-then-register without rollback — a failed reload leaves the system with ZERO bridge tools while reporting 'saved'
findings.impact: One malformed agent_tools save strips every AgentBridgeTool from the live registry; agents whose strategies depend on bridge tools (e.g. asking a GA before ordering) silently lose those tools until the next successful save — degraded decisions with no crash.
findings.fix: Load and build the new tool set FIRST; only after successful construction unregister the old ones and register the new ones (single swap). On failure, keep the old set and return a non-2xx or at least status:'error'.

findings.title: PUT /config/system is non-transactional: disk is written before structural validation, and an exception mid runtime-apply leaves half-swapped state
findings.impact: A single bad save leaves: new config on disk, partially-applied runtime (e.g. old composer still running with new agent set, or a bus-registered zombie agent id that can never be restarted without a process restart). Trading continues in a mixed old/new configuration that matches neither file nor UI.
findings.fix: Validate the parsed structure before writing; wrap each start/stop in try/except that records per-entity errors and continues; unregister the bus member if Agent() init fails after register; always run the composer apply even if the agent apply had per-entity failures; return the error list in the response.

findings.title: Divergent twin session-filter implementations: console 'session_active' logic differs from the agent's live trading logic
findings.impact: For any filter with pre<0 or post>0 (and around holidays/weekends), the console shows session_active=false while the agent is actually trading (or vice versa). Operators trust the dashboard state and mis-diagnose why trades did/didn't happen; the two 'canonical' behaviors drift further with each edit.
findings.fix: Delete the reimplementation and expose Agent._is_session_allowed's logic as a shared pure function (module-level, parameterized by timestamp and offset) consumed by both agent.py and api.py.

findings.title: Order reconcile logic duplicated between api.py and the broker sync loop, with divergent stored field shapes
findings.impact: Two code paths write the same DB rows with different value shapes and different field coverage (close_reason present on one path, absent on the other) — downstream consumers reading close_reason see NULL for API-reconciled closes; behavioral fixes to one copy don't reach the other (as proven by the OrderStatus import bug living only in the api.py copy).
findings.fix: Extract one shared reconcile/close-updates builder (e.g. in a repository-level service) used by both the sync loop and the management API; delete the api.py reimplementation.

findings.title: /ws/monitoring is completely unauthenticated even when MANAGEMENT_API_KEY is set
findings.impact: Anyone who can reach the port streams the full live trading telemetry (strategies, prompts, positions, broker names) bypassing the API-key protection the operator configured.
findings.fix: In ws_monitoring, before accept(), compare `websocket.headers.get("x-api-key")` or a `?token=` query param against _EXPECTED_KEY and close with 4401/policy-violation on mismatch.

findings.title: GET /orderbook applies the status filter AFTER the per-broker row limit — open positions older than the newest `limit` rows silently disappear
findings.impact: With active trading, a still-OPEN position requested more than `limit` (default 200) entries ago is not in the fetched window, so `status_filter=open` omits it. The operator's open-positions view (and any tooling built on it) is silently incomplete — a live position with real P&L exposure becomes invisible in the UI after a few days of trading, matching the 'random loss discovered weeks later' symptom.
findings.fix: Push the status filter into the SQL query (add a status/status-group parameter to get_order_book_entries) so the LIMIT applies after filtering, or fetch open entries with a dedicated unbounded query.

findings.title: GET /events clamps limit only from above — negative limit becomes SQLite `LIMIT -1` (unbounded) and dumps the whole event log on the event loop
findings.impact: `GET /events?limit=-1` returns and decompresses the entire persistent event log in one synchronous call on the trading event loop — multi-second to multi-minute stall of all agents/order handling plus a huge response. Can be triggered accidentally by a UI bug or intentionally by anyone with (or without, in default no-key mode) API access.
findings.fix: Use `limit=max(1, min(limit, 1000))` and `offset=max(0, offset)`, and wrap `read_events`/`read_event`/`read_trace` calls in `asyncio.to_thread(...)`.

findings.title: Event-log created_at is persisted in the hot-reloadable ui_utc offset — changing ui_utc corrupts ordering and time-range filtering of the persistent log
findings.impact: The moment the operator changes ui_utc via the config editor (a documented hot-reload path per CLAUDE.md), new rows carry a different offset suffix. ISO strings with mixed offsets do not compare lexicographically by instant: '2026-07-05T10:00:00+03:00' sorts after '2026-07-05T08:30:00+01:00' although it is earlier. Newest-first ordering, from_time/to_time filters and trace ordering silently return wrong/missing events for all history spanning the change — permanently, since old rows are never rewritten.
findings.fix: Always persist created_at in UTC (fixed offset) in event_log.py and apply ui_utc only at presentation time (UI already receives the offset from /system/ui-settings). Remove `_apply_event_log_tz`'s influence on storage.

findings.title: RCE-grade endpoints (exec of client scripts, writing executable snapshot_helpers.py, PUT docs) behind an API key that defaults to disabled
findings.impact: Any process that can reach the management port on an unconfigured deployment gets arbitrary code execution in the process that holds live broker credentials — it can place/close real trades or exfiltrate keys. CORS restricts browsers, not direct clients.
findings.fix: Refuse to start (or bind only to 127.0.0.1 and log a prominent warning) when MANAGEMENT_API_KEY is unset; use secrets.compare_digest for the key check; consider gating exec/helper-write endpoints behind an additional explicit dev flag.

findings.title: Package import writes agent_tools.json5 but never reloads AgentBridgeTools — unlike the direct save route
findings.impact: After importing a package containing bridge tools, agents referencing the new tools get 'Tool not registered' failures (or keep using stale bridge definitions) until someone happens to re-save agent_tools via the other endpoint or restarts — violating the hot-reload contract and breaking imported agents silently.
findings.fix: Extract the bridge-tool reload block from save_config_file into a helper and call it from import_agent_package when req.import_bridge_tools is true, reporting errors in the response.

findings.title: _resolve_file_refs inlines ANY project-root file — including secret-bearing configs — verbatim into prompts sent to an external LLM, with unbounded size
findings.impact: Broker/LLM credentials exfiltrated to a third-party LLM API (defeating _deep_mask everywhere else), and a single large file reference stalls the entire trading event loop for seconds while read_text runs.
findings.fix: Restrict refs to an allowlisted directory (e.g. config/llm_contexts/ plus docs), or at minimum exclude config/modules/**, .env and any file matching secret patterns; enforce a max bytes limit per resolved file; use asyncio.to_thread for the read.

findings.title: POST /composers/{ec_id}/execute runs the EC script with LIVE bus/tools, concurrently with real triggered runs, bypassing the run lock
findings.impact: A UI 'test' click executes the composer against the live broker and injects real composed events that downstream agents act on (potential real orders), and it can interleave with a concurrent live _run_cycle holding the lock — two simultaneous executions of the same EC mutating shared monitoring/DB state and double-emitting events.
findings.fix: Acquire ec._run_lock in test_run (or in the endpoint) to serialize with live cycles, and/or run test executions in a dry-run ToolContext whose emit()/publish are captured instead of delivered.

findings.title: Package export builds from the env-substituted in-memory config with no masking — 'portable' package can carry live credentials
findings.impact: The docstring calls this a 'portable multi-agent package' meant to be shared/imported elsewhere; sharing it leaks resolved database credentials (and any other substituted secret reachable through the exported sections).
findings.fix: Export from the raw on-disk system.json5 (unsubstituted) or run _deep_mask/strip ${VAR}-derived values over the exported system_config section before returning.

findings.title: /kb router bypasses the X-API-Key authentication that every other management route enforces
findings.impact: Any process/browser page that can reach the management port can read, modify and delete the entire personal knowledge base without credentials. Default bind is 127.0.0.1, but host is constructor-configurable (server.py:55) — binding to a LAN address exposes the KB unauthenticated. Also inconsistent with the security model of every sibling route.
findings.fix: Create the router with the same auth dependency: `router = APIRouter(prefix="/kb", tags=["knowledge-base"], dependencies=[Depends(_check_api_key)])` (import _check_api_key or inject it at include_router time via `app.include_router(kb_router, dependencies=[Depends(_check_api_key)])`).

findings.title: validate_package ignores the import_* section flags that apply_import_package honors — validation and application diverge in both directions
findings.impact: (1) An agent goes live referencing a nonexistent snapshot profile — snapshot construction fails or degrades at decision time, discovered only when the agent behaves oddly in production. (2) Legitimate partial imports (profiles only) are impossible when the package's agents section has local-environment mismatches.
findings.fix: Pass the same import_* flags into validate_package; skip validation of excluded sections, and only include package-side profiles in combined_snapshot_profiles / combined_decision_profiles when the corresponding import flag is true.

findings.title: AGENT_ID_RE is a weaker duplicate of AgentId._ID_RE — validate_package accepts target IDs the runtime cannot parse
findings.impact: An imported agent with such an ID is written into system.json5, but RoutingRule.matches_sender (routing.py:84-87) returns False for unparseable IDs on any non-'*' from-pattern, and every pattern-based to-target skips it — the agent is silently excluded from pattern routing. Weeks later: 'why does this agent never fire?'.
findings.fix: Delete AGENT_ID_RE and validate with `AgentId.try_parse(target_agent_id) is not None` (single source of truth).

findings.title: PUT /kb/documents filters out None values, making 'move to root' (parent_id=null) silently impossible
findings.impact: User clicks 'Verschieben nach... Root' — nothing happens, no error. Document is stuck in its folder forever; combined with the orphaning bug this makes documents unrecoverable via the UI. Same mechanism makes it impossible to ever null any nullable field.
findings.fix: Use body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True) and drop the `if v is not None` filter (or keep it only for fields where null is not a valid value). parent_id=None must reach kb_update_document.

findings.title: Configured agent_trigger_delay_seconds is parsed, validated and logged but never passed to start_background_tasks — broker always uses hardcoded default 60s
findings.impact: Operator sets e.g. agent_trigger_delay_seconds: 5 in the broker module config to trigger agents promptly after M5 candle close; startup log even confirms the value, but agents are actually triggered 60s late on every candle for weeks. Entries/exits execute on ~1-minute-stale prices — exactly the class of random-looking slippage/loss that never crashes.
findings.fix: Add `agent_trigger_delay_seconds=task_cfg.get("agent_trigger_delay_seconds", 60),` to the start_background_tasks call in bootstrap.py.

findings.title: adapters.data package is never imported at runtime — SQLiteDataContainer (WAL mode, synchronous=FULL, agent-memory methods) is dead; its docstring falsely claims "Imported by bootstrap.py"
findings.impact: Crash-safety configuration the code visibly intends (WAL, synchronous=FULL) is silently absent in production; a power loss/crash can lose or corrupt the last committed order-book writes in default rollback-journal mode. The whole agent-memory feature is dead weight, and a latent key-collision timebomb exists if the package ever gets imported.
findings.fix: Either import openforexai.adapters.data in bootstrap and use the DataContainer classes, or delete the adapters/data package and its registrations. Separate the repository and data-container registries (or drop one API entirely).

findings.title: Pause is an advisory poll-based flag checked only at trigger time — in-flight agent cycles and the broker order-execution path are not gated, so orders still execute after pause()
findings.impact: Operator hits Pause during a market event; an agent cycle already running (LLM tool loop can take minutes) completes and publishes ORDER_REQUEST, which the broker executes normally. Real trades occur while the UI reports 'paused' — untraceable losses attributed to randomness. TOCTOU: is_paused() checked, then long await, then trade.
findings.fix: Gate the execution path, not just the trigger path: check runtime_control.is_paused() in brokers/base._handle_order_request (reject or queue the order and publish a monitoring event), and/or re-check pause immediately before an agent publishes ORDER_REQUEST. Consider replacing the polled bool with an asyncio.Event for wakeup and a documented contract of what pause guarantees.

findings.title: load_json_config docstring promises "Keys starting with `_` are stripped from the result" — no such stripping is implemented anywhere in the loader
findings.impact: A user who 'comments out' an agent by renaming it to "_OXS_T-EURUSD-AA-..." (relying on the documented behavior) still gets it bootstrapped: bootstrap.py:69-73 iterates ALL keys of system_config["agents"] and the underscore key passes `cfg.get("enable", True)`. A supposedly-disabled agent trades live money. Underscore comment keys also leak into merged config, API responses and agent config payloads.
findings.fix: Either implement recursive underscore-key stripping in _process()/_load_single() to match the docstring, or delete the docstring claim and rely solely on the `enable` flag.

findings.title: sync_confirmed is a legacy flag that mirrors confirmed_by_broker at every single write site — pure duplicate field persisted in both DB schemas
findings.impact: Redundant state that can silently diverge the moment one future writer updates only one flag — any consumer reading the stale twin then makes decisions on wrong confirmation state. Owner wants all compat shims removed.
findings.fix: Delete sync_confirmed from the model, all write sites, and both DB schemas (drop column / stop selecting); keep confirmed_by_broker as the single source of truth.

findings.title: close_reason is a free-form str in TradeResult but a strict CloseReason enum in OrderBookEntry — same concept, two types, and the DB fallback path can crash model validation
findings.impact: If any writer ever stores a raw broker string (as TradeResult already does elsewhere) or a legacy value in order_book_entries.close_reason, every subsequent read of that row raises ValidationError — order book listing/sync for that trade breaks permanently until manual DB surgery.
findings.fix: Use CloseReason for TradeResult too (put raw broker detail in a separate broker_detail field), and delete the dead str-fallback branches in both DB adapters (or widen OrderBookEntry.close_reason to CloseReason | str if legacy rows must load).

findings.title: CloseReason.SL_HIT, TP_HIT, TRAILING_STOP and BROKER_CLOSED are never produced — all broker-side closes are recorded as SYNC_DETECTED
findings.impact: Every stop-loss hit, take-profit hit, trailing-stop hit and margin-call close lands in the order book as SYNC_DETECTED. The OptimizationAgent (per OrderBookEntry docstring, trade.py:120-127, this record is its primary input) cannot distinguish winning TP exits from losing SL exits by reason, degrading pattern detection and prompt optimization — a slow, invisible feedback-loop corruption.
findings.fix: In the sync/close-detection path (brokers/base.py around 1178-1228), map the broker's raw close reason (OANDA state/reason fields, MT5 deal reason DEAL_REASON_SL/DEAL_REASON_TP) onto SL_HIT/TP_HIT/TRAILING_STOP/BROKER_CLOSED instead of blanket SYNC_DETECTED; otherwise delete the unused members.

findings.title: prompt_version is never populated anywhere — always None end-to-end — and its type diverges (int in models, str in data-container ports)
findings.impact: The documented purpose of OrderBookEntry ('primary input for the OptimizationAgent', trade.py:125-127) is silently defeated: trades can never be attributed to the prompt version that generated them, so prompt A/B evaluation and BacktestResult.vs_baseline comparisons run on unattributable data.
findings.fix: Thread the active PromptCandidate.version into TradeSignal at signal creation (agents/agent.py signal path), and unify the type to int | None across ports/data_container.py and adapters/data/*.

findings.title: Scraper falls back to soup.body with no content validation — bot-block/consent/error pages are silently delivered to the trading LLM as 'news'
findings.impact: GetNewsTool returns garbage markdown (nav remnants, challenge text, or an unrelated page) which the decision-making LLM treats as economic news context. The agent then reasons about non-existent or wrong fundamentals — silent wrong-data influence on trade decisions, surfacing only as unexplained bad trades weeks later.
findings.fix: Only accept `eventContentPanel` (the actual calendar container); if it is absent, raise RuntimeError instead of degrading to main/article/body. Optionally validate the markdown contains the event name before returning.

findings.title: Request/response-future bus pattern hand-rolled in 8 places with diverging cleanup semantics
findings.impact: The copies that skip the finally-cleanup (llm_helpers, api.py) leak entries in EventBus._pending_futures whenever publish() raises (e.g. schema validation error) or the awaiting task is cancelled — unbounded dict growth over weeks of live trading; behavioral drift between copies (asyncio.shield vs not) makes timeout handling inconsistent.
findings.fix: Expose one `await bus.request(msg, timeout)` on EventBus (register/publish/wait/cancel in one place) and delete the 7 re-implementations.

findings.title: Pip-size heuristic `0.01 if sample_price > 20 else 0.0001` duplicated in EMASlope and SMASlope, diverging from the unused canonical pip table
findings.impact: SLOPE_E/SLOPE_S values are off by 100x for high-quote non-JPY instruments, feeding wrong trend-strength numbers to the LLM; two copies guarantee future drift.
findings.fix: Pass the pair into the plugins (calculate_indicator knows context.pair) and use normalizer.pip_size(); delete both heuristic blocks.

findings.title: system.json5 read raw with json5.loads in 3 places, bypassing load_json_config — no env-var substitution, no config.default.json5 merge, re-read from disk per call
findings.impact: Any chartshot/news setting placed in config.default.json5 or written as ${ENV_VAR} is invisible to these code paths while visible everywhere else — divergent effective config depending on which module reads it; plus blocking disk IO on the event loop per request.
findings.fix: Route all three through load_json_config (or better, through the running ConfigService which already caches system config in memory).

findings.title: data/normalizer.py (pip_size/pips/price_from_pips/normalize_price) is imported by nothing — the canonical pip table sits unused while a heuristic duplicates it
findings.impact: The single correct home for pip math is dead; live code uses heuristics that are wrong for exotic pairs.
findings.fix: Either wire pip_size() into indicator_plugins/spread normalization (preferred) or delete the module.

findings.title: Dual repository/data-container registry API kept for backward compat — and the 'backward compat' method is the one production actually uses
findings.impact: Two names for one dict confuse which storage abstraction is live; the 'preferred' data-container API has zero production callers.
findings.fix: Keep exactly one pair (register_repository/get_repository since that is what runs); delete register_data_container/get_data_container/list_data_containers, the alias, and the compat registrations.

findings.title: Supervisor approval publishes SIGNAL_GENERATED without schema-required "direction" and no component ever publishes SIGNAL_APPROVED/REJECTED — supervisor mode can never approve
findings.impact: Any tool configured with approval_mode "supervisor" either crashes the whole agent cycle (ValueError) or, if the schema were relaxed, silently rejects every trade after a 15 s stall. Dormant until someone enables the documented supervisor gate — then trading stops with no clear cause.
findings.fix: Hoist "direction" (from arguments) to the top-level payload or drop the schema requirement; implement or remove the SIGNAL_APPROVED/REJECTED responder; move _check_approval inside the try so approval failures become ToolResults instead of cycle crashes.

findings.title: history_deals_get date range built from datetime.now(UTC) while MT5 deal times are broker-server wall clock — recent closes inside the offset window are missed
findings.impact: find_closed_trade_by_sync_key and the position-id fallback in get_closed_trade_result return None for trades closed within the last ~3 h; _resolve_orphaned_entry (base.py:1236) then marks genuinely FILLED-and-closed orphan entries as REJECTED, and sync closes lose pnl/close_price. Self-heals only if a later sync re-queries after the offset elapses — but the entry status was already finalized. Verify against the specific MT5 build's datetime handling.
findings.fix: Shift the range by the configured broker offset (e.g. `date_to = datetime.now(self._broker_tz).replace(tzinfo=UTC)`) mirroring _broker_timestamp's inverse transform.

findings.title: Auto-derived SL/TP are sent to brokers as raw unrounded floats — normalize_price exists but is never used anywhere
findings.impact: Brokers that enforce price precision reject such orders (OANDA PRICE_PRECISION_EXCEEDED, MT5 invalid stops on some servers) — sporadic, symbol-dependent rejections of otherwise valid signals, i.e. randomly missed trades in live use.
findings.fix: Round derived SL/TP with normalize_price(pair) (and quantize entry/limit/stop prices) before building the TradeSignal.

findings.title: Entire openforexai/adapters/data package (SQLiteDataContainer/PostgreSQLDataContainer) is never imported at runtime — WAL mode and the whole agent-memory persistence API are dead
findings.impact: Documented features (LLM conversation resume after restart, performance snapshots, crash-safe WAL journaling) silently do not exist in production. Also a latent hazard: if anyone ever imports openforexai.adapters.data, its register_repository("sqlite", SQLiteDataContainer) would silently swap the production DB class depending on import order.
findings.fix: Decide: either wire it in (import openforexai.adapters.data in bootstrap AFTER adapters.database, use get_data_container, and actually call the agent-memory methods) or delete adapters/data/, ports/data_container.py, the agent_conversations/agent_performance parts of migrations/003, and the duplicate registration. Remove the register_repository back-compat aliases either way.

findings.title: decision_type_new dual-column shim: both columns always written with identical value, reads use COALESCE(decision_type_new, decision_type) — owner wants this removed
findings.impact: Every agent_decisions read/write carries the dual-column logic; any future writer that fills only one column produces rows that filter differently in get_analysis_records (COALESCE) vs UI expectations — shape drift on the decision-history path feeding get_last_decision tool and the Analysis view.
findings.fix: Removal plan: (1) new migration 009: `UPDATE agent_decisions SET decision_type = COALESCE(decision_type_new, decision_type);` then drop column decision_type_new (SQLite: table rebuild or ALTER DROP COLUMN on 3.35+). (2) Simplify INSERTs in database/sqlite.py:244-268 and database/postgresql.py:272-308 to write decision_type only. (3) Replace COALESCE clauses at sqlite.py:294/317/344 and postgresql.py:340/368/397 with plain decision_type. (4) Delete the dead adapters/data writers (see dead-code finding). (5) PG _ensure_core_tables needs no decision_type_new after this.

findings.title: Deprecated '@handlers' routing target still defaulted/validated in UI and half-supported in routing.py although the bus explicitly removed it — new rules silently do nothing
findings.impact: A user who saves a rule with the UI default target creates a rule that matches events (suppressing the unmatched-event monitoring warning) but delivers to no one — events like m5_candle_trigger vanish without any UNMATCHED_EVENT alert. Weeks-later 'agent stopped reacting' class of defect.
findings.fix: Remove '@handlers' everywhere: EMPTY_RULE default to '' with required validation, drop it from looksLikeAgentExpr and help text; delete routing.py:37-40 docstring section and the :109-110 branch; make resolve() treat '@handlers' as a config error (matched_any stays false or emit explicit monitoring error); update config/README.md:138, AGENTS.md:180, docs/openforexai.messaging.en.md:128.

findings.title: Twin implementations of _row_to_analysis_record diverge: PostgreSQL returns 'setup_type', SQLite does not
findings.impact: GET /analysis records expose setup_type only when running on PostgreSQL; UI/consumers coded against one backend silently lose the field on the other. Duplicate logic guarantees further drift.
findings.fix: Add setup_type to the SQLite version (or remove from PG) and extract the shared row→record mapping into one helper used by both adapters.

findings.title: Legacy candle_requests fallback synthesizes six default tool blocks for profiles without tool_blocks
findings.impact: Owner wants all compat shims removed. Additionally: opening a legacy profile and hitting Update writes six invented tool blocks (with hardcoded EMA20/50, RSI7, ATR7 on H1) into the live profile — the snapshot content changes without the user configuring anything.
findings.fix: Delete buildLegacySnapshotToolBlocks; migrate any remaining candle_requests profiles in system.json5 once; treat missing tool_blocks as an empty list plus a validation error.

findings.title: GET /monitoring/pinned returns raw model_dump keys (source_module/broker_name) while every other monitoring path serializes to source/broker — UI PinnedMonitoringEvent type is wrong at runtime
findings.impact: `pe.source` is always undefined for pinned events: the agent badge in the Pinned Events panel never renders, source-based display in the detail dialog shows nothing, and any future filtering on pinned .source/.broker silently matches nothing. Auto-pinned error events (llm_error, broker_error, …) lose their agent attribution exactly where the user looks for failure causes.
findings.fix: Serialize pinned events through _serialize_monitoring_event (plus auto_pinned flag) in the /monitoring/pinned handler, or have pinned_events() emit the source/broker key names used everywhere else.

findings.title: /kb/* router is mounted without the X-API-Key auth dependency applied to all other REST routes
findings.impact: When MANAGEMENT_API_KEY is set, every management endpoint requires the key except the knowledge base: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /kb/documents are fully unauthenticated — anyone who can reach the port can read, modify and delete all handbook documents (which may contain strategy notes).
findings.fix: Create the kb router with `APIRouter(prefix="/kb", dependencies=[Depends(_check_api_key)])` (import _check_api_key from api or move it to a shared module).

findings.title: calculateIndicator ignores ToolExecuteResponse.is_error and casts the error payload to the indicator result shape — indicator failures render as silently-empty overlays
findings.impact: When the indicator tool fails (broker disconnected, bad period, no candles), the chart simply shows no EMA/RSI/ATR lines with zero error indication. A trader manually validating a setup against the same indicators the agents use sees a clean chart and draws wrong conclusions; the failure is indistinguishable from 'no data'.
findings.fix: In calculateIndicator, check `r.is_error` (and that `r.result.values` is an array) and throw with the embedded error message so the existing .catch handlers can surface it (set an error state instead of silently clearing values).

findings.title: GET /events and /events/{id}/trace run synchronous sqlite queries directly on the trading event loop
findings.impact: Opening the Event Log view or expanding a trace on a database that has accumulated weeks of events (LIKE-scans over every row, repeated per frontier level) blocks the shared asyncio loop for the full query duration — candle dispatch, agent cycles and order handling all stall. Intermittent trading latency correlated with UI usage.
findings.fix: Wrap the reads like the writes: `await asyncio.to_thread(read_events, ...)` / `await asyncio.to_thread(read_trace, event_id)`; longer-term index descendant lookup instead of chain LIKE scans.

findings.title: When a tool's schema is unavailable, typed forced_arguments are silently re-persisted as strings (boolean "false" becomes truthy in Python)
findings.impact: Most tools int()-coerce (e.g. get_candles.py L50) so numbers survive, but a boolean forced argument persisted as the string "false" is truthy for any Python `if arguments.get(...)` check — a forced safety flag meant to be off is treated as on. Also objects become JSON strings. Triggered whenever the wizard is saved while a tool is temporarily unregistered/disabled.
findings.fix: If the tool schema is unavailable, keep the original raw value from row.raw instead of the stringified form value; or refuse to save forced_arguments for tools whose schema cannot be resolved.

findings.title: Ctrl+S saves stale mount-time content — user edits to snapshot_helpers.py are silently discarded while UI reports 'Saved'
findings.impact: User edits a snapshot helper function (which feeds every snapshot transform used in trading decisions), presses Ctrl+S, sees 'Saved. Python syntax valid.' — but the OLD file content was rewritten. The buggy/old helper keeps producing snapshot data for live decisions; the edit only takes effect if the user later happens to click the toolbar Save button.
findings.fix: In the Ctrl+S command callback read the current model value: `const current = editor.getValue()` and save that (or keep a ref: `const textRef = useRef(text); textRef.current = text` and have handleSave read textRef.current).

findings.title: formToRaw rebuilds the EC config from scratch — tool_config.forced_arguments and any other unknown fields are dropped on save
findings.impact: An EC with hand-configured tool_config.forced_arguments (e.g. forcing a pair or units cap on a trading tool) loses them the moment the EC is saved in the wizard. The EC's tool calls then run without the forced constraints — silently different behavior on a money path.
findings.fix: Keep the original raw per EC row (it is already stored in ECRow.raw but unused) and serialize as `{ ...raw, ...formFields, tool_config: { ...(raw.tool_config ?? {}), allowed_tools, max_tool_turns, script_timeout_seconds } }`, mirroring AgentConfigWizard.serializeAgent.

findings.title: persist() rewrites ALL bridge tools through the form model — legacy target_agent_ids entries are converted to targets[] with empty tool_name, changing the generated tool names
findings.impact: After saving ANY bridge tool, previously registered tool names of legacy multi-target tools change. Agents whose allowed_tools / prompts reference the old generated names (ask_x_1) silently lose that tool — inter-agent queries stop working with no error at save time.
findings.fix: Persist only the edited/added/deleted entry and keep the raw JSON of untouched entries verbatim; validate all rows before save.

findings.title: Bridge tool normalizer carries three layers of legacy field aliases (tool_name|name|alias, target_agent_id|agent_id, targets|target_agent_ids)
findings.impact: Owner explicitly wants all backward-compat paths removed. Dual-field reads let divergent configs exist (two spellings of the same concept), which is the root enabler of the tool-rename defect above.
findings.fix: Migrate config/RunTime/agent_tools.json5 to the canonical shape (targets[] with tool_name/description/target_agent_id) once, then delete the alias fallbacks in both BridgeToolsEditor.tsx and openforexai/tools/system/agent_bridge.py.

findings.title: Renaming a snapshot/decision-prompt profile deletes the old key without updating agents that reference it — agents silently lose their snapshot
findings.impact: After a rename, every agent still pointing at the old profile name receives a config WITHOUT snapshot_profile_config on its next reload: it keeps trading but its decision input loses the entire prepared market snapshot. No crash, no warning — decisions quietly degrade until someone notices losses.
findings.fix: On rename, rewrite all agents[*].snapshot_profile / decision_prompt_profile and decision_prompt_profiles[*].fallback_snapshot_profile references in the same payload, or block the rename while references exist (the wizard already knows cfg.agents).

findings.title: Four divergent timezone models across UI views — same event timestamp renders as different wall-clock times depending on which view shows it
findings.impact: When investigating a losing trade, the operator sees the same event at three different clock times: Monitor stream shows ui_utc-shifted time, Event Log shows stripped wall-clock, Trace viewer shows browser-local time, and the header 'Last:' uses a fourth (localStorage) offset. Cross-referencing broker fills with agent decisions gives hour-scale misattribution — exactly the class of 'random-seeming' loss the owner reports when trades are audited against the wrong candle/session.
findings.fix: Route every timestamp render through utils/time.ts formatters; delete the private formatTs in EventLogView/TraceViewer and the Header-local offset store; decide ONE storage semantic (offset-carrying ISO strings) and document it in one place.

findings.title: Saved-monitor-filter change rewrites the entire system.json5 via unserialized async read-modify-write with no error handling
findings.impact: system.json5 is the master trading config (agent enable flags, prompts, broker/LLM wiring). A UI filter save racing a concurrent agent-config save silently reverts the other change — e.g. an agent the operator just disabled becomes re-enabled by the stale overwrite and keeps trading. Save failures are also swallowed (unhandled rejection), so the UI claims the filter is saved when it is not.
findings.fix: Serialize saves (queue/mutex), send a targeted PATCH endpoint that only updates system.ui.monitor.saved_filters server-side instead of round-tripping the whole config, and surface save errors in the UI.

findings.title: Auto-Write applies multiple LLM patches against the same stale source — only the last patch survives and line numbers are wrong
findings.impact: An LLM response containing two patches (e.g. 'fix guard on L12-L18 and add logging after L40') silently drops the first patch when Auto-Write is on. The user believes both edits landed in the EC/snapshot script; the saved script is missing one change — a hard-to-detect corruption of the trading-logic scripts that only shows up later as wrong behavior.
findings.fix: Accumulate: `let src = codeRef.current; for (...) { const r = applyPatch(src, block); if (r.error) { surface it; break } src = r.result } onApplyCode(src)`. Also apply patches bottom-up or recompute offsets so earlier edits don't shift later line numbers.

findings.title: Leftover debug POST to /debug/log fires on every overlay-effect run, and unmemoized overlayLines/oscillators props make that effect run on every parent render
findings.impact: During live monitoring with EMA enabled, every UI interaction spams 2 POSTs and re-feeds the whole line series — network/CPU churn in the browser and log-file growth on the backend, degrading the monitoring UI precisely during busy trading periods. It is also debugging leftover the owner wants removed.
findings.fix: Delete the fetch('/debug/log') block; wrap overlayLines/oscillators in useMemo in Orderbook.tsx and AgentChat.tsx (ChartAnalysis already memoizes).

findings.title: captureImageForPrint 'restores' a dark theme the chart never had — printing permanently flips the on-screen chart from light to dark
findings.impact: After using Print in Orderbook or ChartAnalysis, the live chart switches to dark background/grid and stays that way until remount — visible state corruption; also indicates the restore constants will silently diverge again on the next theme change.
findings.fix: Capture the current options before applying the print theme (`const prev = chart.options().layout/grid`) and restore exactly those, or keep the theme constants in one shared object used by both createChart and the restore call.

findings.title: Event log re-fetches on every filter keystroke with no debounce and no out-of-order guard — stale responses can overwrite newer results
findings.impact: While auditing a loss, typing 'order_result' fires 12 queries; if the response for 'order_r' arrives last, the table silently shows results for the wrong filter — the operator concludes events are missing. Also concurrent 'Load more' (load(offset)) racing an auto-reload can duplicate or misorder rows.
findings.fix: Trigger load only from the Search button / Enter (drop filter states from the auto-fetch path or debounce), and guard with a request sequence number or AbortController so only the latest response is applied.

findings.title: All indicator-math functions in utils/indicators.ts are unused — only TF_MINUTES is ever imported
findings.impact: A second, client-side implementation of EMA/RSI/ATR that can silently diverge from the backend's authoritative math; if a future dev wires it up 'because it exists', chart indicators would disagree with the values agents trade on.
findings.fix: Delete resampleCandles, warmupCount, calcSma, calcEma, calcRsi, calcAtr; keep only TF_MINUTES (or move it to a constants module).

findings.title: Grouped-row computation is O(n²) with per-comparison Date parsing, recomputed unmemoized on every render of the live stream
findings.impact: With a full 500-event buffer this is ~250k payload lookups plus thousands of Date allocations per incoming event — the Monitor tab becomes visibly laggy exactly during event storms (order placement bursts), when the operator most needs it responsive.
findings.fix: Wrap the grouping in useMemo keyed on [visible, expandedParents], reuse the childrenByParent map from buildGroupedRows instead of re-filtering, and precompute epoch ms once per event for sorting.

findings.title: CopyButton component copy-pasted five times
findings.impact: Any fix (e.g. clipboard-permission error surfacing) must be repeated 5 times; versions already differ slightly in icon size, guaranteeing drift.
findings.fix: Extract a single components/common/CopyButton.tsx and import it everywhere.

findings.title: Analysis-marker construction (primary_bias regex, U/D/N label, confidence %, nearest-candle lookup) implemented three times with diverging behavior
findings.impact: The same analysis renders at different candles and with different visual semantics per view; a bias-regex fix (e.g. new BIAS_* values) applied in one place leaves the other two silently misclassifying analyses as neutral.
findings.fix: Extract shared helpers (parseBias(record), buildAnalysisMarkers(records, candles, tf)) and one AnalysisModal component; cite all three views as consumers.

findings.title: Sync reconciliation logic duplicated in _sync_loop and trigger_sync with a real divergence: trigger_sync's matched-entry update omits stop_loss/take_profit refresh
findings.impact: When an agent runs the trigger_sync tool after the broker (or another party) moved SL/TP, the local order book keeps stale SL/TP levels; agents then reason about protection levels that no longer exist — a classic rare, weeks-later financial-loss defect. Any future fix applied to one copy will silently miss the other.
findings.fix: Extract one shared `_reconcile_positions(pair, event_bus) -> list[dict]` used by both the loop and trigger_sync; include SL/TP in the matched-entry update.

findings.title: M5 candle-trigger pipeline tests broken (EventBus.subscribe removed) and enshrine an outdated payload type: they assert trigger candle close as string "1.1018" while production now publishes floats
findings.impact: The only tests covering the candle-update/trigger publishing contract (which every analysis agent consumes) do not run; and if naively 'fixed' by restoring subscribe they would then fail on (or worse, get inverted to hide) the string-vs-float payload change.
findings.fix: Port the tests to register_member/flush; update assertions to the current trigger payload types (float OHLC, string OHLC on M5_CANDLE_UPDATE) — or better, fix the production inconsistency first (see separate finding) and assert one canonical type.

findings.title: test_info_monitoring_keeps_m5_candle_queued_events_visible asserts behavior production explicitly removed — M5_CANDLE_QUEUED is now in _INFO_SUPPRESSED_EVENT_TYPES
findings.impact: Either the suppression is an unintended production regression (operators lose candle-queue visibility at INFO) or the test is stale — the contradiction is unresolved and the red test trains developers to ignore suite failures.
findings.fix: Decide the intended behavior: if suppression is intended, rewrite the test to assert suppression at INFO and visibility at DEBUG; if not, remove M5_CANDLE_QUEUED from _INFO_SUPPRESSED_EVENT_TYPES.

findings.title: Both tests call removed API ConfigService.resolve_runtime_tool_config — agent tool-policy resolution (which tools an agent may call, incl. auto_place_order/close_position) has zero coverage
findings.impact: A regression in tool-policy resolution could grant an analysis agent order-placement tools (or strip a trading agent of close_position) with no test tripping — direct trading-safety impact.
findings.fix: Find the successor API (likely on ConfigService or the tools config loader) and rewrite the two tests against it; also reconsider asserting exact live-config tool lists (they break on every legitimate config edit) in favor of testing the resolution mechanism with fixture configs.

findings.title: Azure LLM tests construct the provider via __new__ + manual private-attribute stuffing; production added _reasoning_effort and both tests now crash — the pattern guarantees breakage on any new field and bypasses from_config validation
findings.impact: Transcript logging and HTTP-attempt debug diagnostics (the primary forensic tools for diagnosing bad LLM trade decisions) are untested; additionally the __new__ pattern means these tests validate a hand-built object, not the real from_config construction path, so config-parsing bugs pass unseen.
findings.fix: Build the provider through from_config with a stub AsyncAzureOpenAI (as test_azure_llm_config.py already does) and inject only the fake client; set _reasoning_effort via config.

findings.title: Migration runner has no tracking table and no error tolerance: unguarded ALTER TABLE in 003/008 makes any second run (or first run against an app-initialized DB) crash, so later migrations can never be applied
findings.impact: Adding migration 009 later and running db_migrate.py against the production DB crashes at 003 with a traceback; the new migration is never applied. Partial statements before the failing ALTER are already committed (executescript autocommits), leaving untracked half-applied files.
findings.fix: Create a schema_migrations(filename PRIMARY KEY, applied_at) table, skip already-applied files, and record each file after success; alternatively wrap per-statement execution and tolerate 'duplicate column name' for ALTER statements as 003's header expects.

findings.title: sqlite_path and --config resolved against CWD, not repo root — running from any other directory silently creates and migrates a brand-new empty database
findings.impact: Invoked from anywhere but the repo root (cron job, different shell dir), the script reports '[migrate] Migrations applied' successfully — against a freshly created empty DB in the wrong location. The production DB stays unmigrated with zero indication of failure.
findings.fix: Resolve both the config path and a relative sqlite_path against ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent, exactly as the backfill scripts do.

findings.title: When no exit deal is found, falls back to the last deal — which can be the ENTRY deal — writing pnl=0, entry price and entry time as close results
findings.impact: A CLOSED order book entry gets pnl_account_currency=0, close_price=entry price and closed_at=opened_at permanently written; because the fields are then non-NULL, _needs_backfill never revisits it. Real losing/winning trades silently recorded as break-even — accumulating P&L distortion.
findings.fix: If no deal with entry in {1,3} exists, return None instead of guessing (skip the entry so a later run with full history can fill it). Same fix needed in mt5.py:538-539.

findings.title: Fallback deal search window ends at datetime.now(UTC) although MT5 deal timestamps are server-time epochs (UTC+3) — deals closed in the last ~3 hours fall outside the window
findings.impact: Backfill run shortly after trades close intermittently finds no deals for recently closed positions and silently skips them (`if not broker_result: continue`) — looks random, depends on time-of-day. Same latent bug in mt5.py:504-506.
findings.fix: Pad the window: date_to = datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(hours=broker_utc_offset_hours + 1) (or use the configured broker offset).

findings.title: _mt5_closed_trade_result is a diverged copy of MT5Adapter.get_closed_trade_result (different tz handling, 90d vs 30d window, missing fill_price/opened_at)
findings.impact: Twin implementations drift: the adapter's tz fix (relabel to broker_tz) was applied to mt5.py but not to this copy, which is exactly how the +00:00 regression (finding above) happened. Any future fix to deal aggregation must be applied in 2+ places or the DB gets mixed-quality data.
findings.fix: Delete the copy: instantiate the MT5 broker adapter (as backfill_order_results.py does) and call broker.get_closed_trade_result(); extract the shared _load_env/_create_repository/_needs_backfill helpers into one module. If the 'temp' script is superseded by backfill_order_results.py, remove the file entirely.

findings.title: Test 5 patches BrokerBase._sleep_until_next_m5 which no longer exists anywhere in the package — AttributeError makes Test 5 always FAIL (including in the setup wizard)
findings.impact: The broker connectivity test can never pass against the current codebase. During setup or troubleshooting the owner sees a FAIL for a perfectly working broker (or learns to ignore FAILs — masking real broker problems later).
findings.fix: Delete the stale monkey-patch; the current _m5_loop already polls every poll_interval_seconds (default 30 s), so Test 5 can simply pass a short poll interval via start_background_tasks kwargs (candle_poll_interval) and wait, or drop Test 5's patching entirely.

findings.title: last_ts only advances for DISPLAYED events — filtered-out events are re-fetched every poll and written to the --log audit file again and again (duplicate/corrupted audit log; with a non-matching filter, last_ts never advances at all)
findings.impact: The --log file — explicitly advertised as 'ALL events, full payload' audit data — contains the same events duplicated dozens/hundreds of times. Anyone reconstructing what the trading system did from this audit file (e.g. post-mortem after a loss) gets a corrupted picture; with e.g. '--llm --log llm.json' during a quiet period, the file grows unboundedly with duplicates.
findings.fix: Move the last_ts update to immediately after _log_event(), before the display-filter continues (mirror tools/logging.py).

findings.title: monitor.py sends no X-API-Key header and has no --api-key option, but the management router protects /monitoring/events; its sibling tools (logging.py, ask.py) both support the key
findings.impact: On any secured deployment the console monitor silently shows nothing — the operator believes the system is down or idle while it trades, or runs production without an API key just to keep the monitor working.
findings.fix: Add --api-key (default os.environ.get('MANAGEMENT_API_KEY')) and send the X-API-Key header in _fetch, like tools/logging.py; distinguish HTTP 401/403 from network errors in the retry message.

findings.title: Log writer thread is a daemon and is never joined; KeyboardInterrupt is only caught around time.sleep() — the closing ']' and queued events are frequently lost, producing an invalid/truncated --log JSON file
findings.impact: The file documented as 'a fully valid JSON file' on clean exit routinely ends mid-array or without the closing bracket; downstream json.load of the audit file fails, and the last events before shutdown (often the interesting ones) are silently dropped. Additionally the inner 'except Exception: pass' at line 387-388 swallows disk-write errors, so disk-full data loss is invisible.
findings.fix: Wrap the whole poll loop in try/finally like tools/logging.py: on any exit put the sentinel and join the (non-daemon or joined) writer thread with a timeout; report write errors instead of pass.

findings.title: Update trigger is `remote != local` (string inequality), not a version comparison — the updater happily downgrades; and get_remote_version selects the max version INCLUDING prereleases, diverging from the management API which shows the first (latest published) non-draft release
findings.impact: If the latest tag is deleted/re-pointed, or GitHub returns an older release as highest parseable, a scheduled '--yes' run silently DOWNGRADES the live trading system; prerelease builds are auto-installed onto production; the UI can display one 'available version' while the updater installs another.
findings.fix: Compare _parse_version(remote) > _parse_version(local) before updating (require explicit --version for downgrades), skip releases with prerelease=true unless a --pre flag is given, and share one release-selection implementation with openforexai/management/api.py.

findings.title: install_update has no rollback, no atomicity and never deletes files removed by the new release — a failed pip/npm step leaves a half-updated live installation; renamed/deleted modules linger as stale importable files
findings.impact: A network hiccup during pip install leaves disk state = new code, running process = old code, dependencies = old set; the next (possibly automatic wrapper) restart boots an untested old/new mix. Stale .py files from removed modules remain importable and can be silently picked up (e.g. an old adapter still registered via config), producing subtle behavioral drift rather than a crash.
findings.fix: Stage the new tree next to the install, run pip/npm against the staged copy, then swap atomically (or at minimum: snapshot the overwritten files first and restore them on any failure; delete files that no longer exist in the release, respecting the preserve list).

findings.title: Release archive is applied and its setup code executed (pip install -e) with no integrity verification beyond TLS — no checksum, signature, or tag pinning
findings.impact: Anyone who can move a tag in the GitHub repo (compromised account/repo, force-pushed tag) gets arbitrary code execution on the trading host with access to broker credentials in .env — the classic supply-chain path for slow, targeted financial loss.
findings.fix: Pin releases by commit SHA or verify the zipball SHA-256 against a checksum published in the GitHub release assets (fetched via the API over a separate request); at minimum record and log the resolved commit SHA before applying.

findings.title: Production launch wrapper does not restart the app after a crash — it only restarts on the explicit restart flag; any unexpected child exit terminates supervision
findings.impact: A 3 a.m. crash leaves open leveraged positions completely unmanaged (no SL adjustments, no sync loop, no monitoring) until a human notices — a direct 'losses that surface later' scenario for a system whose whole design assumes it keeps running.
findings.fix: Add crash-restart with a backoff and restart-storm limit (e.g. restart on non-zero exit up to N times per hour, with logging); wrap the post-kill wait in try/except; optionally attempt a graceful stop (CTRL_BREAK_EVENT to a CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP child) before terminate().

findings.title: Backward-compat 'repository' parameter chain: BrokerBase.start_background_tasks keeps a dead repository kwarg 'for compat', and test_broker.py still builds and passes two stub repository classes that are never used
findings.impact: Owner explicitly wants all compat shims removed; the dead parameter plus stub classes mislead readers into thinking the broker persists via an injected repository, hiding the real event-bus persistence path.
findings.fix: Delete the repository kwarg from BrokerBase.start_background_tasks and remove _StubRepo/_LiveRepo and both repository= arguments from tools/test_broker.py.

findings.title: .env parser implemented six times across tools/ and scripts/ — all copies share the same parsing flaws (inline '#' comments become part of the value; existing environment variables are unconditionally overwritten)
findings.impact: Six divergence-prone copies of security-critical parsing; a user adding an innocent inline comment to .env corrupts a broker/LLM credential, and an operator overriding a key via the service environment is silently beaten by the stale .env value.
findings.fix: Create one shared loader (e.g. openforexai/config/env.py or use python-dotenv with override=False), strip inline comments, and import it from all six call sites.

findings.title: monitor.py and logging.py are divergent twin implementations of the same poll-/monitoring-events pipeline (fetch with since-cursor, connection-state tracking, queue + background writer thread) — and every behavioral difference between them is a defect in one of the two
findings.impact: Each future change (auth, endpoint shape, since-semantics) must be made twice; three of the concrete bugs reported above exist only because one copy was fixed/written correctly and the other was not.
findings.fix: Extract a shared poll client (fetch + since-cursor + api-key + writer-queue lifecycle) into one module used by both tools, keeping only the rendering (console vs rotating JSONL) separate.

findings.title: ec_runs and assessment_memory tables are never created on PostgreSQL — save_ec_run and assessment-memory methods fail with UndefinedTableError
findings.impact: On Postgres, every EventComposer run log write and every assessment-memory read/write raises UndefinedTableError. EC observability and agent assessment memory silently or loudly break depending on caller error handling.
