findings.fix: Create ec_runs and assessment_memory in _ensure_core_tables (with Postgres-appropriate types) or add a Postgres migration path; align save_ec_run upsert semantics with the SQLite implementation.

findings.title: decision_type_new column is a pure backward-compat shim: both adapters write the same value to decision_type AND decision_type_new and read via COALESCE
findings.impact: Dead weight the owner explicitly wants removed; the COALESCE also makes the hot get_analysis_records filter unindexable (see separate finding) and every new reader must remember the dual-key dance.
findings.fix: Backfill `UPDATE agent_decisions SET decision_type = decision_type_new WHERE decision_type_new IS NOT NULL` once, then drop decision_type_new from writes and reads in both adapters and (via table rebuild) from the schema.

findings.title: Fib retracement levels are anchored at p1 (trend start), inverting the standard convention — the '23.6%' line is drawn at the 76.4% retracement price
findings.impact: A trader drawing a retracement from swing low to swing high sees a line labeled '38.2%' at the price everyone else's platform labels '61.8%' — key entry/stop levels for shallow retracements (23.6%) are placed at completely different prices than intended. Directly produces bad manual entries that look random.
findings.fix: Anchor levels at the trend end: `const price = p2.price - (p2.price - p1.price) * level` (or equivalently keep the formula and relabel `((1-level)*100)`), matching the standard 0%-at-p2 convention.

findings.title: Fib time zones use cumulative sums of the Fibonacci sequence (1,2,4,7,12,20,33,...) instead of Fibonacci numbers (1,2,3,5,8,13,21,...)
findings.impact: All time-zone verticals beyond the second are drawn at wrong bar offsets (4 instead of 3, 7 instead of 5, 12 instead of 8, ...), and the on-chart labels display these wrong numbers. A trader timing reversals off these zones acts on non-Fibonacci intervals.
findings.fix: Drop the cumulative sum and use the sequence values directly as offsets: `const offsets = [1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 55]; const x = startX + offsets[i] * unitPx; ctx.fillText(String(offsets[i]), ...)`.

findings.title: Drawings silently vanish whenever any anchor time is not an exact bar time in the loaded window (timeToCoordinate exact-match returns null, primitives bail entirely)
findings.impact: A trendline/channel/fib the trader drew days ago silently disappears once its left anchor falls off the loaded 500-candle window or after a timeframe switch, even though most of the line should still be visible across the pane. The trader loses the level they were trading against without any indication; looks random.
findings.fix: Convert times to coordinates via logical index instead of exact time match: use timeScale().timeToIndex(time, true)/logicalToCoordinate, or store bar-offset/logical anchors, or clamp missing anchors by linear extrapolation from the two nearest known times, so partially-off-window drawings still render their visible portion.

findings.title: Leftover debug logging: fire-and-forget POST to /debug/log for every overlay line on every overlayLines render
findings.impact: Continuous network chatter to a debug endpoint in production (N requests per 30s refresh per chart), wasted string/array work per render, and a 404/console-error stream if the endpoint is absent. Pure development leftover.
findings.fix: Delete the fetch('/debug/log') block and the `outside` computation (line 628) used only by it.

findings.title: Null-coordinate fallback assumes off-screen, so a session boundary inside the visible range that matches no exact bar time makes the band disappear or snap to the pane edge
findings.impact: Session bands intermittently vanish or render with a wrong start/end edge around weekends, holidays, and on timeframes whose bar times don't align with session boundaries (H4/D1). The trader's session-context display is silently wrong exactly at week open — the period this overlay exists to clarify.
findings.fix: When timeToCoordinate returns null for an in-range timestamp, resolve via the nearest bar: use timeScale().timeToIndex(ts, true) + logicalToCoordinate (or binary-search the series data for the first bar >= ts) instead of assuming off-screen.

findings.title: Three competing writers set the right price-scale scaleMargins with contradictory values — pan-mode exit and double-click reset to a fixed 0.32 bottom that ignores oscillator panes, and the creation-time margins are immediately overwritten
findings.impact: With any oscillator visible (bottom should be 0.25-0.55), toggling pan mode off or double-clicking the chart forces bottom back to 0.32, so candlesticks overlap or misalign with the oscillator/volume panes until the oscillators prop next changes. Layout appears randomly broken depending on user interaction order.
findings.fix: Centralize margin computation in one function (deriving bottom from current oscillator count) and call it from the pan-mode effect, the dblclick handler, and the oscillators effect; delete the now-dead creation-time margin literals at lines 304-309.

findings.title: PRAGMA foreign_keys never enabled — kb_documents ON DELETE SET NULL is inert; deleting a folder orphans its children invisibly
findings.impact: SQLite defaults foreign_keys OFF per connection, so SET NULL never fires. Children keep a dangling parent_id; DocTree.buildTree (DocTree.tsx:56-64) groups them under a key that no node renders, so entire subtrees silently disappear from the tree after a folder delete. Documents still exist in the DB and appear in search, but are unreachable via the tree and cannot be moved back to root (see the parent_id=null bug).
findings.fix: Execute PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON in initialize() (note: also audit effects on other tables), or make kb_delete_document explicitly re-parent (UPDATE kb_documents SET parent_id=NULL WHERE parent_id=?) / recursively delete children.

findings.title: MovePicker allows moving a folder into its own descendant; backend has no cycle check — subtree vanishes from the tree
findings.impact: Moving folder A into its child B creates a parent cycle. buildTree then has no root path to A or B, so the whole subtree disappears from the DocTree with no error; with move-to-root broken (parent_id=null bug), there is no UI way to repair it.
findings.fix: In MovePicker exclude all descendants of the moved folder; in the backend, before applying parent_id, verify the target exists, is a folder, and walk the parent chain to reject cycles.

findings.title: saveNow has try/finally without catch — failed saves produce no user feedback, only an unhandled promise rejection
findings.impact: User hits Ctrl+S, save fails (backend restart, network blip), UI looks normal, user closes the tab — edits are silently lost and only discovered much later.
findings.fix: Add a catch that surfaces the error (toast/inline banner, keep 'unsaved' state); apply the same to the other API call sites.

findings.title: Broker template omits abstract modify_position — class cannot be instantiated at all
findings.impact: Every user who scaffolds a broker adapter from this template ships an adapter that crashes at bootstrap with `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ... modify_position`. The template's own tests (demo_broker_test.py) fail at the first line for the same reason, but are never run in CI (pyproject.toml testpaths=["tests"]), so the drift is invisible.
findings.fix: Add `async def modify_position(self, position_id: str, stop_loss: Decimal | None = None, take_profit: Decimal | None = None) -> TradeResult` to the template, matching ports/broker.py.

findings.title: close_position signature drifted: missing units/pair params that BrokerBase always passes
findings.impact: An adapter scaffolded from this template raises `TypeError: close_position() got an unexpected keyword argument 'pair'` on every POSITION_CLOSE request. In BrokerBase._handle_close_request the exception is caught and returned as `{"success": False, "error": ...}` — the position is silently never closed at the broker, which is exactly the class of quiet financial-loss defect the owner reports (SL/TP-less positions left open).
findings.fix: Update the template signature to `close_position(self, position_id: str, units: int | None = None, pair: str | None = None)`.

findings.title: Template subclasses AbstractBroker, but the system requires BrokerBase (bus handlers + background loops)
findings.impact: A registered adapter built from this template crashes at startup with AttributeError on start_background_tasks; if that were ever guarded, the adapter would silently never stream M5 candles, never poll the account, never sync the order book, and never answer order/close/modify requests — dead trading pipeline.
findings.fix: Change the template to subclass `openforexai.adapters.brokers.base.BrokerBase` (calling `super().__init__(monitoring_bus=None)`), and document that BrokerBase provides the loops while the subclass implements the data/order primitives.

findings.title: LLM template complete()/complete_with_tools() signatures drifted: missing images and reasoning_effort params
findings.impact: A provider scaffolded from this template fails with `TypeError: complete_with_tools() got an unexpected keyword argument 'images'` on every single LLM request routed through LLMService — all agents using it stop producing decisions.
findings.fix: Align both signatures with ports/llm.py: add `images: list[str] | None = None` and `reasoning_effort: str | None = None`, and change temperature/max_tokens defaults to None to match the port.

findings.title: Demo tool reads context.data_container — a field explicitly removed from ToolContext
findings.impact: Executing this demo tool (or any tool a user builds by copying this 'context usage' example) raises AttributeError on every call — the template actively teaches a removed API instead of the mandated bus_request() pattern.
findings.fix: Rewrite the candle-preview section to use `bus_request(context, EventType..., ...)` / `repo_request(...)` from openforexai.tools.base, matching how real tools fetch candles.

findings.title: Deregister uses exact-string line matching that misses the real aligned register lines — leaves __init__.py importing a moved file, bricking startup
findings.impact: `python template/data/data_adapter_manager.py --deregister --name sqlite` removes the import and moves openforexai/adapters/data/sqlite.py to template/data/, but leaves `PluginRegistry.register_data_container("sqlite", SQLiteDataContainer)` behind → `NameError: SQLiteDataContainer` on `import openforexai.adapters.data` → the entire system fails to boot. The same whitespace-sensitive dedupe check at lines 104-109 also fails to detect the existing registrations and appends duplicates.
findings.fix: Remove/dedupe lines by regex (reuse REGISTER_DC_RE/REGISTER_REPO_RE/IMPORT_RE with the parsed name/class), not by exact string equality. Apply the same fix to the identical logic in broker_adapter_manager.py:149, llm_adapter_manager.py:136 and tool_registry_manager.py:123-124, which are equally whitespace-fragile.

findings.title: Register silently overwrites existing production adapter modules, breaking the package import
findings.impact: If the new file does not define the old class name, the next `import openforexai.adapters.brokers` raises ImportError and the whole system cannot start; if module names merely collide, live adapter source is destroyed without warning. Same unchecked copy2 in data_adapter_manager.py:97, llm_adapter_manager.py:99, and tool_registry_manager.py:226 (where it can overwrite built-in tools like openforexai/tools/market/get_candles.py).
findings.fix: Refuse to overwrite an existing target module (or require an explicit --force), and verify the expected class exists in the copied file before rewriting __init__.py.

findings.title: Four near-identical copies of the registry-manager machinery (parse/insert/detect/move/main)
findings.impact: The data-manager whitespace bug and the overwrite hazard each exist in 4 places; fixing one copy leaves the others broken (already observable: the four copies have drifted, e.g. llm IMPORT_RE accepts multi-class imports, the others do not).
findings.fix: Extract a shared template/_registry_manager_lib.py (or a single script parameterized by kind: broker|data|llm|tool) and keep one implementation of the line-rewriting logic.

findings.title: register_agent / unregister_agent kept as 'migration' aliases — and still actively used
findings.impact: Owner explicitly wants all backward-compat shims removed; dual APIs invite divergence.
findings.fix: Change config_service.py:47 (and any other callers) to register_member/unregister_member, then delete both aliases.

findings.title: Fan-out delivers the SAME AgentMessage instance (shared mutable payload dict) to every target queue and to monitoring
findings.impact: If any consumer (or monitoring sink serializing later) mutates the payload or a nested list/dict, all other consumers of the same event see the mutated data — classic source of random-seeming divergence between agents receiving 'the same' candle trigger. Grep found no top-level `msg.payload[...] =` mutations today, but nothing enforces this.
findings.fix: Either freeze the model (`model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)`) and document payload immutability, or deliver `message.model_copy(deep=True)` per queue (cost: one deep copy per target). What to verify: nested-structure mutations in agent.py/composer.py consumers.

findings.title: register_response_future silently overwrites an existing future under the same correlation_id; abandoned futures leak in _pending_futures
findings.impact: Keys are `str(uuid4())` so collisions are practically impossible, but a caller cancelled at the wrong instant leaves a permanent dict entry that will intercept and swallow any late response, plus unbounded slow growth of _pending_futures over weeks of uptime.
findings.fix: In register_response_future, assert/log if the key already exists; add done-callback based self-cleanup (future.add_done_callback that pops the key) so cancellation of the awaiting task always removes the entry.

findings.title: Rule-disable flag is read from JSON key 'disable' while the dataclass field is named 'disabled' — 'disabled: true' in the file is silently ignored
findings.impact: A user disables a rule (e.g. to stop a signal route during maintenance) using the intuitive key 'disabled'; the rule keeps firing — silent, config-shaped trap.
findings.fix: Accept both keys during a deprecation window or, better, standardize on one name end-to-end (file key, dataclass field, API serialization) and reject unknown keys in _rules_from_dict with a warning.

findings.title: Stale comment: 'None = broadcast to all subscribers' — actual behavior is routing-table resolution, potentially a silent drop
findings.impact: Developers relying on the comment assume unrouted events reach everyone; in reality they vanish.
findings.fix: Update the comment to 'None = resolve via routing table (dropped if no rule matches)'.

findings.title: Docs say TYPE ∈ {AA, BA, GA, AD} but _VALID_TYPES also contains 'EC'
findings.impact: Stale docs; a maintainer 'fixing' the set to match the docstring would break all EC routing.
findings.fix: Update both doc comments to include EC.

findings.title: Monitoring 'target' field emitted with three different types: str, list, or None depending on path
findings.impact: Any monitoring consumer/UI filtering or grouping by target must handle str vs list vs None; easy to write a filter that silently misses multi-target deliveries.
findings.fix: Always emit `targets: list[str]` (possibly empty) for a uniform shape.

findings.title: 4-segment pattern silently matches IDs that carry a 5th extension segment
findings.impact: A routing from-pattern or wildcard target intended for the base agent also captures/delivers to extension variants (e.g. an experimental '-V2' optimizer receives production events). Whether this is intended is undocumented — verify against how extension agents are used.
findings.fix: Decide and document: either require patterns to explicitly use '-*' to include extensions (add `if len(parts) == 4 and aid.extension: return False`), or document the prefix-match behavior in the matches() docstring.

findings.title: Legacy-schema migration shims: runtime ALTER TABLE probes in _get_conn and redundant _column_exists guard in read_events
findings.impact: Per-call PRAGMA overhead on the hot write path and a misleading dual code path kept only for old database files; the owner explicitly wants compat shims removed.
findings.fix: Run migrations once at startup (or ship a one-time migration script), then delete _column_exists, the ALTER blocks, and the line-177 guard (use `clauses.append("is_trace_root = 1")` unconditionally).

findings.title: Class docstring claims queue default of 10 000 events; actual DEFAULT_QUEUE_SIZE is 1 000
findings.impact: An operator sizing consumers from the docstring expects 10x more headroom before drops; slow consumers silently lose 10x more monitoring events than documented.
findings.fix: Correct the docstring to 1 000 (or raise the constant) and state explicitly that the newest event is dropped on overflow.

findings.title: MonitoringEvent.timestamp is 'always UTC' by comment only — no timezone validation, naive datetimes are accepted
findings.impact: One future emitter using `datetime.utcnow()` (naive) makes `recent_events(since=...)` raise 'can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes', turning GET /monitoring/events into a permanent 500 until restart — monitoring blindness during live trading. Currently latent; report kept low because all present producers are aware-UTC.
findings.fix: Add a pydantic field validator that rejects (or coerces) naive datetimes: `if v.tzinfo is None: raise ValueError(...)` / `v.astimezone(UTC)`.

findings.title: AnyCandle divider counter is restored on session-filter skips but NOT on runtime_paused or llm_busy skips — post-resume analysis is delayed a full divider cycle
findings.impact: With AnyCandle=3: a due candle arriving while paused or while the LLM is busy is dropped AND the counter restarts at 0, so the next analysis happens 3 candles (15 min) later instead of on the next candle — inconsistent with the session-skip behaviour and a source of randomly delayed signals after every pause or long cycle.
findings.fix: Apply the same `self._m5_candle_event_count = self._any_candle_divider - 1` restore in the runtime_paused and llm_busy skip branches (or move the divider consumption after all skip checks).

findings.title: AGENT_CYCLE_END is published with success=true even when the cycle aborted early (paused, not initialised, invalid snapshot, cancelled by assembly script, LLM failure already handled)
findings.impact: Observability data lies: dashboards/DB show successful cycles for candles where no analysis or decision actually happened, masking the silent-skip cases the owner is hunting (invalid snapshots, paused runtime, LLM failures).
findings.fix: Have _run_cycle_inner return a status (completed/skipped/failed + reason) and publish it in the AGENT_CYCLE_END payload instead of a hard-coded success=true.

findings.title: _measure_trigger_age_ms raises uncaught TypeError for naive timestamps, and the message-loop catch then drops the entire trigger event
findings.impact: MT5 candles are currently tz-aware (+03:00 via _broker_timestamp), but normalize_candle (adapters/brokers/base.py:52-54) yields naive datetimes for offset-less strings, and repaired/DB-sourced candles could too. One naive timestamp → the M5 trigger (or analysis_result) is silently dropped: no analysis, no trade, only a generic message-loop error line.
findings.fix: Catch (ValueError, TypeError) around parse+subtraction, or normalise: `if trigger_ts.tzinfo is None: trigger_ts = trigger_ts.replace(tzinfo=UTC)`. Trigger-age measurement must never be able to kill trigger delivery — compute it in its own try.

findings.title: Agent uses the migration alias bus.register_agent(), which bus.py marks 'kept during migration'
findings.impact: Backward-compat alias kept alive by this call site; owner wants all compat shims removed. Also note stop() never calls unregister — cleanup relies entirely on the management API.
findings.fix: Call bus.register_member(agent_id) directly and delete the register_agent/unregister_agent aliases in bus.py once all callers are migrated.

findings.title: Multiple dead items: unreachable return, unused Path import, never-passed images parameter, unused publish() wrapper, uncalled load_prompt()
findings.impact: Dead surface area that suggests capabilities (vision input, external publish, hot prompt swap) which do not actually exist; load_prompt in particular hides that PROMPT_UPDATED has no real handler (see the _resolve_analysis_timestamp finding).
findings.fix: Delete the unreachable return, the Path import, the images parameter (and its pass-through), Agent.publish, and load_prompt — or wire load_prompt into a PROMPT_UPDATED handler if that behaviour is wanted.

findings.title: The same JSON payloads are re-parsed with _parse_json_object up to 4 times per cycle
findings.impact: Redundant CPU on the hot per-candle path and, more importantly, three separate parse sites that can drift in behaviour (e.g. one adding brace-extraction rules the others lack).
findings.fix: Parse payload["response"] once at the top of _run_cycle_inner and pass the object down (reuse _parsed_response for analysis_object and _resolve_cycle_pair); parse final_text once after the LLM loop and share it with the fallback/persist/accelerate helpers.

findings.title: Entire tool-token-budget plumbing is dead: dispatcher declares used_tokens/max_tokens 'Unused compatibility parameter'
findings.impact: The config key `tool_config.context_budget_tokens` and the budget heuristic have zero runtime effect — operators tuning it change nothing (silent config lie). Line 1173's `budget_tokens = max(response.input_tokens + response.output_tokens, 0)` exists solely to feed the dead parameters.
findings.fix: Remove `_tool_context_budget_tokens`, `budget_tokens`, the config resolution at 279-283, and the parameters from dispatcher.visible_specs/execute_all; or actually implement the tier gating the comment at line 278 promises.

findings.title: Divider progress is lost when a due M5 trigger is skipped due to runtime pause — inconsistent with the session-filter skip which restores the counter
findings.impact: With AnyCandle=3 (live config), a candle that was due during a pause loses the full divider cycle: after resume, the next analysis is delayed up to 2 extra candles (10 minutes) instead of firing on the next candle — late entries/exits that look random.
findings.fix: Apply the same divider-1 restore before the `continue` at line 582 (and consider a shared helper so the two skip paths cannot diverge again).

findings.title: DECISION_END is only published on success — a failed LLM call leaves DECISION_START unpaired
findings.impact: Observability consumers pairing start/end events (latency dashboards, trace views) see dangling DECISION_STARTs whenever the LLM errors or times out; failure latency/tokens are never reported for the decision engine path.
findings.fix: Publish DECISION_END with `success: False` and the error string in the except path, mirroring the AGENT_CYCLE_END pattern.

findings.title: Unused parameters: `images` and `correlation_id` in _run_with_tools; unreachable `return None` in _wait_for_config
findings.impact: Code hygiene only: dead parameters imply capabilities (image input, correlation propagation) that do not exist, misleading future callers.
findings.fix: Remove `correlation_id` and `images` from the signature (or wire images through from a real caller), delete line 190.

findings.title: force_run triggers reset the M5 divider counter and are still subject to session-filter/pause skips
findings.impact: An operator manually firing an agent gets a 202 Accepted but no cycle (only an info log), and the next organic analysis is additionally delayed up to divider-1 candles because the counter was zeroed. Confusing, looks like random non-determinism.
findings.fix: Let force_run bypass the session filter (it already bypasses the divider), or return an explicit skipped-reason via monitoring; do not reset `_m5_candle_event_count` for forced runs.

findings.title: latest_price silently falls back to 0.0, and the candle-based fallback takes the first list-typed raw output in block order (possibly stale long-timeframe close)
findings.impact: On timer-triggered cycles (trigger_payload={}) with only indicator blocks, the LLM receives latest_price 0.0 as valid market data; with H1-first block ordering it receives a stale price — SL/TP distance reasoning is silently wrong. Fail-open on the money path.
findings.fix: Prefer the short_timeframe candle output (match block arguments) for the fallback; if no price can be resolved, append "latest_price_unavailable" to errors instead of defaulting to 0.0.

findings.title: Dual-key reads of 'values' or legacy 'value' throughout indicator handling — calculate_indicator only ever returns 'values'
findings.impact: Legacy dual-field reads the owner explicitly wants removed; the `or`-chain also silently falls through when 'values' is an empty list, masking the values-is-None 'Not enough candle data' case as a normal empty series.
findings.fix: Read only 'values'; delete the 'value' fallbacks and the `del result["value"]` line in all four locations.

findings.title: Triple output-variable aliases (result / out / in_) in script sandboxes — dual-read compat convention
findings.impact: Two competing output conventions kept alive for backward compatibility; a script assigning to `out` while another assigns `result` behaves differently in subtle ways (result always wins because it is pre-seeded — meaning `out = ...` assignments are ALWAYS ignored since 'result' is always present in locals: the `out` branch at line 348 is actually unreachable dead code).
findings.fix: Standardize on `result` only: remove the 'out'/'in_' seeds and the get('out') fallbacks (line 343, 348).

findings.title: Unused parameters threaded through the whole snapshot API: repository, broker, strategy_aggressiveness, key_present, block_id, profile
findings.impact: Misleading API surface — readers assume tools receive the repository; future refactors keep threading dead arguments.
findings.fix: Remove all six dead parameters/variables and update the call sites.

findings.title: _json_snapshot uses json.dumps without a default handler while the sandbox hands scripts Decimal — non-JSON types in tool/assembly outputs crash user-message building
findings.impact: Cycle dies with an unrelated-looking TypeError at message-build time instead of a block-level validation error; on the agent loop this surfaces as a raised exception outside the snapshot error gate.
findings.fix: Use `json.dumps(..., default=str)` or sanitize snapshot values (Decimal→float/str) before serialization.

findings.title: SNAPSHOT_START/SNAPSHOT_END publish failures swallowed with bare except-pass
findings.impact: If the event bus starts failing (routing misconfig, queue full), snapshot lifecycle monitoring silently disappears — operators lose the exact telemetry needed to diagnose the rare-defect class, with no hint anything is wrong. Monitoring-only path, so low.
findings.fix: Log at warning level in the except blocks (logger is available to callers; pass one in or use module logger).

findings.title: Previewing a block with enabled:false returns the misleading generic error 'tool_preview_failed'
findings.impact: UI preview of a currently-disabled block reports a failure instead of either previewing it or saying 'block disabled' — operator confusion only.
findings.fix: Force `enabled: True` on the copy inside preview_snapshot_tool_block (it is a preview), or return a specific 'block_disabled' message.

findings.title: EC message loop executes queued stale triggers sequentially instead of skipping when busy — old candles/analyses are processed as if current
findings.impact: A guard EC triggered by analysis_result/signal_generated evaluates a minutes-old signal against get_open_positions state as if it were current, and its EC_OUTPUT is then relayed to the BA which places an order based on stale market context. Occurs only when scripts occasionally run long — rare, timing-dependent losses.
findings.fix: Match the agent behavior: check `self._run_lock.locked()` and skip stale trigger processing (emitting a trigger-skipped monitoring event), or attach a freshness check on the trigger's created_at before running.

findings.title: Timer loop drifts: interval is slept AFTER each run, so the true period is interval + lock-wait + script runtime; stop() can also take a full interval to be observed
findings.impact: A 300s timer EC whose script takes 5-20s drifts by minutes per day relative to candle boundaries; over weeks its runs land at arbitrary offsets inside candles, producing time-inconsistent decisions. A stopped bootstrap timer-EC with a long interval lingers up to that interval.
findings.fix: Compute the next fire time from a fixed anchor (`next_t += interval; sleep(max(0, next_t - loop.time()))`) and sleep in ≤1s slices (or use an asyncio.Event set by stop()) so stop() is observed promptly.

findings.title: Pending response future is only unregistered on TimeoutError — publish failure or task cancellation leaks the future in the bus registry forever
findings.impact: Every cancelled/failed LLM request leaks a future in bus._pending_futures (unbounded growth over weeks), and a very late LLM_RESPONSE with that correlation_id is consumed by the dead future (bus.py:298-301) instead of being routed/logged — quiet loss plus memory growth in a long-running trading process.
findings.fix: Use try/finally: `finally: event_bus.cancel_response_future(future_key)` (removal after normal resolution is a no-op since _dispatch already pops it).

findings.title: Instrument precedence differs between the script's message context and the published EC_OUTPUT
findings.impact: An EC with pair=EURUSD configured that is triggered by a USDJPY event tells its script instrument=USDJPY but publishes EC_OUTPUT tagged instrument=EURUSD. Any instrument-based routing/filtering or downstream consumer reading msg.instrument mislabels the output's market — a guard verdict about USDJPY gets attributed to EURUSD.
findings.fix: Use one precedence rule in both places (trigger instrument first, falling back to configured pair, matches message_ctx) — extract to a helper.

findings.title: ECRun.run_at default_factory=datetime.utcnow is timezone-naive while the only producer passes aware datetime.now(UTC)
findings.impact: Any ECRun created without an explicit run_at (tests, future callers, partial dicts through repository_service._deserialize_args) stores offset-less timestamps next to offset-bearing ones in ec_runs.run_at; string comparison/ordering and parsing then behave inconsistently.
findings.fix: `run_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))`, matching AgentMessage.created_at in models/messaging.py:125.

findings.title: pass_trigger is written into every EC config by the UI wizard and system.json5 but never read by the EC container
findings.impact: An operator toggling pass_trigger on an EC in the wizard expects the trigger payload to be withheld/passed accordingly; the EC ignores it and always passes the full payload as `input`. Dead config key inviting wrong mental models.
findings.fix: Remove pass_trigger from the EC wizard and from event_composers entries in system.json5 (or implement it in _execute if the semantic is wanted).

findings.title: test_run bypasses _run_lock — a management-API test execution runs the script concurrently with a live cycle
findings.impact: A test run of e.g. the trailing-SL EC executes real tool calls (order modification, get_open_positions) interleaved with a concurrent live cycle of the same script — double SL modifications or decisions computed on state mid-mutation. Rare, operator-action-correlated anomalies.
findings.fix: Acquire `self._run_lock` in test_run too (optionally with a short timeout returning 'busy'), keeping monitoring/DB behavior unchanged.

findings.title: EC_CYCLE_END is published without instrument and both cycle events omit correlation_id, unlike EC_CYCLE_START/EC_OUTPUT
findings.impact: Observability consumers correlating a cycle's start/end with the triggering signal by correlation_id or filtering by instrument see asymmetric data: ends cannot be matched to their pair/correlation, making latency/failure analysis of specific trade chains unreliable.
findings.fix: Add `instrument=self._pair` and `correlation_id=correlation_id` to both EC_CYCLE_START and EC_CYCLE_END messages.

findings.title: Session-filter logic implemented twice with diverging semantics (and needed a third time for ECs)
findings.impact: The management API's 'session active' display can disagree with the agent's actual gating for edge configs (e.g. pre=-10 or post=+30), misleading operators about whether an agent will trade; a third divergent copy is the likely outcome when EC session filtering is added.
findings.fix: Extract one canonical session-window evaluator (parameterized by reference time source) into openforexai/tools/market/session_status.py and use it from agent, management API, and the EC container.

findings.title: retry_async discards the original exception message, defeating the transient-error classification in _m5_loop
findings.impact: Every broker 502/timeout during weekends/maintenance is treated as non-transient: full exception tracebacks logged (base.py:614) instead of the intended WARNING, flooding logs and masking real errors; callers can no longer branch on exception type (httpx.ConnectError etc.) anywhere in the stack.
findings.fix: Re-raise the last exception: `raise last_exc` (or chain but include str(last_exc) in the message: `RuntimeError(f"All {attempts} attempts failed: {last_exc}")`). Prefer `raise last_exc` to preserve type.

findings.title: Dead compat parameters: repository= in start_background_tasks and trigger_sync, unused request_agent_reasoning in trigger_sync
findings.impact: Owner explicitly wants all compat kept-for-migration surface removed; the unused request_agent_reasoning also means agent-triggered syncs can never request reasoning even if callers pass it — silent no-op parameter.
findings.fix: Delete both repository parameters and either wire request_agent_reasoning into the returned discrepancy dicts/events or remove it.

findings.title: _build_sync_close_updates migration wrapper has zero callers
findings.impact: Dead migration shim the owner wants removed; the getattr-based OrderBookEntry fallback inside it would also silently drop fields if ever revived.
findings.fix: Delete the method.

findings.title: M5 gap detection counts closed-market periods as missing candles — spurious CANDLE_GAP_DETECTED storms after every weekend/holiday
findings.impact: Weekly false gap events; if a consumer reacts with CANDLE_REPAIR_REQUESTED, it triggers pointless bulk fetches (base.py:326) every Monday open for every pair — noise that buries real gaps.
findings.fix: Suppress or annotate gaps that span the weekend/market-closed window (e.g. compare against a trading-calendar-aware expected timestamp, or cap/flag gaps > N hours as session breaks).

findings.title: _handle_modify_request forwards float SL/TP straight into a port that declares Decimal
findings.impact: Type contract broken on the money path; a future adapter (MT5) that trusts the Decimal annotation for pip math can produce subtly wrong stop prices.
findings.fix: Convert in the handler: `Decimal(str(v)) if v is not None else None` before calling modify_position (and have the tool send strings, not floats).

findings.title: Abstract fetch_latest_m5_candle is never called by any framework code and its docstring claims a caller that does not exist
findings.impact: Every future adapter is forced to implement a method nothing calls; stale docstring misdescribes the streaming loop.
findings.fix: Remove the abstract method and the OANDA implementation.

findings.title: close_position fetches ALL open trades before every close just to learn the target's units
findings.impact: Adds a full openTrades round-trip of latency to the time-critical close path, and races: if the broker closed the position (SL hit) between listing and the close call, the tool receives 'position not found' as an error even though the desired outcome (flat) already holds — agents may retry or escalate needlessly.
findings.fix: Use GET /v3/accounts/{id}/trades/{position_id} for the single trade, or pass units='ALL' for full closes and derive status from the close response's tradesClosed/tradeReduced fields; treat 404 on close as already-closed, not an error.

findings.title: close_position does a TOCTOU get_open_positions round-trip only to find target.units — stale by the time the close executes
findings.impact: If the SL hits between the lookup and the PUT, close raises/404s although the desired outcome already happened; if another partial close lands in between, the CLOSED/OPEN classification is computed against stale units and can label a full close as partial (entry stays OPEN locally). Also one extra full-account API call per close.
findings.fix: Skip the pre-fetch: send the close, and derive closed-vs-open from the response (tradeReduced vs tradeClosed / units in orderFillTransaction); treat 404 as already-closed and fall through to get_closed_trade_result.

findings.title: Concurrent MT5 API calls from multiple threads without serialization
findings.impact: Occasional garbled/empty results or wrong last_error attribution under load — intermittent, unreproducible data anomalies. Verify against the MetaTrader5 package's thread-safety guarantees; if unsafe, symptoms match the 'rare random' defect class.
findings.fix: Guard _call_blocking with an asyncio.Lock (single in-flight MT5 call per adapter) and fetch last_error inside the same locked call.

findings.title: OANDA get_closed_trade_result omits the "fill_price" key that the MT5 twin returns and that _resolve_orphaned_entry consumes
findings.impact: Orphaned OANDA entries recovered via sync_key are stored without a fill price; MT5 sync-detected closes also lose the broker-confirmed fill price. Divergent twin shapes make every consumer subtly broker-dependent.
findings.fix: Add "fill_price" (OANDA trade["price"]) to the OANDA result and copy fill_price in _build_sync_close_updates_dict too.

findings.title: practice parameter is stored but never used — legacy from before api_url became mandatory
findings.impact: Dead config knob: setting practice=false does nothing — a user could believe they toggled live/demo via config while the URL alone decides. Owner wants all compat leftovers removed.
findings.fix: Remove the practice parameter, the self._practice field, the from_config pass-through, and the stale docstring sentence.

findings.title: Dual-field read clientExtensions OR tradeClientExtensions on the Trade object — the second key never exists on OANDA Trade JSON
findings.impact: Dead fallback branch that hides the real defect and suggests the producer/consumer key mismatch was noticed but papered over.
findings.fix: After fixing place_order to send tradeClientExtensions, read only `t.get("clientExtensions", {}).get("comment")` and delete the fallback.

findings.title: Dummy TradeSignal/TradeOrder scaffolding to satisfy the TradeResult schema is copy-pasted four times
findings.impact: Four divergence-prone copies of schema-appeasement code; the real smell is that TradeResult requires a full TradeOrder for operations that have none.
findings.fix: Add a module-level helper (e.g. in base.py: _dummy_trade_result(...)) or make TradeResult.order optional for modify/close results.

findings.title: fetch_latest_m5_candle implemented identically in both adapters
findings.impact: Twin implementation; a fix (e.g. the MT5 forming-candle exclusion) applied to one copy can miss the other.
findings.fix: Move it into BrokerBase as a default implementation over get_historical_m5_candles.

findings.title: short_name validation and margin_level computation duplicated across both adapters
findings.impact: Copy-pasted invariants drift over time (e.g. one adapter loosening the 5-char limit would silently break _adapter_agent_id routing padding in base.py:26-34).
findings.fix: Hoist the validation into BrokerBase.__init__ and margin_level into a shared helper or the AccountStatus model.

findings.title: Docstring examples use short_names that the adapters' own validation rejects
findings.impact: Anyone following the documented examples gets an immediate ValueError; documentation contradicts enforced invariants.
findings.fix: Update all examples to ≤5-char names (e.g. 'OAND1', 'MT5PP') or centralize and relax the constraint.

findings.title: save_trade stores NULL for pnl/fill_price when the Decimal value is exactly 0 (falsy check instead of `is not None`)
findings.impact: Any code resurrecting the trades table (or tests validating it) will misclassify breakeven trades as PnL-unknown, skewing win-rate/total-PnL statistics that feed the optimization loop.
findings.fix: Use `str(trade.pnl) if trade.pnl is not None else None` (and same for fill_price) in both adapters.

findings.title: Runtime ALTER-if-missing column shims in _ensure_order_book_table; the PG twin lacks the sync_confirmed shim the SQLite twin has
findings.impact: Schema-evolution logic lives in per-call shims instead of migrations (owner wants shims gone), and the twins have already diverged: identical old databases behave differently per backend.
findings.fix: Move column additions into numbered migration files run by both backends; delete the per-call PRAGMA/ALTER blocks.

findings.title: update_order_book_entry interpolates dict keys directly into SQL with no column allowlist (SQL injection surface); kb_update_document right below it does use an allowlist
findings.impact: Any future caller that forwards request-derived keys (e.g. a management API PATCH endpoint) becomes an SQL injection into the money-critical order book table. Inconsistent hygiene within the same file invites that mistake.
findings.fix: Validate keys against the known order_book_entries column set before building set_clause, in both adapters.

findings.title: kb_documents declares parent_id ... ON DELETE SET NULL but SQLite foreign keys are never enabled (PRAGMA foreign_keys is off by default), so deleting a folder leaves children with dangling parent_id
findings.impact: Deleting a KB folder orphans its children under a nonexistent parent_id; depending on UI tree-building, those documents become invisible/unreachable.
findings.fix: Execute `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` after connect, or explicitly `UPDATE kb_documents SET parent_id=NULL WHERE parent_id=?` inside kb_delete_document.

findings.title: save_ec_run upsert semantics diverge: PG's ON CONFLICT updates only 5 of 12 columns while SQLite's INSERT OR REPLACE replaces the whole row
findings.impact: Re-saving an ECRun with corrected input/config/run_at produces different stored rows per backend; audit data diverges silently.
findings.fix: Make PG update all columns (matching the other upserts in this file), or make both update only the mutable subset — but identically.

findings.title: `Any` is used in annotations but never imported in sqlite.py — masked only by `from __future__ import annotations`
findings.impact: Latent NameError the moment any tooling resolves these annotations; postgresql.py imports Any correctly (line 7), another twin drift.
findings.fix: Add `from typing import Any` to sqlite.py imports.

findings.title: _row_to_order_book_entry is declared async yet contains no await, and re-executes a deferred import per row
findings.impact: Needless coroutine overhead per row on the sync path and misleading code; no functional error.
findings.fix: Make it a plain (static) method, hoist OrderType into the module-level import, in both adapters.

findings.title: Port docstring says get_open_order_book_entries returns 'status PENDING or OPEN' but both implementations also include PARTIALLY_FILLED
findings.impact: Contract documentation is wrong; a future third adapter written to the docstring would drop partially-filled positions from the sync loop — the exact silent-loss class.
findings.fix: Update the port docstring to name all three statuses (or reference OrderStatus members programmatically).

findings.title: All temporal ordering (ORDER BY timestamp/decided_at/requested_at/recorded_at DESC) is lexicographic on raw isoformat TEXT with no tz normalization — correct only while every producer emits UTC datetimes in a uniform format
findings.impact: get_latest_account_status / get_candles(newest first) / get_open_order_book_entries ordering silently returns stale data as 'latest' whenever offset formats mix — decisions made on stale account equity or candles; rare and invisible.
findings.fix: Normalize to aware UTC (`dt.astimezone(UTC)`) before isoformat() in every save path of both adapters, and attach UTC on read for naive legacy strings.

findings.title: Gap repair always fetches only the newest 200 M5 candles — gaps older than ~16.7 hours are never repaired and the gap payload is ignored
findings.impact: After an outage longer than ~17h, the M5 history keeps a permanent hole that the CANDLE_GAP_DETECTED/repair path reports as repaired; resampled H4/D1 bars spanning the hole aggregate fewer M5 bars with no indication. Only a later `_ensure_m5_complete_for_read` with a large enough window papers over it — with null rows.
findings.fix: Have the broker adapter include gap start/end in the payload and size the fetch to cover `now - gap_start` (bounded), or compute the fetch count from the oldest missing slot found in the DB.

findings.title: _fetch_candles_from_broker: possibly-unbound future_key in finally, silently swallowed per-candle parse errors, deprecated get_event_loop
findings.impact: A payload schema change (e.g. a renamed candle field) would make all repairs/backfills silently return 0 candles forever — no warning, no error; gap-repair 'completes' having repaired nothing. The unbound-name path converts a clear validation error into a confusing UnboundLocalError.
findings.fix: Assign `future_key = None` before the try and guard the finally; log a warning with a counter when candles fail to parse; switch to `asyncio.get_running_loop()`.

findings.title: Backfill task created fire-and-forget without a saved reference — may be garbage-collected mid-run and its exceptions are unobserved
findings.impact: On a fresh deployment the initial 8064-candle backfill can silently vanish (GC) or die on the first store error without any log at the time — pairs start live trading with an empty history, all indicators return None or compute on the trickle of live candles, and nobody knows why until much later.
findings.fix: Store the task on self (`self._backfill_task = asyncio.create_task(...)`) and attach a done-callback that logs exceptions; cancel it in shutdown.

findings.title: Entire normalizer.py module is unused — and contains latent hazards (missing JPY crosses default to 0.0001, pips() strips sign) plus a duplicate of pip-size logic living elsewhere
findings.impact: Dead module with money-math footguns; the duplicate heuristic in EMASlopePlugin and this table can drift (e.g. exotic pairs, metals), producing 10-100x scaled slope values depending on which copy a future caller picks.
findings.fix: Delete normalizer.py, or make it the single pip-size authority (complete the table / derive from broker symbol digits), fix abs(), and refactor EMASlopePlugin to use it.

findings.title: Port methods are plain `...`-bodied (not @abstractmethod) — a backend that forgets to implement one silently no-ops and returns None
findings.impact: A new backend (e.g. the planned MariaDB) that misses one method passes instantiation and runs: agent decisions/LLM conversations are silently never persisted, discovered only weeks later when an agent restart loses all memory.
findings.fix: Decorate every method with @abstractmethod (the class already inherits from an ABC-based AbstractRepository), so incomplete backends fail at construction.

findings.title: _is_null_candle and the broker-adapter-id builder are each implemented twice, identically
findings.impact: If the null-candle definition or the adapter ID format changes in one copy only (e.g. adding a NULL marker column, widening pair field for metals like XAUUSD which already fills all 6 chars), the DataContainer would address a non-existent bus member or mis-classify nulls — repairs silently time out.
findings.fix: Move both helpers to a shared module (e.g. openforexai/models/market.py for is_null_candle, openforexai/messaging or utils for the adapter-id) and import from both sides.

findings.title: RSI/ATR minimum-length guards (period+1) permit heavily unconverged Wilder values; EMA at len==period returns the SMA seed
findings.impact: Agents comparing 'RSI 71' from the tool against strategy thresholds trained on chart RSI act on values biased by warm-up truncation — small, systematic, and invisible; worst right after data gaps/restarts when history is short.
findings.fix: Require e.g. `len >= period * 4` (or document the tolerance) for Wilder-smoothed indicators, and raise the fetch multiplier in calculate_indicator accordingly; require `period + 1` minimum for a true EMA value.

findings.title: synthetic_dxy uses the 6-pair ICE constant (50.14348112) while omitting USDSEK — absolute index level systematically ~10% below real DXY
findings.impact: Any agent prompt logic or human comparing dxy_close against known DXY levels (e.g. 'DXY above 100') is systematically wrong; direction/correlation are unaffected, making the bias easy to miss.
findings.fix: Either renormalize (scale constant by an average USDSEK^0.042 factor, or renormalize the 5 exponents to sum appropriately) and document the residual error, or rename the output (e.g. `usd_index_5`) so it is not mistaken for DXY levels.

findings.title: Bus CANDLES_REQUEST path returns DB-as-is (no completeness repair) while direct get_candles repairs — agents via tools and management API can see different candles for the same query at the same moment
findings.impact: Operator inspects a pair in the UI (triggers repair, sees clean data) while the agent that just traded used the pre-repair gappy series — post-incident analysis shows 'correct' data that the agent never saw; irreproducible bad decisions.
findings.fix: Make the read semantics uniform (e.g. both DB-only, with repair driven exclusively by the background M5 flow and a periodic completeness job), or at minimum include a `repaired: bool`/`missing_slots: int` field in CANDLES_RESPONSE so decisions are auditable.

findings.title: market_snapshot serialization diverges between twins: SQLite json.dumps without default=str will crash on Decimal/datetime, PG stringifies silently
findings.impact: Latent (method currently uncalled), but the moment agent memory is wired up on the default SQLite backend, every decision containing market data fails to persist with a TypeError — behavior differs per backend, the #1 twin-divergence class the audit targets.
findings.fix: Use `json.dumps(market_snapshot, default=str, ensure_ascii=False)` on the SQLite path too (or a shared serializer helper used by both twins).

findings.title: Conversation storage format diverges: SQLite writes zlib-compressed BLOB with is_compressed=1, PG writes plain JSON and its reader has no decompression path
findings.impact: The same port method produces incompatible on-disk representations per backend. Any tooling, export/import, or backend migration that moves agent_conversations rows between SQLite and PostgreSQL silently yields undecodable blobs (PG reader json.loads on zlib bytes -> exception swallowed -> conversation reported as nonexistent). Also PG's insert would fail outright if the table were created from migration 003+008 semantics with is_compressed NOT NULL and no default.
findings.fix: Pick one representation. Either add zlib+is_compressed handling to the PG twin (matching migration 008), or drop compression from both and store plain JSON everywhere.

findings.title: save_agent_decision_with_reasoning: unreachable ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING diverges from SQLite twin and would silently drop records if it ever fired
findings.impact: Dead clause today; if id generation ever changes (e.g. deterministic ids), PG silently swallows lost decision records while SQLite raises — divergent failure modes on an audit-trail write.
findings.fix: Remove the ON CONFLICT clause to match the SQLite twin (both are pure inserts with fresh UUIDs).

findings.title: get_last_llm_conversation: isinstance(row, dict) branches are unreachable — aiosqlite row_factory is aiosqlite.Row, never dict
findings.impact: No runtime effect, but dead defensive branches obscure the actual access pattern and suggest a row-shape uncertainty that does not exist.
findings.fix: Simplify to `raw = row["messages"]; is_compressed = row["is_compressed"]`.

findings.title: Timestamp filtering/ordering relies on lexicographic ISO-string comparison of caller-supplied datetimes — breaks if naive or non-UTC-offset datetimes are ever passed
findings.impact: Latent (no callers yet): mixed-offset or naive datetimes silently misorder 'recent decisions' and mis-filter performance windows — an agent would reason from the wrong 'most recent' decision. Exactly the rare, random-seeming defect class; low only because the API is currently dead and internal writes are uniformly UTC.
findings.fix: Normalize all inbound datetimes at the adapter boundary: `dt.astimezone(UTC).isoformat()` (and reject/assume-UTC for naive values) before storing or comparing, in both twins.

findings.title: market_snapshot deserialization loop duplicated verbatim between the two container twins
findings.impact: Four implementations of 'parse JSON field, default {}' drift independently (the parents already differ from the containers in what they catch/return); a fix in one location will predictably miss the others.
findings.fix: Extract one shared helper (e.g. in adapters/database/base.py, currently a near-empty placeholder of unused table-name constants) and use it from all four sites.

findings.title: Candle-store twin divergence: SQLite interpolates unquoted table identifiers, PG quotes them via _q_ident
findings.impact: A broker configured with a short_name starting with a digit persists candles on PG but throws sqlite3.OperationalError on every save/read on the default SQLite backend — backend-dependent candle blackout.
findings.fix: Quote the identifier in the SQLite twin too (wrap in double quotes, mirroring PG's _q_ident), or reject/prefix names that don't match a valid-identifier regex in _series_table (shared by both twins — also a duplicate: sqlite.py:557-561 vs postgresql.py:629-634).

findings.title: Both module docstrings claim 'Self-registers at import time' but registration actually lives in the package __init__, not these modules
findings.impact: Minor doc drift: someone importing the module file directly (bypassing the package) expecting registration gets a silently unregistered backend.
findings.fix: Reword both docstrings to 'registered by openforexai.adapters.data.__init__', or move the register calls into the modules to match the docs.

findings.title: _schedule_transcript_record creates a fire-and-forget task without a reference
findings.impact: Error transcript records (written from retry-error callbacks, lines 510-518/562-570) can silently never be written — exactly the diagnostic evidence needed to investigate rare live failures is randomly missing.
findings.fix: Track tasks in a set with done-callback discard, or make the error callbacks await the write (llm_retry callbacks are sync, so store and await later, or use loop.create_task with a holder set).

findings.title: complete() assumes msg.content[0] exists and is a text block
findings.impact: Sporadic IndexError/AttributeError classified as an LLM error; with a thinking-enabled model the adapter is unusable. Contrast: complete_with_tools (lines 212-214) correctly iterates blocks and filters type=='text'.
findings.fix: Join all text blocks: `content="".join(b.text for b in msg.content if b.type == "text")`.

findings.title: Prompt-comment stripping is performed twice per request: once in LLMService, again by the port's __init_subclass__ wrapper
findings.impact: Redundant O(prompt) regex passes and dict copies per LLM call on the hot path, plus two places to keep in sync; the wrapper's `.strip()` also silently trims whitespace on every message copy.
findings.fix: Drop the stripping in llm_service.py (the port wrapper already guarantees it), or remove the metaclass-style wrapper and strip once in the service.

findings.title: Explicit compatibility shim: assistant content forced to '' 'for compatibility across API versions'
findings.impact: Owner wants all compat shims removed; the dict-vs-list return-type divergence forces every caller into defensive isinstance branching and is a trap for the next call site.
findings.fix: Standardize tool_result_message to return list[dict] on all providers (anthropic wraps its single dict in a list), pick one null-content policy for both OpenAI-family builders, and delete the hasattr/isinstance branching in api.py.

findings.title: llm_retry retries ALL exceptions (including non-transient 400/auth errors) and erases the exception type by wrapping in RuntimeError
findings.impact: Deterministic failures burn 3 attempts + backoff delay (added latency on every failed trading cycle), and downstream error handling can only string-match, which breaks the moment the provider changes its error wording.
findings.fix: Retry only on transient error types (rate-limit, timeout, 5xx — anthropic/openai SDKs expose typed exceptions), re-raise the last exception directly (`raise last_exc`), and have azure's fallback check the typed BadRequestError code instead of substring matching.

findings.title: Anthropic and OpenAI clients are created without any HTTP timeout while Azure mandates timeout_seconds — SDK default (10 min) x 3 retries far exceeds the 180 s bus timeout
findings.impact: A hung Anthropic/OpenAI connection keeps the request (and its llm_retry loop) alive for up to ~30 minutes after the caller already timed out — wasted tokens/money and zombie in-flight requests; also stacked SDK-internal retries multiply with llm_retry's 3 attempts.
findings.fix: Pass timeout and max_retries=0 to AsyncAnthropic/AsyncOpenAI from config, same as the Azure adapter.

findings.title: ask_llm drops port capabilities: no images and no reasoning_effort parameters; llm_complete_with_tools' images kwarg unused from EC path
findings.impact: EC scripts cannot pass images or reasoning effort even though the whole pipeline supports it; silent capability gap between agents and EC scripts.
findings.fix: Add images/reasoning_effort passthrough parameters to ask_llm.

findings.title: LLMResponseWithTools.raw contains the provider's raw API dump on the direct-adapter path but the bus payload dict on the bus path
findings.impact: Any code inspecting response.raw for provider details (e.g. finish_reason, usage details, content filter results) works in unit tests / management-API checker (direct adapter) but silently sees a different, poorer shape in production (bus path).
findings.fix: Either document that raw is transport-dependent, or include the provider raw (or the fields consumers need) in the LLM_RESPONSE payload.

findings.title: Broker/pair override path force-uppercases while the default agent context preserves original casing
findings.impact: DataContainer keys candles by the exact short_name string it receives from broker updates; a case-mismatched override produces empty candle lookups only on the calls where the LLM explicitly passed the argument — intermittent, hard to reproduce. Also the equality short-circuit in _context_for_call (line 289) never matches, always creating a replaced context.
findings.fix: Normalize once at the source: uppercase (or preserve) broker short_name and pair identically when building the agent ToolContext and in the override resolvers, so both paths produce byte-identical keys.

findings.title: After bus_request timeout, a late response falls through to direct delivery and lands in the requesting agent's inbox as a stray message
findings.impact: Agents currently ignore event types not in _event_triggers (agent.py:543), so the stray message is usually dropped — but it inflates the agent queue, is logged/monitored as a delivered event, and if any response event type is ever configured as an agent trigger, a timed-out request would later fire a spurious agent cycle. Verify: whether any agent config lists repo_response/candles_response as a trigger.
findings.fix: In the bus dispatch, drop (or dead-letter) response-type messages whose correlation_id has no registered future, instead of falling through to delivery; or keep a short-lived tombstone set of timed-out correlation ids.

findings.title: Unresolved placeholder in forced_arguments is passed to the tool verbatim as a literal template string
findings.impact: A bridge tool or trading tool silently receives the literal string "{broker_name}" as an argument value; downstream routing/target resolution fails or targets a nonexistent member, producing timeouts or wrong behavior with no indication that a template failed to resolve.
findings.fix: When a forced-argument template cannot be fully resolved, raise or log an error and omit the argument rather than injecting the raw template text.

findings.title: Redundant re-assignments partially contradict the copy loop: empty-string config values are reintroduced and pair/broker precedence is asymmetric
findings.impact: A config entry like "broker": "" yields placeholder {broker} = "" so a forced argument template resolves to an empty string instead of falling back; and the pair-vs-broker precedence difference makes {pair}/{broker_name} resolve from different sources on otherwise symmetric configs — subtle wrong values in forced tool arguments.
findings.fix: Delete the redundant lines 28-33 for keys already handled by the loop (or guard them with `and cfg.get(key) != ""`), and use one consistent precedence rule (runtime context first or config first) for both broker and pair.

findings.title: used_tokens/max_tokens are documented 'Unused compatibility parameter' on execute_all and visible_specs but callers still pass real token budgets
findings.impact: Dead compatibility surface the owner explicitly wants removed; worse, agent.py maintains and passes a token budget that silently does nothing, misleading anyone tuning _tool_context_budget_tokens.
findings.fix: Remove both parameters from execute_all/visible_specs, update the call sites in agent.py, and remove the now-unused budget plumbing there (or actually implement the budget if it is still wanted).

findings.title: Dual-field read arguments.get("broker_name", arguments.get("broker")) — no tool schema declares a broker_name argument
findings.impact: Legacy dual-key read the owner wants removed; it also means a forced_arguments entry keyed "broker_name" would shadow the LLM's "broker" argument through a path no schema documents.
findings.fix: Read only arguments.get("broker").

findings.title: Approval machinery is entirely unused: every tool sets requires_approval=False, no config defines approval_modes, and 'human' mode is a stub that always rejects
findings.impact: Dead feature surface (attributes, _check_approval branching, spec docs) that suggests trading tools are gated when in reality every registered tool executes 'direct'; combined with the unresolvable supervisor future (separate finding) the whole gate is decorative.
findings.fix: Either wire the approval feature end-to-end and configure it, or remove requires_approval/default_approval_mode, _check_approval, and _supervisor_approval.

findings.title: No-op `except asyncio.TimeoutError: raise` in bus_request
findings.impact: Noise only.
findings.fix: Delete the except clause, keep try/finally.

findings.title: AgentToolConfig.load crashes on non-dict JSON5 root and does not catch OSError, taking down bootstrap/hot-reload
findings.impact: A malformed-but-valid-JSON5 agent_tools.json5 (e.g. accidentally saved as a top-level array) crashes system startup or the PUT /config/files/agent_tools hot-reload with an unhandled AttributeError instead of the intended graceful 'use defaults' degradation.
findings.fix: Validate `isinstance(data, dict)` before .get, and broaden the read error handling to OSError, returning cls([]) with an error log in both cases.

findings.title: ToolDispatcher docstring claims configuration 'via AgentToolConfig' but the parameter is a plain dict from system.json5; AgentToolConfig is the unrelated bridge-tools loader
findings.impact: Misleading twin naming: a maintainer wiring a new dispatcher may pass the wrong object; the class name and the parameter name collide while representing different config sources.
findings.fix: Fix the docstring and rename one of the two (e.g. BridgeToolFileConfig for the loader class).

findings.title: _emit_monitoring swallows all exceptions with bare except-pass
findings.impact: Observability-only path, but this is the audit trail for every tool call including order placements ('complete result stored for audit/evidence purposes'); a systematic emit failure would silently erase the trading audit trail for weeks.
findings.fix: Log the exception at warning level (rate-limited if needed) instead of pass.

findings.title: Image marker path is project-root-relative but the LLM adapter resolves it against os.getcwd() — images silently dropped and temp files leaked when cwd != repo root
findings.impact: If the service is started from any directory other than the repo root (systemd WorkingDirectory, task scheduler, `python -m` from elsewhere), resolve_images logs 'file not found' and the chart is NOT sent to the LLM — the agent decides without the chart it believes it attached. delete_tmp_images also misses, so temp PNGs accumulate indefinitely (disk-fill after weeks). Additionally, no cleanup happens at all if the LLM call errors before delete_tmp_images runs.
findings.fix: Emit an absolute path in the marker (`image_marker = f"{marker_type}[{out_path.as_posix()}]"`) or make _resolve_path anchor relative paths at the same project root chartshot uses; add a periodic sweep of the chartshot temp dir for orphaned files.

findings.title: DEFAULT_INDICATOR_TRANSFORM_SCRIPT calls float() on BB indicator values which are dicts — every BB snapshot block fails its transform
findings.impact: Any snapshot profile configured with a BB calculate_indicator block never delivers Bollinger data to the decision LLM — permanently, every cycle. The agent decides on a snapshot missing a configured volatility band with only a buried error string as evidence.
findings.fix: In the transform script, handle dict values: extract e.g. 'middle' for the direction series (`raw_value = raw_value.get("middle") if isinstance(raw_value, dict) else raw_value`) and keep the full dict in result["values"].

findings.title: _pair_context slices the raw un-normalized pair string — separators or lowercase break the premier-liquidity override and the returned pair field
findings.impact: For any pair passed as 'EUR/USD', 'eur_usd' etc. (the schema does not forbid separators, and the LLM frequently emits them), the London/NY overlap very_high override silently never fires and pair_liquidity is understated — an agent gating trades on liquidity skips valid premier-window entries. The pair_context.pair field is also garbled.
findings.fix: Normalize once at the top of _pair_context (reuse the same normalization as _pair_primary_sessions: uppercase + strip separators) and slice base/quote from the normalized string for both the override check and the output field.

findings.title: VWAP period=0 anchor documented as '00:00 UTC' in the tool schema but implemented/documented as broker-local midnight in the plugin
findings.impact: MT5 broker feeds typically carry broker-server time (often UTC+2/+3). The LLM is told the VWAP resets at UTC midnight while it actually resets at broker midnight — up to a 3-hour shifted anchor changes the daily VWAP value the agent compares price against, producing systematically skewed intraday bias. Also, if any path delivers mixed tz-aware/naive timestamps, comparisons mix wall clocks.
findings.fix: Pick one contract: if UTC is intended, use `_candle_ts_utc` (currently dead, indicator_plugins.py:177) for the day-start computation and delete `_candle_ts_naive`; then align both descriptions. If broker-local is intended, fix the tool schema text.

findings.title: count is capped at 500 but has no lower clamp — a negative count inverts the tail slice
findings.impact: Schema minimum=1 is advisory only — LLMs do emit out-of-range integers. A negative count silently returns a wrong, oversized candle window instead of erroring.
findings.fix: count = max(1, min(int(...), 500)) — mirroring the clamps used in swing_levels/chartshot.

findings.title: Identical _ts timestamp-formatting helper implemented in both swing_levels and calculate_indicator
findings.impact: Twin implementations drift independently (e.g. a future fix converting non-UTC aware timestamps to UTC would likely land in only one).
findings.fix: Move to a shared helper in openforexai/tools/base.py next to candle_dicts_to_objects.

findings.title: swing_levels and calculate_indicator do not validate timeframe against _VALID_TIMEFRAMES (get_candles and chartshot do)
findings.impact: A hallucinated timeframe like 'H2' yields a clean 'no levels / not enough data' answer instead of an error, so the LLM never learns its argument was invalid and may proceed without S/R context.
findings.fix: Raise ValueError for unknown timeframes exactly as get_candles.py:47-48 does; same in calculate_indicator.execute.

findings.title: Output timestamp appends 'Z' to the input's local wall time when a non-UTC offset is supplied
findings.impact: Session statuses themselves are correct (astimezone is used per session), but the echoed timestamp mislabels the reference time as UTC; anything correlating the result by this field (logs, snapshot assembly) is shifted by the input offset.
findings.fix: Normalize first: `utc_dt = utc_dt.astimezone(UTC)` before building the result (or format with utc_dt.astimezone(UTC)).

findings.title: closed_holiday takes precedence over out-of-hours, so a London/NY holiday forces recommended_action='avoid' for the entire 24h day
findings.impact: Agents trading Asia-session pairs are told to avoid trading all day whenever London or NY has a bank holiday — including hours where that session would be closed anyway. Systematically missed valid entries (opportunity cost, not loss) that look random.
findings.fix: Only classify closed_holiday when the session WOULD be in session (`elif is_holiday and open_m <= current_m < close_m`), otherwise plain 'closed'; or scope major_holiday to sessions whose normal hours overlap the query time.

findings.title: holidays.country_holidays() constructed fresh for all 4 countries on every call
findings.impact: Unnecessary allocation/computation on a hot path; the holiday calendars are static per (country, year).
findings.fix: Module-level cache: `@lru_cache` keyed on (country, year) returning the holidays object.

findings.title: Oscillator panel is reserved in osc_types_seen BEFORE the all-NaN skip, desynchronizing panel_ratios from the panels actually plotted
findings.impact: When an oscillator series aligns to all-NaN (e.g. its timestamps fail to parse, or cross-timeframe data starts after the chart window), mpf.plot receives panel_ratios longer than the number of panels actually used — mplfinance raises and the whole chartshot fails, or with multiple oscillators the panels shift/blank. Chart tool errors ripple back as tool failures to the agent.
findings.fix: Compute arr and the NaN check first; only append to osc_types_seen (and derive panel_idx) after confirming the series is plottable.

findings.title: Dual-key read smooth_period / smoothPeriod (snake_case + camelCase) in indicator config
findings.impact: Backward-compat shim the owner wants removed; two spellings of the same config key keep both alive in configs and UI.
findings.fix: Standardize on snake_case `smooth_period`, migrate existing chartshot configs in system.json5, and drop the camelCase fallback.

findings.title: Dual-key read timestamp / time in _align_to_df and _align_bb_to_df
findings.impact: Legacy fallback for a payload key that no producer emits anymore; masks future key typos instead of failing loudly.
findings.fix: Read only "timestamp" in both helpers.

findings.title: Auto filename has second granularity — concurrent chartshots collide, and temp-mode deletion after the first LLM call removes the file the second call still needs
findings.impact: Rare, timing-dependent: one agent occasionally analyzes without the chart it requested (or with the other config's chart if configs differ), with only an ERROR log line as trace.
findings.fix: Include uniqueness in the auto name: uuid4 hex fragment or microseconds + agent_id.

findings.title: filename argument is used unsanitized — path separators escape output_dir or crash relative_to
findings.impact: LLM-supplied filename with separators writes files to arbitrary repo-relative locations and/or crashes the tool after writing; with temp mode the stray file is never cleaned up.
findings.fix: Sanitize: keep only the basename (`Path(filename_arg).name`), reject empty results, enforce '.png' suffix.

findings.title: CHARTSHOT_END is only published on success — failures leave a START without matching END
findings.impact: Any consumer/monitor correlating start/end events (elapsed tracking, in-flight chart gating) sees phantom in-progress chartshots forever; the success field is always True so failure is unobservable on the bus.
findings.fix: try/except around the body publishing CHARTSHOT_END with success=False and the error message before re-raising.

findings.title: DXY path ignores smooth_period and echoes a 'period' that has no effect on the computation
findings.impact: The schema advertises smooth_period for the tool generically; an agent smoothing DXY silently gets raw values. The echoed period implies a lookback semantics that does not exist.
findings.fix: Apply the same smoothing block to dxy_values (after fixing warm-up), or document/return that period and smooth_period are ignored for DXY.

findings.title: with_aa_analysis=true has no effect for the default 'open' filter — repository strips market_context_snapshot/entry_reasoning for get_open_order_book_entries
findings.impact: Agents requesting the open order book with AA analysis (the default) never see entry reasoning or market context for open trades; LLM decisions that were supposed to weigh original entry rationale silently operate without it.
findings.fix: Either use get_order_book_entries + local open-status filter when with_aa_analysis is true, or make the slim stripping opt-in via an arg instead of tying it to the operation name.

findings.title: Dual-field read order_response.get('order_id') or .get('broker_order_id') — 'order_id' is never produced by any broker path
findings.impact: Legacy dual-read the owner wants removed; it also masks the real contract, which contributed to close_position.py reading the wrong keys (finding #4).
findings.fix: Read only `order_response.get("broker_order_id")`.

findings.title: _entry_status/_entry_to_dict carry dead object-vs-dict dual handling — repo responses are always JSON dicts
findings.impact: Dead compat branches obscure the actual data shape and invite the producer/consumer drift this audit is hunting.
findings.fix: Reduce to dict-only handling: `str(e.get("status", ""))` and `d = dict(e); d.pop("market_context_snapshot", None)`.

findings.title: trade_allowed check fails open: missing key defaults to True
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth gap on the money path — a schema drift in the account-status producer would remove the broker-trading-disabled block without any error.
findings.fix: Default to False (fail closed): `if not account_data.get("trade_allowed", False): ...`, or validate the status dict against AccountStatus first.

findings.title: Cross-rate for risk sizing uses the last stored M5 close of the cross pair with no staleness check
findings.impact: quote→account conversion (JPY, GBP, CHF crosses) can use a stale rate; a 2-3% FX move since the stored candle skews `per_unit_risk` and therefore position size — risk_pct silently over/under-shoots. Small, random-seeming sizing drift.
findings.fix: Apply the same _MAX_M5_DATA_AGE freshness check to the cross-pair candle and raise (fail closed, as the existing RuntimeError does for missing data).

findings.title: float(arguments.get('risk_pct', 1.0)) crashes with TypeError if the LLM passes an explicit null risk_pct
findings.impact: A units-based order with `"risk_pct": null` in the tool call dies with an unhandled TypeError after the order-book entry may already be created (line 461 is post-sizing, pre-save; line 133 is during snapshot build inside entry construction) — flaky tool failures.
findings.fix: Use `float(arguments.get("risk_pct") or 1.0)` in both places.

findings.title: Tool description repeats the same sentence twice
findings.impact: Wasted prompt tokens on every LLM call that carries the tool manifest; cosmetic.
findings.fix: Delete one of the two identical sentences.

findings.title: Direct-close request routes by pair_arg but sets instrument=context.pair — two different pair notions in one message
findings.impact: Latent contract drift: any future adapter that starts honoring the pair hint (e.g. symbol-suffix mapping) will act on the wrong pair.
findings.fix: Send `instrument=pair_arg` (the same value used for routing).

findings.title: Returned 'closed_units' is the requested partial size (None for full closes) rather than what was actually closed
findings.impact: Agents reading the tool result see closed_units=null on every full close and must guess; combined with remaining_units always null (finding #4) the close result gives no usable size information.
findings.fix: Populate closed_units from the broker response (response['order']['units']) and remaining_units from local entry units minus closed units.

findings.title: append is a non-atomic read-modify-write over two bus round-trips — concurrent appends silently lose updates
findings.impact: Two agents appending behavior extensions (e.g. a risk instruction 'never trade during NFP') to the same target agent at the same time → one instruction silently vanishes. The target agent then behaves without that constraint for weeks. No error anywhere; classic hard-to-detect drift.
findings.fix: Add an atomic `append_sub_prompt(agent, text)` repository operation (single SQL UPDATE ... SET prompt = prompt || ?) and call that instead of get+set.

findings.title: Future registered before publish, but publish is OUTSIDE the try/finally — an exception from bus.publish leaks the future in bus._pending_futures forever
