findings.impact: Each such failure leaks one dict entry (unbounded growth over weeks) and, if a stale response later arrives with that correlation_id, it is consumed by the dead future instead of being routed. Low probability (payloads are statically well-formed) but a permanent leak when it fires.
findings.fix: Move `await bus.publish(...)` inside the try block (register → try: publish + wait_for → finally: cancel_response_future) in both agent_bridge.execute and tools/base.bus_request.

findings.title: AgentBridgeTool.execute re-implements the register/publish/wait_for/cancel pattern of tools/base.bus_request instead of reusing it
findings.impact: Twin implementations drift: fixes applied to bus_request (e.g. moving publish into try) will not reach the bridge path and vice versa.
findings.fix: Refactor execute() to call bus_request(context, EventType.AGENT_QUERY, target_agent_id, payload, timeout=self._timeout) and keep only the BRIDGE_CALL_START/END envelope locally.

findings.title: _expand_bridge_tool_config error messages use 1-based indices in 'targets[{idx}]' — off-by-one relative to the actual JSON array
findings.impact: Operator fixing config edits the wrong array element; renumbered tool names on config edits break agents' learned tool references. Diagnostic-quality only.
findings.fix: Use enumerate(targets) (0-based) for the error text, or say 'entry #%d (1-based)'.

findings.title: Explicit hoursBack=0 / hoursFor=0 silently coerced to defaults via `or`
findings.impact: LLM asking for strictly-future events (hoursBack: 0) still receives events up to 1h in the past and may treat an already-released figure as upcoming — subtly wrong news assessment.
findings.fix: Use `float(arguments.get("hoursBack", 1))` guarding only None: `v = arguments.get("hoursBack"); hours_back = 1.0 if v is None else float(v)`.

findings.title: matches_time_filter compares event time against aware bounds — any event whose time_server lacks a UTC offset raises TypeError and kills the whole get_news call
findings.impact: Any EA update/reinstall that writes naive timestamps (MQL5 TimeToString default has NO offset) makes get_news throw TypeError on every call from then on; the agent silently trades without news awareness. Check: format contract of the EA writing economic_calendar.json.
findings.fix: In matches_time_filter, normalize: if event_time.tzinfo is None, attach the configured broker tz (or skip with a logged warning) before comparing.

findings.title: _broker_adapter_id helper duplicated verbatim in 9 locations across the codebase
findings.impact: Any change to the adapter member-ID scheme must be replicated 9 times; one missed copy silently routes trading requests to a non-existent member (direct-target messages are DROPPED by the bus, bus.py:326-329, and the caller just times out).
findings.fix: Export the function from openforexai/adapters/brokers/base.py (it already exists there) and import it everywhere else.

findings.title: append concatenates without any separator — old and new prompt text fuse into one token stream
findings.impact: "...never risk more than 2%" + append "Always avoid news spikes" → "...never risk more than 2%Always avoid news spikes". The fused sentence can change how the target agent's LLM parses BOTH instructions — subtle behavioral drift with no error.
findings.fix: Join with a newline: `prompt = f"{current}\n{prompt}" if current else prompt` (or require the caller to include separators and document it).

findings.title: LLM-supplied context dict is spread AFTER the standard alarm fields and can overwrite severity/agent_id/pair/timestamp in the emitted payload
findings.impact: A critical alarm can appear as info (or attributed to the wrong agent/pair) in the MonitoringBus and notification channels — humans never see it. Divergence between the tool's return value and the emitted event.
findings.fix: Spread extra_context FIRST (or nest it: "context": extra_context) so canonical fields win.

findings.title: Tool description promises a 'bias' field but the returned decision record contains 'decision', not 'bias'
findings.impact: The LLM is told to expect record['bias']; when reasoning over the tool result it may misread which field carries the directional call, or report 'bias missing'. LLM-facing contract mismatch.
findings.fix: Change the description to name the actual field 'decision' (and the other real keys).

findings.title: Swallowed system.json5 load failure produces a misleading 'not configured' error and silently falls back to UTC offset 3
findings.impact: During a config hot-save race the tool reports a wrong root cause; operator hunts a nonexistent config-key problem. If only the offset were needed it would proceed with a possibly wrong hard-coded 3.
findings.fix: Let the config load error propagate (or include the load error in the RuntimeError); better: use ConfigService instead of re-reading the file (see the re-read finding).

findings.title: ui_utc default is 0 in _apply_event_log_tz but 3 in /system/ui-settings — event-log and UI timestamps disagree by 3 h when ui_utc is unset
findings.impact: With no ui_utc in system.json5, the persistent event log renders times at UTC+0 while the UI renders live times at UTC+3. When correlating a bad trade against the event log, timestamps appear 3 hours apart — misleads incident analysis of exactly the rare-loss investigations the owner is doing.
findings.fix: Use one shared default constant (single accessor function for ui_utc) in both places.

findings.title: Reconcile never checks PENDING entries against broker closed-trade history — fast fill+close leaves entries PENDING forever on this path
findings.impact: Entries for orders that filled and closed between syncs stay PENDING in the order book indefinitely when viewed/reconciled through the API; their realized P&L is never backfilled on this path.
findings.fix: Include "PENDING" in the closed-trade lookup set (or call find_closed_trade_by_sync_key for PENDING entries), mirroring base.py's orphan recovery — ideally by sharing the code (see duplicate finding).

findings.title: ask_agent cleans up the pending response future only on timeout — other exceptions leak futures in the bus registry
findings.impact: Slow accumulation of dead futures in the bus's pending map over weeks of uptime; a late response resolves a dead future silently.
findings.fix: Wrap in try/finally with `_bus.cancel_response_future(future_key)` in the finally; use `asyncio.get_running_loop()`.

findings.title: setup_query_handler is a documented no-op kept for backward compatibility, still imported and called by server.py
findings.impact: Dead compatibility surface the owner explicitly wants removed; misleads readers into thinking a query handler is being wired.
findings.fix: Delete the function and remove the import/call in openforexai/management/server.py.

findings.title: Migration aliases register_agent/unregister_agent still used (bus.py marks them 'kept during migration')
findings.impact: Two names for one concept; the migration is never finished and every new reader must learn both.
findings.fix: Switch all callers to register_member/unregister_member and delete the aliases from bus.py.

findings.title: Dead code cluster: _resolve_agent_runtime_context, _llm_services, _ws_safe_payload, unused locals, duplicate global declaration, unused _CONFIG_FILES values
findings.impact: Dead surface that misleads maintenance (e.g. one might 'fix' _resolve_agent_runtime_context believing it is the live pair-resolution path) and hides the actually-used twin _resolve_agent_snapshot_context.
findings.fix: Delete _resolve_agent_runtime_context, _llm_services (param llm_services in build_app too, unless a future use is imminent), inline _ws_safe_payload, remove the unused context locals, dedupe the global statement, and make _CONFIG_FILES a frozenset of names.

findings.title: Chartshot GET and DELETE endpoints duplicate an identical system.json5 disk-read block and bypass the in-memory config
findings.impact: Redundant blocking disk I/O per image request; two copies to keep in sync; possible output_dir mismatch when chartshot.output_dir lives in config.default.json5 (raw read misses it → 404s for existing chartshots).
findings.fix: Extract one helper `_chartshot_dir()` that reads `_system_config.get("chartshot", {}).get("output_dir", "data/chartshots")` and use it in both endpoints.

findings.title: llm_checker re-resolves (and re-reads from disk) the LLM module config on every tool turn; float max_tokens silently dropped
findings.impact: Wasted blocking I/O on the event loop during checker runs; a float-typed max_tokens in a module config is silently ignored, so the provider default applies without any warning.
findings.fix: Hoist the _resolve_llm_checker_params call out of the loop; accept `isinstance(max_toks, (int, float))` and cast.

findings.title: _DEBUG_LOG_PATH is CWD-relative while every other path in the module is project-root-anchored
findings.impact: When the service is started from a different CWD (systemd, wrapper, task scheduler), a stray logs/ tree is created elsewhere and frontend debug output lands where nobody looks. Also blocking file I/O in an async handler.
findings.fix: Use `_project_root() / "logs" / "frontend_debug.log"` (and consider asyncio.to_thread for the append).

findings.title: Path-containment via str.startswith is prefix-unsafe in five file endpoints (currently masked by filename regexes)
findings.impact: Latent traversal guard that does not guard; one regex tweak away from arbitrary file read/delete (DELETE /chartshots/... unlinks the resolved target).
findings.fix: Replace all five startswith checks with `target.resolve().relative_to(base.resolve())` in try/except ValueError, as done elsewhere in the file.

findings.title: list_agents iterates agents config without the isinstance(dict) guard used by every other consumer
findings.impact: A non-dict agents entry (typo/comment artifact in system.json5) makes GET /agents and the config-refresh trigger 500 with AttributeError while other endpoints keep working — inconsistent tolerance of the same config.
findings.fix: Add the same `isinstance(cfg, dict)` guard in list_agents and _trigger_agent_config_refresh.

findings.title: execute_tool silently falls back to an arbitrary first connected broker when none was requested
findings.impact: With multiple connected brokers (e.g. demo + live), a /tools/execute call without broker_name runs against whichever broker happened to connect first — a manual test order can land on the live account.
findings.fix: Only auto-select when exactly one broker is connected; otherwise return 400 requiring an explicit broker_name for tools that use the broker context.

findings.title: Unknown status_filter values silently return ALL order-book entries instead of erroring
findings.impact: A client/UI sending a mis-cased filter believes it sees only e.g. closed trades but gets everything — counts and P&L aggregations built on the response are wrong with no error signal.
findings.fix: Whitelist explicitly: raise HTTPException(422) when status_filter is not in {'all','open'} ∪ exact_status_map.

findings.title: Orderbook candle window falls back to the full unrelated candle set when the window is empty
findings.impact: The trade-detail chart for older entries renders a candle range that does not contain the trade at all; entry/exit markers appear against wrong price context, misleading post-trade analysis.
findings.fix: Return `[]` (or an explicit 'no data for window' response) instead of `windowed or candles`, or fetch candles by time range instead of newest-N.

findings.title: /ws/monitoring is completely unauthenticated and streams full LLM prompts, tool results and trade payloads
findings.impact: Even when MANAGEMENT_API_KEY is configured, anyone who can reach the port reads live trading telemetry — account activity, LLM prompts (may contain strategy), order details.
findings.fix: Validate the API key inside ws_monitoring from `websocket.query_params` or the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol/first message before accept(), and close with 4401 otherwise.

findings.title: Chartshot routes re-read and re-parse system.json5 from disk on every request — with the logic duplicated in both routes
findings.impact: Every chartshot preview blocks the trading event loop with disk IO and a full JSON5 parse of the master config; duplicated logic invites divergence.
findings.fix: Read `(_system_config.get("chartshot") or {}).get("output_dir")` from memory in a single shared helper used by both routes.

findings.title: llm_checker re-reads the LLM module config file from disk on every tool turn inside the loop
findings.impact: Unnecessary blocking IO on the shared trading loop during checker sessions; latency spikes proportional to tool turns.
findings.fix: Hoist the `_resolve_llm_checker_params` call out of the loop (its inputs are constant per request).

findings.title: GET /orderbook performs live broker network calls (open positions + per-entry 30-day deal-history scans) on every poll
findings.impact: A UI polling the order book every few seconds hammers the broker API with redundant history scans (worsened by the OrderStatus NameError making entries permanently 'unconfirmed', so the same failing reconciles repeat forever), adding latency to the route and risking broker-side rate limiting that then affects real trading calls.
findings.fix: Move reconciliation to a periodic background task (or throttle per entry via last_broker_sync) instead of doing it inline in the GET handler.

findings.title: _llm_services is populated in build_app but never read anywhere
findings.impact: Dead state and a dead `llm_services` build_app parameter mislead readers into thinking the API uses these service handles.
findings.fix: Remove `_llm_services`, the global declaration at line 4442, the assignment at 4462, and the `llm_services` parameter (and its caller argument in management/server.py).

findings.title: Assorted dead code: no-op _ws_safe_payload with unused param, unused context locals, shadowing re-imports of AgentMessage/EventType
findings.impact: Noise that obscures the real logic; the identity wrapper suggests payload sanitization happens when it does not.
findings.fix: Inline `event.payload` in `_build_ws_message`, delete the unused locals and the duplicate function-level imports.

findings.title: Candle-to-dict serialization and the timeframe whitelist are copy-pasted three times each
findings.impact: A future field or timeframe addition must be made in 3-4 places; divergence produces UI endpoints returning different candle shapes.
findings.fix: Extract `_serialize_candle(c)` and a module-level `_VALID_TIMEFRAMES` frozenset reused everywhere (also by _timeframe_delta).

findings.title: M5 trigger candle payload building/rounding logic duplicated across api.py (twice) and the broker adapter base
findings.impact: Three payload producers for one event shape: any change to the canonical adapter payload (new key, precision change) silently desynchronizes the manual-trigger and snapshot-preview paths — the exact producer/consumer shape drift class under audit.
findings.fix: Extract one shared `build_m5_trigger_payload(broker_short_name, candle, *, force_run=False)` helper (e.g. in models or messaging) and use it in the adapter and both api.py sites.

findings.title: Frontend debug log path is CWD-relative while every other file path is project-root-anchored; endpoint appends unbounded, unauthenticated-by-default content synchronously
findings.impact: Started from a different working directory (service manager, scheduled task) the log lands in an unexpected location or fails; the file grows without bound; sync IO on the trading loop.
findings.fix: Anchor with `_project_root() / "logs" / "frontend_debug.log"`, cap size or rotate, and use asyncio.to_thread for the append.

findings.title: llm_checker hasattr fallback branch building Anthropic-format messages by hand is unreachable dead compat code
findings.impact: Dead dual-path kept for backward compatibility (owner wants these removed); latent divergent-twin bug if ever reached.
findings.fix: Delete the else branch (lines 3410-3433) and the hasattr check; require the methods on AbstractLLMProvider (declare them on the port) and call unconditionally.

findings.title: save_llm_context writes non-atomically (direct write_text) unlike every other save endpoint, and silently writes empty content when the body key is missing
findings.impact: A crash mid-write corrupts/truncates an LLM context file; a client-side key typo silently erases it — the assistant then answers with an empty system context and nobody is alerted.
findings.fix: Use a Pydantic model with required `content: str` and write via _write_text_file.

findings.title: Python syntax validation implemented twice in the same file (ast.parse vs compile)
findings.impact: Divergent behavior between the editor's validate button and the snapshot-helpers save check (different error formats; compile also catches some late-stage errors ast.parse misses), confusing operators and inviting drift.
findings.fix: Have _validate_python_source delegate to one shared checker that returns (line, column, message) and reuse it in both places.

findings.title: build_app declares `global _active_agents` twice
findings.impact: Pure hygiene; harmless but signals copy-paste drift in the globals wiring.
findings.fix: Remove the second `_active_agents` from line 4443.

findings.title: GET /events/{id}/trace returns the full server traceback in the HTTP 500 detail — debug leftover / information disclosure
findings.impact: Leaks internal file paths, code structure and library versions to any API client on error; inconsistent error contract vs all other endpoints.
findings.fix: Return a short detail string and log the traceback server-side instead.

findings.title: save_event_schemas / reload_event_schemas reach into the EventBus private attribute _event_schemas
findings.impact: Encapsulation break — a rename of the private field silently breaks two endpoints; hygiene only.
findings.fix: Add a public schema_count property (or have reload_event_schemas return the count) and use it here.

findings.title: tags round-trip shape mismatch: API accepts list[str] on write but returns a JSON-encoded string on read
findings.impact: Every consumer must know to json.loads the tags field; any client treating the documented list shape (e.g. `doc.tags.includes(x)`) silently does substring matching on a string instead — wrong filter results, no error.
findings.fix: Decode in the repository (or router) before returning: `row["tags"] = json.loads(row["tags"] or "[]")` and `row["is_folder"] = bool(row["is_folder"])` for list and get endpoints.

findings.title: search limit clamped only upward — negative limit means unlimited in SQLite; and repository swallows all search exceptions
findings.impact: A negative limit returns the entire KB in one response; real database errors are masked as empty search results, hiding corruption until unrelated symptoms appear.
findings.fix: Clamp both sides: `limit=max(1, min(limit, 50))` (or Query(ge=1, le=50)). In kb_search, narrow the except to sqlite FTS syntax errors (sqlite3.OperationalError on MATCH) and let other exceptions propagate.

findings.title: Routing rules without a string 'id' are appended on every re-import — repeated imports of the same package duplicate rules unboundedly
findings.impact: event_routing.json5 grows with duplicate rules on every re-import. RoutingTable.resolve dedups targets (routing.py:196-211) so no double delivery, but rule count and evaluation cost grow, and priority ordering among duplicated rules becomes ambiguous when one copy is later edited.
findings.fix: Also dedupe by structural identity for id-less rules (e.g. key on (event, from, to)), or require ids at validate_package time for packaged routing rules.

findings.title: Deprecated-key handling kept for backward compatibility: agent_tools.agents warning and '@handlers' target support in export filtering
findings.impact: Per the owner's directive all compat shims must be removed. The '@handlers' export path actively produces packages containing rules the runtime discards, i.e. dead cargo.
findings.fix: Drop the deprecated agent_tools.agents warning branch (make it a hard error or ignore silently after the migration window), and stop exporting '@handlers' rules entirely (remove handler_relevant, lines 116-119) once RoutingTable support is deleted.

findings.title: Package import rewrites the whole hand-maintained system.json5 via json.dumps — all comments in the JSON5 file are destroyed even when importing a single agent
findings.impact: One package import silently strips every comment from system.json5, event_routing.json5 and agent_tools.json5 — documentation the operator relies on (per the comment-preserving text-edit endpoints) is irreversibly lost.
findings.fix: Either perform a text-level merge (patch only the touched sections into the raw JSON5 text) or, at minimum, back up the original file (system.json5.bak) before overwriting and warn in the import response that comments were dropped.

findings.title: _deserialize_args swallows Pydantic validation errors with except-pass on money-path saves (save_order_book_entry, save_account_status)
findings.impact: When a producer sends a slightly wrong order-book payload (e.g. renamed field), the persisted-trade write fails with a cryptic secondary error or writes unvalidated data; the root-cause field name never appears in any log, making the intermittent 'trade executed but not in DB' incidents nearly undiagnosable.
findings.fix: Log the validation exception (operation, key, error) and return an error response immediately instead of passing the raw dict through: `error = f"invalid {key} for {operation}: {exc}"`.

findings.title: Dual repository/data_container API kept 'for backward compatibility' with a shared aliased dict — owner wants all compat shims removed
findings.impact: Same name key ('sqlite') can be bound to two different classes depending on import order (SQLiteRepository vs SQLiteDataContainer) with no error — behavior of get_repository('sqlite') is import-order dependent. Pure maintenance hazard plus explicit compat debt the owner wants gone.
findings.fix: Pick one API (data_container per the docstring's own 'preferred'), delete the other three methods and the alias, give each registry its own dict, and update bootstrap.py:90 and adapters/*/__init__.py accordingly.

findings.title: ConfigService registers via legacy bus.register_agent alias ('kept during migration') while RepositoryService uses register_member — divergent twin usage of a compat shim
findings.impact: No functional failure today, but the half-finished migration keeps two names for one concept; owner explicitly wants compat aliases removed. Risk of future divergence if register_agent ever gains agent-specific behavior.
findings.fix: Switch config_service.py:47 and agents/agent.py:97 to register_member, then delete register_agent/unregister_agent aliases from EventBus.

findings.title: Single serial handler loop awaits repository call with no timeout — one hung DB call stalls ALL repo traffic system-wide
findings.impact: A single slow/hung PostgreSQL query (network blip, lock) freezes the only repo worker; every broker sync, order-book read and account-status save across all brokers times out until the query returns — trade persistence silently drops for minutes.
findings.fix: Wrap the repository call in `async with asyncio.timeout(...)` (configurable, e.g. 30s) and return an error response on timeout; optionally handle requests in per-message tasks to avoid head-of-line blocking.

findings.title: modules["broker"] is resolved (fresh disk read per request) but no consumer uses it — and its shape diverges from the live broker config (missing bootstrap's broker_utc_offset_hours injection)
findings.impact: Dead disk I/O on every config request today; latent timezone-divergence trap (broker-local vs UTC candle timestamps) the moment someone starts consuming the payload field.
findings.fix: Remove the modules["broker"] resolution from _handle_request, or if it must stay, apply the same broker_utc_offset_hours injection bootstrap applies.

findings.title: Shallow copy of agent config shares nested mutable dicts/lists between the live system config and agent/tool code
findings.impact: A tool or agent that mutates its config dict (e.g. annotating state into it) silently corrupts the master in-memory system config; the corrupted values are then served to other agents on config refresh and can be persisted to disk on the next config save. Classic weeks-later, unreproducible drift.
findings.fix: Use copy.deepcopy(agent_cfg) (configs are small; per-request cost negligible) in _handle_request and _handle_ec_request.

findings.title: KeyboardInterrupt handler calls os._exit(0) — brokers never disconnected, repository never closed, pending event-persist tasks dropped
findings.impact: Operator Ctrl-C during an active session can lose the last order-book/account writes and leaves broker sessions dangling; the DB then disagrees with the broker on open positions at next start.
findings.fix: Catch KeyboardInterrupt, cancel the TaskGroup gracefully (asyncio.run already propagates cancellation), await broker disconnects and repository.close(), then return normally; use sys.exit(0) instead of os._exit.

findings.title: bootstrap() return annotation declares a 5-tuple and the docstring a 4-tuple incl. management_server — actual return is a 9-tuple without management_server
findings.impact: Type checkers and readers are actively misled about the bootstrap contract; a refactor trusting the annotation would unpack wrongly.
findings.fix: Correct the annotation to the real 9-tuple (or better, return a small dataclass) and fix docstring steps 10-11.

findings.title: broker_candle_utc_offset_hours read from system config twice with identical expressions
findings.impact: Two copies of the same default-bearing lookup can drift (e.g. someone changes the default 3 in one place only), silently splitting the timezone offset between brokers and agents — a timezone-class defect waiting to happen.
findings.fix: Compute once at the top of bootstrap() and reuse the variable for both broker injection (line 161) and agent construction (line 309).

findings.title: REPO_REQUEST request/response-future logic implemented twice (tools/base.py repo_request vs adapters/brokers/base.py _repo_request)
findings.impact: Divergent twins: timeouts differ (15s vs 60s), error handling differs, and fixes applied to one (e.g. the whitelist errors) won't reach the other. The UnboundLocalError variant turns a clear validation error into a confusing crash inside broker code.
findings.fix: Extract a single shared bus_request/repo_request helper (tools/base.py already has bus_request) and have brokers use it; assign future_key before the try block.

findings.title: ImportRules honored only from the default config; an ImportRules key in system.json5 is ignored for merging yet leaks into the merged result
findings.impact: User-authored replace rules in system.json5 are silently ignored (arrays keep merging append-style), and a junk ImportRules key pollutes the runtime config and any config export/save round-trip.
findings.fix: Also read/merge ImportRules from the custom file (or explicitly reject it), and pop the key from custom_cfg before merging.

findings.title: _run_ec_safe and _run_agent_safe are structurally identical twin wrappers
findings.impact: Divergence risk: a fix to crash reporting applied to one wrapper (e.g. adding restart logic) will silently miss the other.
findings.fix: Collapse into one generic `_run_member_safe(coro_factory, member_id, prefix, monitoring_bus)` helper.

findings.title: Synchronous disk I/O (json5 parse via Path.read_text) inside the async event loop on every agent config request
findings.impact: During config refresh storms (management API broadcasting AGENT_CONFIG_RESPONSE to many agents) the loop stalls for the cumulative parse time, delaying candle trigger delivery by milliseconds to tens of milliseconds.
findings.fix: Run load_json_config via asyncio.to_thread() in _resolve_module_config, keeping fresh-read semantics.

findings.title: TradeOrder.approved_by ('supervisor agent ID') is always the hardcoded literal 'supervisor' at every construction site
findings.impact: The field records no information; audit trails claiming supervisor approval are fabricated placeholder data.
findings.fix: Either populate it from the actual approving agent in the approval flow, or remove the field and the placeholder writes.

findings.title: normalize_log_level silently collapses every level except DEBUG to INFO — WARNING/ERROR configuration is ignored
findings.impact: Operators configuring WARNING/ERROR get full INFO noise (or believe they raised verbosity when they did not); misconfiguration is silent.
findings.fix: Validate against the full set {DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL} and return the requested level (falling back to INFO with a warning for unknown values).

findings.title: One failed event page aborts the whole news batch — no partial-result tolerance
findings.impact: Around clustered high-impact releases (many events → many sequential requests → rate limiting most likely) the agent gets a tool error instead of the news it needs, precisely when news matters most. Intermittent, environment-dependent, never reproducible locally.
findings.fix: Catch per-event fetch/parse failures, append an explicit '<!-- fetch failed for event X -->' section, and continue; only fail if ALL events failed.

findings.title: create_event_markdown default output path is relative to process CWD and collides across languages
findings.impact: Stray .md files pollute the process CWD; a German fetch destroys the English artifact of the same event without warning. Mission-focus 'file naming collision' confirmed.
findings.fix: Require out_file (like create_events_markdown does) or default into a configured output dir and include the language in the default filename.

findings.title: normalize_int_list raises uncaught ValueError on non-numeric input while the per-event importance parse swallows the same error
findings.impact: An agent passing importance_codes=['high'] gets an unhandled ValueError from deep inside the filter instead of a parameter-validation error or a graceful skip.
findings.fix: Wrap int(value) in try/except and raise a descriptive ValueError naming the parameter, or skip invalid entries consistently.

findings.title: Duplicate and shadowed imports: Path imported twice at module level; requests/markdownify/re/Path all re-imported inside functions
findings.impact: Pure hygiene: dead top-level imports plus three redundant local import blocks obscure the real dependency surface (bs4 is only imported locally, so a missing bs4 install passes import time and blows up mid-trade at first news fetch).
findings.fix: Keep one canonical top-level import block (json, re, unicodedata, requests, deepcopy, datetime, Path, typing, BeautifulSoup, md); delete line 16 and all function-local imports.

findings.title: --hours default is 10 but help text and script description both claim 4
findings.impact: Anyone running the script per its --help gets a 10-hour (plus 1 back) window while believing it is 4 hours — wrong mental model of upcoming news exposure.
findings.fix: Align default and help text (pick one value) and document the 1-hour lookback.

findings.title: listEvents.py is an unused dev script inside the package tree with a flat import that breaks package importability and a hardcoded machine-specific path
findings.impact: Dead developer scaffolding shipped inside the package: it cannot be imported as a module, is tied to one developer's machine, and any pkgutil/test-collection walk of the package errors on it.
findings.fix: Move it to a scripts/ or tools-dev directory outside the openforexai package (fixing the import to the package path), or delete it.

findings.title: id2md.py has no __main__ guard — argparse.parse_args() and a live HTTP scrape execute at import time
findings.impact: Package-walking tooling dies with SystemExit or performs network IO/file writes during import; combined with the CWD-relative default output of create_event_markdown (mql5_calendar_lib.py:308) this can drop stray .md files anywhere.
findings.fix: Wrap the body in `def main(): ...` + `if __name__ == "__main__": main()`, use the package import path, or move the script out of the package (see listEvents finding).

findings.title: Sibling CLI scripts use divergent defaults for the same calendar file: id2md defaults to CWD-relative 'economic_calendar.json', listEvents to a hardcoded absolute MetaQuotes path
findings.impact: Running id2md.py from the repo root fails with FileNotFoundError (or worse, picks up a stale copied calendar file lying in CWD and produces markdown for outdated events without any warning).
findings.fix: Point both scripts at the config value (system.json5 news.economic_calendar_file) or at least the same default.

findings.title: MT5 candle timestamps are relabeled broker-local tz while OANDA candles are UTC — VWAP daily reset boundary differs per broker
findings.impact: The same VWAP(0) request returns values computed over different day windows depending on broker; resampled D1/H4 bucket boundaries and session labels drift the same way — subtle per-broker indicator disagreement.
findings.fix: Pick one convention (UTC everywhere, with broker offset applied only where wall-clock day boundaries are needed) and make OANDA honor broker_utc_offset_hours or MT5 emit UTC.

findings.title: DXY component pair list defined in three places
findings.impact: Adding/removing a component (e.g. USDSEK) in one list but not the others silently desynchronizes data-collection loops from the DXY formula: the broker would not track a pair the formula needs, making synthetic_dxy return None/stale forever.
findings.fix: Single home in data/indicators.py (the weights dict is authoritative); derive DXY_COMPONENT_PAIRS and DXY_COMPONENTS from _DXY_WEIGHTS.keys().

findings.title: Chartshot output_dir resolution + filename validation + traversal check duplicated verbatim in GET and DELETE routes, and a third time in the chartshot tool
findings.impact: Three copies of a security-relevant path check; fixing a traversal edge case (e.g. case-insensitive prefix on Windows) in one route but not the other leaves an inconsistency. Also sync disk IO per request in async routes.
findings.fix: One `_resolve_chartshot_dir()` + `_safe_chartshot_path(filename)` helper used by both routes and (for output_dir) the tool.

findings.title: Broker-result → order-book-updates field extraction duplicated between _build_sync_close_updates_dict and _resolve_orphaned_entry
findings.impact: The two close-reconciliation paths already differ (fill_price only in one); further drift means orphan-recovered trades and sync-detected closes record different P&L fields.
findings.fix: Extract one _updates_from_broker_result(broker_result, include_fill_price=...) helper.

findings.title: Row→model converters and schema DDL duplicated wholesale between SQLite and PostgreSQL repositories
findings.impact: Every schema/field change must be made twice; a single missed copy makes the two backends return differently-shaped OrderBookEntry objects (the sync_confirmed/pnl_pips columns already require careful mirroring).
findings.fix: Extract shared row→model converters (dict-based) into a common module used by both adapters; keep only SQL dialect differences local.

findings.title: OrderBookEntry.pnl_pips is persisted, migrated and re-read but no code path ever computes/writes it
findings.impact: DB column and API field that are always NULL; consumers (UI/optimization) that trust the field silently get no pip-P&L data.
findings.fix: Either compute pnl_pips in _build_sync_close_updates_dict / close_position (needs the unused normalizer.pips()) or drop the field/column.

findings.title: '@handlers' legacy routing target still supported in RoutingTable although the bus explicitly removed handler-based delivery
findings.impact: Docs and code advertise a delivery path that no longer exists; a rule using @handlers is silently a no-op (messages matched by it go nowhere).
findings.fix: Delete the @handlers branch, the docstring section, and treat @handlers rules as config errors on load.

findings.title: sanitize_agent_tool_config strips deprecated 'context_tiers'/'tier_tools' keys at runtime — migration shim that hides stale config
findings.impact: Deprecated keys are silently swallowed on every config request forever instead of being rejected once; users keep editing dead keys.
findings.fix: Turn the silent strip into a one-time validation warning/error on config save, then remove the shim.

findings.title: llm_complete duplicates llm_complete_with_tools almost entirely; module also carries an unused uuid import
findings.impact: The future-leak fix (see separate finding) must be applied twice; response parsing already differs (complete builds LLMResponse inline vs _payload_to_response_with_tools).
findings.fix: Implement llm_complete as a thin wrapper over a shared _llm_request(method, payload, timeout) core; drop the uuid import.

findings.title: _compute_dxy assigns ref_candles 'to attach timestamps' but emits timestamp: None for every value
findings.impact: Dead variable plus an output-shape inconsistency: DXY series lack timestamps while all other indicators have them, so snapshot transform scripts keying on timestamps treat DXY differently.
findings.fix: Use ref_candles tail to fill timestamps (mirroring lines 111-126) or delete the assignment and the misleading comment.

findings.title: utils/metrics.py is a stub module never called from anywhere — counters/gauges/histograms are no-op bodies
findings.impact: Suggests metrics exist when nothing is instrumented.
findings.fix: Delete the module (or actually wire it up).

findings.title: EMASlopePlugin description states '× 1 000 for JPY pairs' but the code divides by 0.01 (× 100)
findings.impact: This description is fed verbatim to the LLM as tool documentation; the model may rescale JPY slope values by the wrong factor when reasoning.
findings.fix: Correct the description to '× 100 for JPY pairs' (and fix SMASlope's description to match once pip logic is centralized).

findings.title: M5-slot/null-candle helpers duplicated between DataContainer and BrokerBase (plus _broker_adapter_id duplicated in 6 modules)
findings.impact: A format change to the adapter member-ID or M5 boundary logic must be edited in 6-7 places; any missed spot silently breaks direct bus targeting for that tool.
findings.fix: Move both helpers into one shared module (e.g. messaging/agent_id.py already exists for ID logic).

findings.title: 13 EventTypes are never published anywhere: SIGNAL_APPROVED/REJECTED, ORDER_PLACED, POSITION_OPENED/CLOSED, RISK_BREACH, ANALYSIS_REQUESTED, OPTIMIZATION_COMPLETE, PROMPT_UPDATED, INDICATOR_REQUEST/RESPONSE, SWING_LEVELS_REQUEST/RESPONSE, ORDER_BOOK_CLOSE_REASONING
findings.impact: Dead enum members and dead schema entries mislead — UI routing editors and docs offer events that can never fire; the messaging.py:33-36 payload comment for order_book_sync_discrepancy also promises keys (pair, close_price, pnl) the producer (base.py:781-787) does not send.
findings.fix: Remove unpublished EventTypes + their schema entries, or wire them; fix the ORDER_BOOK_SYNC_DISCREPANCY payload comment to match the producer.

findings.title: execute_all/visible_specs carry 'Unused compatibility parameter' token budgets — the agent's context_budget_tokens config is therefore dead
findings.impact: Operators configuring context_budget_tokens get no behaviour change; misleading dead plumbing through the hottest code path.
findings.fix: Remove the parameters, the agent-side budget computation and the config key, or reinstate real gating.

findings.title: Tools targeting `{BROKER}-ALL___-AD-ADPT` hit an unregistered bus member — guaranteed 20 s timeout for agents without a context pair
findings.impact: Any GA/pair-less agent calling get_open_positions/get_account_status (or modify without a pair) stalls 20-30 s and then errors, though the broker is healthy.
findings.fix: Register one broker-wide `-ALL___-AD-ADPT` member per adapter in start_background_tasks, or route to any registered pair member of that broker.

findings.title: Order-book lookup after a close uses context.pair even when the closed position belongs to the pair passed as argument
findings.impact: Closing a position of another pair leaves its order-book entry un-updated (no AGENT_CLOSED, no reasoning) until the sync loop mislabels it SYNC_DETECTED.
findings.fix: Query with pair=None (broker-wide) and match on broker_order_id.

findings.title: Shielded LLM futures are never cancelled/cleaned on non-timeout failures — pending-future entries leak in the bus registry
findings.impact: Slow leak of futures/dict entries keyed by message id over weeks of runtime; a later message that accidentally reuses a correlation id would resolve a stale future.
findings.fix: Use try/finally around the await (as bus_request does) and drop the shield or cancel the shielded future explicitly.

findings.title: Timestamp serialization styles diverge across the codebase: strftime('...Z'), isoformat().replace('+00:00','Z'), and plain isoformat('+00:00')
findings.impact: Same field ('timestamp') appears in three formats depending on producer and broker; brittle string-prefix comparisons and confusing LLM inputs (mixed Z/+03:00 in one snapshot).
findings.fix: One helper (e.g. utils.time_utils.to_iso_utc) that first does astimezone(UTC) then isoformat, used everywhere.

findings.title: Two divergent session implementations: naive UTC-hour detect_session vs zoneinfo/holiday-aware get_session_status
findings.impact: The 'session' the LLM sees in the snapshot can contradict the session gate that decided to run the agent, and both disagree with the session_status tool output — divergent-twin inconsistency.
findings.fix: Make detect_session delegate to get_session_status (or delete it after the is_market_open fix).

findings.title: reasoning_effort accepted 'for port compatibility' but silently dropped by OpenAI and Anthropic adapters while Azure honors it
findings.impact: An operator configuring reasoning_effort on an OpenAI (non-Azure) module gets no error and no effect — the model runs at default effort, degrading/altering trading decisions relative to what was configured and tested on Azure.
findings.fix: In OpenAILLMProvider, forward reasoning_effort to chat.completions.create for reasoning models (mirror azure.py's handling incl. temperature/max_tokens conflicts); in AnthropicProvider either map to thinking budget or raise/log a clear 'unsupported parameter' warning instead of a silent noqa drop.

findings.title: Legacy saved-filter format migration (mode/negated → per-rule join) kept in normaliseSavedMonitorFilters
findings.impact: Owner explicitly wants all backward-compat shims removed; this one silently reinterprets old configs and hides schema drift in system.json5.
findings.fix: One-time migrate saved_filters in system.json5 to the per-rule join format, then reduce the mapper to a strict-shape parse that rejects/ignores unknown legacy fields.

findings.title: Hidden 'test' top section kept 'for type completeness' plus commented-out monitoring stream in AgentChat
findings.impact: Dead navigation branch and commented-out code accumulate; 'kept for' comments are exactly the class the owner wants purged.
findings.fix: Remove 'test' from the TopSection union, DEFAULT_SUB, the switch case, and the HANDBOOK_FILE remnants; delete the commented-out useMonitoringStream line in AgentChat.tsx.

findings.title: Broker decision fallback auto-executes trades parsed from free-form LLM text when no tool call ran — verify against fail-closed policy
findings.impact: A model that merely DESCRIBES a hypothetical decision in JSON (e.g. quoting the schema in its reasoning) can trigger a real order without ever calling the tool. Given the owner's documented fail-closed preference for guards, this silent execute-on-parse fallback is the kind of path that produces unexplained live trades. Flagged for owner decision — it may be intentional.
findings.fix: Confirm intent with the owner. If kept: require the fallback JSON to be the ENTIRE response (no substring extraction), log a monitoring event of a dedicated type (not just logger.info), and gate it behind an explicit per-agent config flag. If not intended: delete _execute_broker_decision_fallback and its call site.

findings.title: useProjectRoot caches a rejected promise forever — one failed /config/root request leaves every path display broken until full page reload
findings.impact: If the first /config/root call fails (backend briefly restarting when the tab loads), all views using useProjectRoot permanently show the relative fallback paths and no retry ever happens, despite the backend being healthy seconds later.
findings.fix: Reset the module cache on failure: `_promise = api.getProjectRoot().then(...).catch(err => { _promise = null; throw err })`.

findings.title: kbDeleteDocument and llmContextSave never check res.ok — failed DELETE/PUT reported as success
findings.impact: A failed LLM-context save (e.g. 400 Invalid filename, disk error) shows the normal saved state in the editor; the user's prompt-context edits are silently lost — the agent keeps running with the old context, a slow-burn behavioral drift. Failed KB deletes likewise appear to succeed until the next reload.
findings.fix: Route both through the existing put()/a shared delete() helper that throws on !res.ok.

findings.title: connect depends on the filter array by identity — the documented inline-array usage would tear down and reconnect the WebSocket on every render
findings.impact: Any caller following the documented pattern gets a self-sustaining reconnect loop: constant socket churn, repeated 1000-event replays, and gaps in the live stream. Currently latent (App.tsx:258 uses no filter; AgentChat's filtered usage is commented out), but it is a trap armed by the hook's own docs.
findings.fix: Depend on a stable key instead: `const filterKey = filter?.join(',') ?? ''` and use filterKey in the useCallback deps (rebuilding the URL from filterKey).

findings.title: useAgents 10s polling has no overlap/ordering guard — a slow older response can overwrite a newer one
findings.impact: Agent list/queue depths shown in the UI can briefly regress to stale values under network jitter; self-corrects on the next poll. Cosmetic-level, but the same unguarded pattern is copy-paste fodder for money-relevant views.
findings.fix: Track a request sequence number (or AbortController per tick) and ignore responses that are not the latest.

findings.title: MonitoringEvent → dict serialization implemented three times in api.py (and skipped entirely on the pinned path)
findings.impact: The divergence already produced the source_module/source shape bug; any future field addition must be made in three places or the streams drift further apart.
findings.fix: Make _serialize_monitoring_event the single serializer; monitoring_events maps over it, _build_ws_message json.dumps() it, and /monitoring/pinned spreads it with auto_pinned.

findings.title: Candle → JSON dict serialization duplicated four times in api.py
findings.impact: Field/precision changes (e.g. rounding policy) must be replicated in 4-5 places; the trigger paths already round to 5 digits while the chart endpoints don't — a latent precision inconsistency between what agents see and what the UI charts.
findings.fix: Extract one `_serialize_candle(c, *, rounded: bool = False)` helper and use it in all five locations.

findings.title: Legacy sync_confirmed flag is serialized and typed in the UI alongside its replacement confirmed_by_broker (dual-field read)
findings.impact: Two flags for one concept; consumers can key off the legacy one and diverge from the authoritative one. Owner explicitly wants compat fields removed.
findings.fix: Remove sync_confirmed from the model, serializer, DB mapping and UI type; keep only confirmed_by_broker.

findings.title: _llm_services registry is populated at build_app but never read anywhere
findings.impact: Dead state plus a dead `llm_services` build_app parameter threading through server startup.
findings.fix: Remove _llm_services, the global declaration at 4442, the assignment at 4462, and the llm_services parameter of build_app (and its caller argument).

findings.title: Unused `context` locals in preview_snapshot and preview_snapshot_tool
findings.impact: Dead locals implying context is used in the preview when it is not.
findings.fix: Delete both assignments.

findings.title: get() lacks the content-type/JSON hardening that getText() has, while the backend SPA catch-all returns 200+HTML for any unknown GET path — missing endpoints surface as cryptic parse errors instead of 404s
findings.impact: Any GET route drift between UI and backend is masked as a JSON SyntaxError with no path/status info — exactly the class of silent producer/consumer mismatch this audit hunts, made harder to detect by the transport layer.
findings.fix: Apply the same content-type check from getText() inside get() (throw `GET {path} returned non-JSON (SPA fallback?)`), or make _serve_spa return 404 for paths containing no file extension under known API prefixes.

findings.title: GET /orderbook reconciles N×limit entries against live broker APIs before truncating the response to limit, and the 'per-broker' limit is silently applied as a total
findings.impact: With multiple brokers the endpoint does broker round-trips and DB updates for rows that are never returned; polling UIs multiply the load and slow the shared event loop. The limit semantics differ between fetch (per broker) and response (total), so callers cannot page reliably.
findings.fix: Truncate/merge before reconciling (reconcile only the entries that will be returned), and pick one limit semantic (total) for both fetch and slice.

findings.title: KbDoc.tags typed as string in the client while the create endpoint requires list[str] — caller works around it with an `as unknown as string` cast
findings.impact: The same field is a JSON-string on read and a string[] on write; the TS type matches neither contract fully, forcing unsafe casts, and any future code passing an actual string to create gets a 422.
findings.fix: Type tags as string[] in the API layer and have the backend deserialize on read (or expose tags consistently as string[] end to end).

findings.title: ws_monitoring docstring promises a 500-event replay but the code replays 1000 into a client ring buffer of 500
findings.impact: Half the replay work (serialization + WS frames, ~1000 messages per tab connect/reconnect) is guaranteed wasted; documentation lies about behavior.
findings.fix: Replay limit=500 to match the client buffer (or make both configurable from one constant).

findings.title: All wizard editors save parsed objects — backend rewrites system.json5/event_routing.json5/agent_tools.json5 with json.dumps, destroying every JSON5 comment
findings.impact: First save from any wizard permanently strips all documentation comments from config/system.json5 and config/RunTime/*.json5. Operational knowledge (why a rule exists, what a threshold means) is silently lost; later misconfiguration becomes more likely.
findings.fix: Have the wizards PUT surgical updates (a dedicated endpoint that patches only the edited section into the JSON5 text with a comment-preserving writer), or at minimum use a JSON5 emitter that round-trips comments server-side.

findings.title: handleSave proceeds as if save succeeded even when persistConfig failed (marks new EC as existing, fires config-reload event)
findings.impact: On a failed save (server down, validation error) the UI switches the new EC into 'existing' mode pointing at an EC that does not exist in config, and sends a reload request for it; the ConfigService reloads the OLD config into a running EC while the user believes the new script is active.
findings.fix: Make persistConfig return a boolean (or rethrow) and gate the isNew-flip and the injectEvent on success.

findings.title: All config editors discard unsaved edits without any dirty-check when switching selection or refreshing
findings.impact: A long prompt or script edit is lost by one stray click on another list entry — the user may believe the edited prompt was saved and is live. Mission-flagged 'unsaved-changes loss' class.
findings.fix: Track a dirty flag per editor (compare form to the normalized source) and window.confirm before selection change / refresh; optionally add a beforeunload handler while dirty.

findings.title: EC form exposes and persists pass_trigger, but the composer backend never reads it
findings.impact: User toggles a control that has zero runtime effect for ECs — misleading configuration; the persisted key is dead weight in system.json5.
findings.fix: Remove pass_trigger from ECForm/formToRaw/rawToForm (and the corresponding UI control), or implement it in EventComposer._apply_config if the semantics are wanted.

findings.title: No-op ternary in rawToForm and never-used ECRow.raw field
findings.impact: Dead expressions confuse maintenance; the unused raw field hides that saves do not round-trip the original config.
findings.fix: Delete the ternary (use backendTriggers directly). Either use ECRow.raw as the serialization base (preferred, fixes the field-drop bug) or remove the field.

findings.title: Non-'script' calculation-block branches are unreachable: type is hardcoded to 'script' and sources/config are always emptied
findings.impact: Dead branches suggest a non-existent feature and add maintenance risk; sources/config fields in the UI type are always empty objects serialized nowhere.
findings.fix: Remove the non-script ternary branches in serializeSnapshotProfile and executeCalcPreview, and drop sources/config from the CalculationBlock UI type (or actually implement typed handlers backend-side first).

findings.title: config_json is persisted as an escaped JSON string while hand-written configs use an object — dual shapes kept alive by a composer compat shim
findings.impact: The same concept exists as two shapes in system.json5; every wizard save converts a readable object into an escaped one-line string. Worse, if the string is malformed, the composer silently substitutes {} — an EC whose thresholds live in config trades with defaults and no error.
findings.fix: Parse config_json in formToRaw and persist it as an object; then remove the string branch (and at least log loudly instead of silently substituting {} in composer._apply_config).

findings.title: Snapshot tool-block arguments are persisted as raw strings, unlike agent forced_arguments which are schema-coerced
findings.impact: system.json5 contains the same argument concept as number in one section and string in another; any future strictly-typed tool or schema validation will break only for wizard-saved profiles.
findings.fix: Use the already-validated coerceToolArgValue(rawValue, prop) result in serializeSnapshotProfile instead of the raw string.

findings.title: A literal 'timer' entry inside event_triggers loaded from config cannot be removed via the UI
findings.impact: For hand-edited configs containing 'timer' in event_triggers, the wizard shows an unremovable timer chip and the agent config keeps a bogus bus-event trigger named 'timer'.
findings.fix: In removeTrigger's timer branch also filter: `event_triggers: prev.event_triggers.filter(t => t !== TIMER_TRIGGER)`; likewise strip TIMER_TRIGGER from event_triggers in normalizeAgent (mapping it to timer_enabled).

findings.title: Chartshot save persists the fully normalized tree: unknown fields of every named config are dropped and synthetic uid() ids are injected
findings.impact: Any extra keys a user added to a chartshot config are silently removed on save, and volatile timestamp-based ids get committed into system.json5, producing noisy diffs on every save.
findings.fix: Serialize only known fields WITHOUT the transient id (strip it in save()), and merge unedited named configs from the freshly fetched sys.chartshot instead of the normalized state.

findings.title: Debounced Python-syntax validation has no in-flight cancellation — an older slow response can overwrite newer markers
findings.impact: After fast consecutive edits, error squiggles for an already-fixed (or not-yet-existing) syntax error can be displayed, confusing the user editing trading helper code. Cosmetic only — save-side validation is separate.
findings.fix: Capture a request sequence number (or the text snapshot) and ignore responses that do not match the current text before calling setModelMarkers.

findings.title: eventFlow.ts (280 lines) is entirely unused — nothing imports getEventFlow/eventVisibleInTab/eventArrowInTab
findings.impact: 300 lines of stale event-classification rules that silently drift from the real event catalogue; the App.tsx comment actively misleads maintainers into 'fixing' routing display in a file that is never executed.
findings.fix: Delete ui/src/components/views/monitor/eventFlow.ts and the stale comment in App.tsx:44-45.

findings.title: Removed 'module tab' monitor menu and hidden 'test' section leave dead entries in SubMenu, TopMenu types, App routing and HANDBOOK_FILE
findings.impact: Three files carry a phantom 'test' section and a phantom module-tab monitor; new maintainers add entries to lists that are never displayed.
findings.fix: Remove SUB_ITEMS.monitor / SUB_ITEMS.test, the 'test' member of TopSection, DEFAULT_SUB.test, App case 'test', and the monitor:* HANDBOOK_FILE rows (keep a single 'monitor' fallback).

findings.title: EMA/RSI/ATR indicator state, debounced fetch effects and toolbar JSX duplicated between AgentChat and Orderbook
findings.impact: Indicator-request logic (history sizing `Math.min(500, candles.length + period)`, error handling that silently clears values) must be fixed twice; the silent `.catch(() => set...([]))` already hides backend indicator errors in both.
findings.fix: Extract a useChartIndicators(requestContext) hook returning { overlayLines, oscillators, controls }.

findings.title: PromptLibraryModal and SnippetLibraryModal duplicate the whole library CRUD layer (newId, parseVer, nextVersion, sortedEntries, save/delete/duplicate handlers)
findings.impact: Six copies of id-generation and two copies of read-modify-write library persistence; a fix to the save race (whole-library overwrite) or id collisions has to be replicated blindly.
findings.fix: Extract a shared makeId() util and a generic useLibraryCrud(scope, key) hook consumed by both modals.

findings.title: Markdown/inline-code renderer implemented three times (AiAssistantModal.renderContent, LLMChatPanel.renderAssistantContent, assistantShared.renderInlineText)
findings.impact: Rendering fixes (e.g. escaping, nested fences) must be applied in three places; the 'replaced' panel lives on as a divergent twin.
findings.fix: Move one renderer into assistantShared.tsx and consume it from all three; evaluate migrating ProfileConfigEditors to ScriptAssistantPanel and deleting LLMChatPanel.

findings.title: Concurrent recomputeIndicators promises resolve out of order and setIndicators overwrites newer state with stale arrays
findings.impact: User changes RSI period from 14 to 7; a second later the panel and chart silently snap back to 14 — the operator analyzes the chart believing they are looking at period 7. Random-seeming, timing-dependent.
findings.fix: Track a monotonically increasing recompute token (ref); ignore resolutions whose token is stale, or recompute via functional setIndicators merging per-indicator results instead of replacing the whole array.

findings.title: Measure tool candle count includes the 200 synthetic whitespace future bars and returns -1 for empty ranges
findings.impact: Measuring from a past candle into the future (a very common use: projecting time-to-target) reports phantom candles — whitespace slots counted as real bars — so the displayed 'Nc' bar count is inflated by up to 200. A measurement over a data-free span displays '-1c'.
findings.fix: Filter out whitespace before counting: `data.filter(d => d.time >= tMin && d.time <= tMax && 'close' in d).length` and clamp with Math.max(0, count - 1).

findings.title: Empty-orderbook placeholder row uses colSpan={8} in a 10-column table
findings.impact: Cosmetic misalignment of the 'No orders in the orderbook.' cell; indicates the colSpan was not updated when columns were added.
findings.fix: Change to colSpan={10} (or compute from a shared column definition).

findings.title: Detail window and formatPayload globally strip \" and \n escapes from JSON — displayed payloads become invalid/corrupted for values that legitimately contain them
findings.impact: During incident analysis the operator copies a payload from the detail window into a JSON tool and it fails to parse or, worse, parses with wrong values — undermining audit of the exact money-path events this window exists for.
findings.fix: Show the raw JSON.stringify output; if readability of embedded JSON strings is desired, detect and pretty-print those specific string fields instead of regex-replacing escapes globally.

findings.title: 80-entry EVENT_INFO catalogue object is declared inside EventDetailWindow and rebuilt on every render (including every drag mousemove)
findings.impact: Unnecessary allocation churn making window dragging janky; the catalogue also duplicates event-description knowledge that belongs at module scope.
findings.fix: Hoist EVENT_INFO to module scope (const outside the component).

findings.title: Conditional early return before hooks in App() violates the Rules of Hooks
findings.impact: Works only because the URL never changes without a reload; any future code path that flips the condition at runtime crashes with 'Rendered fewer hooks than expected'. It also breaks react-hooks lint, masking real hook-order bugs elsewhere.
findings.fix: Do the ?handbook=1 branch in main.tsx next to the existing ?knowledgebase=1 branch, keeping App() hook-order-stable.

findings.title: Trace fetch has no cancellation — switching events quickly can display the previous event's trace under the new header
findings.impact: Clicking through orders/events during an incident can attach the wrong causal chain to the order being inspected — a subtle audit error.
findings.fix: Add the standard `let cancelled = false` cleanup (as already done in Orderbook.loadDetail) or an AbortController keyed on eventId.

findings.title: KbDoc.tags typed as string in the UI while backend expects list[str] — call site papers over it with `as unknown as string`
findings.impact: Type system actively lies about the wire shape; any other caller that passes a comma-string per the UI type would be rejected or mis-stored by the backend.
findings.fix: Change KbDoc.tags to string[] in ui/src/api/client.ts and drop the cast.

findings.title: computeFutureBars called inline in JSX constructs 8 Intl.DateTimeFormat instances on every render
findings.impact: Milliseconds of wasted main-thread time on every ChartAnalysis render (which happens per hover/selection), contributing to chart UI jank.
findings.fix: useMemo(() => computeFutureBars(timeframe), [timeframe]) and cache the DateTimeFormat instances at module scope (as computeSessionBands already does per call).

findings.title: TIMEFRAMES filter for 'M1' is a no-op and pip-size heuristic is copy-pasted four times
findings.impact: Dead filter misleads about M1 support; four copies of the JPY-pip heuristic will diverge when metals/indices (price > 20 but not 0.01-pip) are added — producing wrong pip readouts in some panels but not others.
findings.fix: Drop the filter; extract a shared pipSize(price) util used by all four call sites.

findings.title: Vite scaffolding leftovers: App.css and assets/react.svg are referenced nowhere
findings.impact: Dead files shipped in the repo; the #root rule would even break the app layout if ever accidentally imported.
findings.fix: Delete ui/src/App.css and ui/src/assets/react.svg.

findings.title: Quick-preset button row duplicated verbatim for the validation-issues and smoke-check-OK branches
findings.impact: Preset changes (e.g. new TRAILING_STOP preset) must be made twice; one branch will inevitably be missed.
findings.fix: Extract the button row into a local <PresetButtons /> element rendered in both branches.

findings.title: Commented-out monitoring-stream subscription and auto-refresh remnants left in AgentChat
findings.impact: Dead comments plus an unused, untested hook option surface (server-side WS filter) that will silently rot; the filter values are also not URL-encoded if ever revived.
findings.fix: Delete the commented code; either remove the filter/enabled options from useMonitoringStream or keep them with a test and encodeURIComponent on filter values.

findings.title: Same candle serialized with different value types on two bus events: M5_CANDLE_UPDATE carries OHLC/spread as JSON strings, M5_CANDLE_TRIGGER converts them to rounded floats
findings.impact: Any consumer handling both events (DataContainer persists UPDATE; agents/snapshot builders consume TRIGGER) must branch on type; code written against one event silently mis-handles the other (e.g. Decimal(str(x)) of a float repr, string comparison of prices). Exactly the producer/consumer shape-mismatch class under suspicion.
findings.fix: Emit the same serialization on both events (keep mode="json" strings); if the LLM prompt needs rounded numbers, round at the consumer/prompt-building layer, not in the bus payload.

findings.title: trigger_sync keeps a dead `repository=None  # kept for compat` parameter that exists only for the stale test-era call signature
findings.impact: The shim masks the wrong-argument-order bug in the tests (mock_repository binds to event_bus) instead of failing loudly, and violates the owner's no-compat-shims policy.
findings.fix: Delete the repository parameter; fix callers (only the stale tests) to the (pair, event_bus) signature.

findings.title: Entire integration and e2e suites deleted without replacement — only __init__.py remains, with stale __pycache__ .pyc files for the removed tests (test_full_cycle, test_trading_agent, test_supervisor_agent, test_optimization_agent, test_technical_analysis_agent, legacy_agents, test_risk_engine, test_pattern_detector, test_analysis_tools)
findings.impact: No end-to-end verification exists for the full candle→analysis→order cycle, and the deleted risk-engine test coverage was never replaced. Stale .pyc files can also be silently imported by tooling and mislead coverage/audit tools.
findings.fix: Delete all __pycache__ directories from tests/ (add to .gitignore if not already), and either restore bus-architecture integration/e2e tests or remove the empty package dirs.

findings.title: MockLLMProvider + mock_llm fixture and make_snapshot/make_tick helpers are unused by any test; MockLLMProvider's signatures also drifted from the AbstractLLMProvider port (missing images/reasoning_effort params)
findings.impact: Dead weight that will produce confusing failures the first time someone wires it into a new agent test; the signature drift means the mock no longer documents the real LLM contract.
findings.fix: Either delete MockLLMProvider/mock_llm/make_snapshot/make_tick (and the now-unused OrderStatus import at conftest.py:13), or update MockLLMProvider to the current port signature and use it in a real agent-cycle test.

findings.title: MockBroker.close_position signature omits the `pair` parameter that AbstractBroker declares — Liskov violation that TypeErrors if any code path passes pair
findings.impact: Any rewritten test driving the real close path (adapter passes pair for close-by-pair, see openforexai/tools/trading/close_position.py) will crash inside the mock instead of testing behavior.
findings.fix: Add `pair: str | None = None` to MockBroker.close_position to match the port.

findings.title: test_rejected_order asserts `entry.closed_at is not None` but the current production rejection path never sets closed_at on the order-book entry
findings.impact: Once the test harness is repaired this assertion will fail; more importantly, rejected entries persist with closed_at=NULL, so any duration/latency analytics or UI sorting on closed_at silently misclassifies rejected orders.
findings.fix: Add `"closed_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()` to rejected_updates in order_execution.py (matching the test's documented intent), or update the test if NULL closed_at for rejections is the intended contract.

findings.title: Over-mocking: bus_request is fully replaced and the fake positions carry Decimal/datetime objects, whereas the real POSITIONS_RESPONSE payload contains JSON strings — the test passes even if adapter response handling or pair filtering is broken
findings.impact: The grouping logic is tested against payload shapes that can never occur in production; a change to the adapter payload key or filter semantics would not fail any test.
findings.fix: Feed the mock with model_dump(mode="json") output of real Position objects, and add one integration-style test running the tool against a stub adapter registered on a real EventBus.

findings.title: test_two_pairs_correlation_range only asserts -1.0 <= corr <= 1.0 for two perfectly linearly increasing series — passes for any implementation, including a completely broken one
findings.impact: compute_correlation_matrix feeds correlation-based exposure decisions; the math could be inverted (sign flip → correlated pairs treated as hedges) without any test failing.
findings.fix: Assert `corr == pytest.approx(1.0)` for the identical-trend case and add an anti-correlated series asserting approx(-1.0).

findings.title: Test pins the exact content of the live, hot-reloadable operator config file config/RunTime/agent_tools.json5 — it breaks on every legitimate config edit and tests data, not code
findings.impact: Per CLAUDE.md this file is runtime-editable via the management API; any operator change turns CI red for non-code reasons, training the team to ignore failures (which is plausibly how the current 35 broken tests accumulated).
findings.fix: Load a fixture json5 from tests/fixtures/ (or tmp_path) asserting parser behavior (bridge-tool filtering, comment stripping), not live config content.

findings.title: _schedule_agent_trigger creates a fire-and-forget task whose non-cancellation exceptions are never observed — a failed _publish_m5_candle_trigger silently drops the agent trigger for that candle
findings.impact: One transient publish failure means analysis agents are never triggered for that M5 candle — a missed decision cycle with no monitoring event, matching the 'random-seeming, weeks-later' loss pattern.
findings.fix: Attach `task.add_done_callback` that logs task.exception() and emits a BROKER_ERROR/monitoring event, or wrap the coroutine body in try/except-log.

findings.title: coverage gap: M5→higher-timeframe resampling (data/resampler.py) has zero tests
findings.impact: An off-by-one bucket boundary or inclusion of the forming bucket shifts every higher-TF indicator (EMA/RSI/ATR) slightly — invisible in any single trade, systematic across weeks.
findings.fix: Add unit tests: exact bucket boundaries (e.g. H1 bucket = 12 M5 candles starting at :00), exclusion of incomplete buckets, gap handling, and OHLC aggregation correctness against hand-computed fixtures.

findings.title: coverage gap: OANDA adapter has zero tests; MT5 adapter is tested only for the _call_blocking timeout helper
findings.impact: A broker-API field mapping error (e.g. wrong sign convention, price parsed as float, pips vs price for trailing distance) executes real orders wrongly and only shows up as unexplained live P&L drift.
findings.fix: Add adapter unit tests with recorded/stubbed broker API responses asserting the exact TradeOrder→API request mapping and API response→TradeResult/Position parsing, including Decimal precision and timezone handling.

findings.title: coverage gap: EventBus dispatch, routing-table matching, request/response futures (register_response_future/cancel) and reload_routing have zero tests
findings.impact: Per CLAUDE.md all inter-module communication (including every order) flows through the bus; an unmatched routing rule or a never-resolved response future silently drops or hangs order placement.
findings.fix: Add unit tests for publish→dispatch→registered member delivery, target_agent_id routing, response-future resolution/timeout/cancellation, and reload_routing hot-swap.

findings.title: Repository never closed (finally only disconnects brokers) while the sibling temp script does close it
findings.impact: For the PostgreSQL backend the connection pool is abandoned at interpreter exit (asyncpg emits warnings, connections linger until server timeout); for SQLite the WAL file may not be checkpointed cleanly. Cosmetic for SQLite, real for Postgres.
findings.fix: Add `try: await repository.close() except Exception: pass` to the finally block, matching the temp script.

findings.title: Backfill update-building logic (broker_result -> order_book updates incl. close_reason->close_reasoning mapping) exists in four places
findings.impact: Four twin implementations of the money-path field mapping; a schema or convention change (e.g. adding commission to pnl) applied to one path silently diverges the others — stored results then depend on WHICH code path wrote them.
findings.fix: Extract one shared helper (e.g. openforexai/models or a reconcile module) that converts a broker close-result dict into order-book updates, and use it from api.py, base.py and both scripts.

findings.title: _ensure_sample silently migrates legacy '{adapter}-sample.json5' filenames to the canonical '.sample.json5' form
findings.impact: Backward-compat fallback the owner wants removed; it also leaves the legacy file in place, so both copies exist and can drift.
findings.fix: Delete the legacy_dash branch; rename any remaining *-sample.json5 files in the repo once and remove the shim.

findings.title: Setup wizard placeholder regex diverges from the runtime loader's substitution regex
findings.impact: A sample config accepted and populated by the wizard (whitespace form) is NOT substituted at runtime — the literal `${ VAR }` string ends up as an API key/account id, failing only when the module is first used.
findings.fix: Import and reuse a single placeholder regex from json_loader in initial_setup.py.

findings.title: db_path and --config resolved against CWD; aiosqlite.connect creates an empty DB file at the wrong path before failing
findings.impact: Confusing failure plus stray empty database files when run from a different working directory.
findings.fix: Resolve config path and relative sqlite_path against Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent as the backfill scripts do.

findings.title: run_backtest.py is an unimplemented stub — parses args, loads config, prints 'not yet implemented'
findings.impact: Dead scaffolding advertised in the usage docstring; an operator 'validating' a prompt via this script gets no validation and might believe a backtest ran.
findings.fix: Either implement the replay or delete the script (and any docs referencing it) until it exists; at minimum exit non-zero.

findings.title: $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' does not stop on native-command failures — pip/npm failures are ignored and setup continues into the wizard
findings.impact: A failed dependency install or UI build is silently skipped; the wizard then runs against a broken venv and the operator only discovers it at first start.
findings.fix: After each native call add `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "... failed" }` (or a small Invoke-Checked helper).

findings.title: Requires a bare `python` binary, which most modern Linux distros do not ship
findings.impact: Setup aborts immediately on a stock Ubuntu/Debian host even though python3 is available. Fail-fast, so no corruption — just broken onboarding.
findings.fix: Detect python3 first: PY=$(command -v python3 || command -v python) and use "$PY" -m venv .venv.

findings.title: --bus filter matches event_type 'event_bus_message', which the backend never emits — the bus publishes monitoring events under the actual bus event value; the flag shows nothing, and the 'payload_keys' display field is never produced
findings.impact: python tools/monitor.py --bus prints nothing, ever — the operator concludes no inter-agent traffic exists while agents are trading; docs/tools.en.md documents the broken flag.
findings.fix: Either have EventBus._emit_monitoring emit event_type='event_bus_message' (with the concrete event in payload) or make --bus filter on source == 'eventbus'; align _TYPE_FIELDS with the real payload keys (payload, message_id) and remove the dead EVENT_BUS_MESSAGE enum member.

findings.title: _ERROR_TYPES and _TYPE_COLOUR have drifted from MonitoringEventType — --errors misses llm_turn_failed, llm_http_attempt_failed, ec_run_failed, routing_reload_failed, agent_decision_snapshot_invalid, unmatched_event; colour map contains dead 'timeframe_calculated'
findings.impact: Running the monitor with --errors during live trading hides EventComposer run failures, LLM turn failures and dropped/unroutable events — precisely the silent failures that later look like random losses (e.g. an EC guard script failing on every run would be invisible).
findings.fix: Derive the error set from MonitoringEventType (e.g. every member ending in _FAILED/_ERROR plus alarms) or keep one shared constant in the package that both the monitor and UI import; drop 'timeframe_calculated'.

findings.title: Rotation filenames are minute-granular — two rotations within the same minute collide: on POSIX Path.rename silently OVERWRITES the previously closed log (audit data loss); on Windows the rename fails and the byte counter resets while appending to the same oversized file
findings.impact: During high-volume periods (exactly when audit data matters) rotated audit log files can be silently overwritten/lost, or a single file grows past the configured limit.
findings.fix: Include seconds (and a collision counter) in _TS_FMT, or check closed.exists() and append a suffix; initialize _bytes_written from self._current_path.stat().st_size.

findings.title: Placeholder-syntax check downgrades a FAIL config-sanity status to WARN, bypassing the early return and running the adapter against a config already known to be broken
findings.impact: The diagnostics tool reports WARN (exit 2) for configs that are definitively broken, misleading scripted health checks that only treat exit 1 as failure.
findings.fix: Only downgrade PASS→WARN (or better, treat unresolved placeholders as FAIL): `if key and "${" in key and sanity.status == "PASS": sanity.status = "FAIL"` with the explanatory detail.

findings.title: _force_stdlib_logging_module is duplicated byte-for-byte in test_broker.py and test_llm.py, and is redundant/hazardous: the sys.path fix at the top of both files already prevents shadowing, and re-executing stdlib logging creates a second logging module instance with a separate root logger
findings.impact: Split logger state can hide log output during broker diagnostics; two copies of a subtle interpreter hack will drift. The clean fix (renaming tools/logging.py to e.g. event_logger.py) removes the need for both copies entirely.
